News.title: Disturbing house of horrors floor plans reveal chilling ‘hidden’ space and just one bathroom where 16 ‘feral’ kids found
News.content:
DISTURBING floor plans of the Ohio house of horrors where 16 children were found have revealed a chilling hidden space – and just one bathroom for the family of 20.

Newly uncovered county property records paint a grim picture of the cramped home where prosecutors claim the children endured years of neglect before four relatives were arrested.



According to property records from the Vinton County Auditor’s Office reviewed by Los Angeles Magazine, the century-old Hamden home at 182 Ohmer Street measures just 1,336 square feet and has only a single full bathroom despite allegedly housing 20 people.

The official floor plans also show a 518-square-foot basement beneath part of the property, although investigators have previously said reports that all 16 children lived downstairs are false.



Authorities have alleged the youngsters were instead kept confined upstairs, while neighbors and investigators said the smell of human waste, garbage and animal feces rose from the basement and spread through the house.

The sketch also reveals two first-floor additions, a front porch and a rear wooden deck, with the modest property made up of just five rooms in total, according to county records.



The home was built in 1900 and is listed as a single-family residence, the records show.

It is currently appraised at $68,670, with the building itself valued at just over $42,000.

Annual property taxes are listed at less than $1,000.

The shocking details come after Vinton County investigators entered the property on June 30 while responding to what authorities have said was an unrelated investigation.



According to prosecutors, officers discovered 16 children, aged between 18 months and 18 years, allegedly living in deplorable conditions.

Gary Siders Jr., Elizabeth Siders, Gary Siders Sr. and Christina “Lynn” Siders have each been charged with 16 felony counts of child endangering.

Prosecutors allege the children suffered prolonged neglect and abuse.



The case has since been sent to a grand jury and remains under investigation.

Law enforcement has previously described the conditions inside the home in graphic detail, while alleging the children were confined to a single room. A gag order has since been imposed on several defendants.

It comes as the children’s grandmother, Christina Siders, has filed her own request for a gag order after being charged alongside her husband, son and daughter-in-law over the alleged abuse.



According to WOWK, Christina’s attorney has asked the court to bar further public comments about her role in the case – mirroring a request already granted to her son, Gary Siders Jr.

It is not yet known whether the judge will approve the latest motion.

All four defendants have pleaded not guilty.

Gary Siders Sr. was released on a recognizance bond after suffering a medical emergency, with Vinton County Prosecutor William Archer saying his treatment “could potentially bankrupt Vinton County” if he remained in custody.

Elizabeth Siders has also asked to be released, with her attorney saying her “principal desire” is to be reunited with her children.



The latest court fight comes after records revealed the family had already come to the attention of authorities five years before the children were rescued.

Court documents obtained by NewsNation affiliate WCMH show Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders were hit with a truancy complaint in October 2021 after six of their oldest children allegedly failed to attend a single day of school during the 2021-22 school year at Addaville Elementary School.

The case was dismissed in January 2022 after officials were unable to locate the parents, with records stating their whereabouts were unknown.

Authorities have since said the children had no school records, no medical records and no previous Child Protective Services involvement before the June 30 rescue.



Officers stumbled upon the children while executing a search warrant linked to unrelated allegations involving Gary Siders Jr., investigators said.

Authorities alleged the youngsters – aged between 18 months and 18 years old – were living in filthy conditions, with many confined to a 12ft-by-12ft area for years.

Seven children were taken to hospitals in Columbus, including two who were airlifted by helicopter, while one child was initially listed in critical condition.

Investigators also said some of the children were unable to speak, and alleged the oldest, an 18-year-old, could not write her own name.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson described what investigators found as “pure evil”, saying: “This is very, it was terrible. I mean, it looked like almost feral animals. It was terrible.”

He also alleged the children had spent most of the last four years confined to an area no larger than 12ft by 12ft, adding: “Most of our livestock was kept in better conditions than the children. It was just a disgusting scene.”

News.title: Dexter fan murdered cellmate while awaiting trial for ‘chopping up his 2 roommates & scattering them by cabin in woods’
News.content:
A DEXTER fanatic murdered his cellmate while awaiting trial for chopping up his two roommates and scattering their remains, a court heard.

James Desborough, 39, strangled 65-year-old cellmate Steven Kempster to death at HMP Exeter in September last year.



Winchester Crown Court heard he was being held on remand at the time accused of killing Daniel Coleman, 43, and Claudio Aquilino, 57.

Desborough pleaded guilty to manslaughter but was convicted of murdering Kempster by a jury.



He is now on trial charged with two counts of murder following Daniel and Claudio’s deaths.

Jurors heard Desborough met the two men at a homeless residence in Newquay, Cornwall.



After he allegedly murdered the pair, he dismembered their bodies in Paramoor Woods, near Sticker in Cornwall, tried to burn and bury their remains then stole their money.

Ahmed Hossain KC, prosecuting, said that parts of Daniel’s dismembered body, including his torso, legs and feet, were found in a shallow grave.

Daniel’s DNA was discovered on an axe that was hanging from a tree nearby, Winchester Crown Court heard.

Claudio’s shallow grave was found 18 metres away.



Cops discovered 1,900 burnt bone fragments – belonging to Claudio – at a stream nearby, jurors were told.

A “piece of flesh” – also from the alleged victim – was in the water, and a search party also found “two pieces of unburnt scapula”, it was said.

Mr Hossain KC said Desborough was a fan of the hit TV show Dexter – in which the lead character is a serial killer who dismembers people.



The alleged killer told a forensic biologist involved in the woodland searches that he “particularly enjoyed the dismemberment scenes” in the show, the prosecutor said.

Police later seized a large number of handwritten notes in the woodland cabin.

One said: “I know I’m a killer, ready to kill and execute any predators.”



Another included “detailed travel plans and intent to leave the UK”.

This note mentioned a “shuffle bag liner”, “bodies buried”, “new disguise”, “new burner phone” and “safe house”, jurors heard.

Desborough denies murdering Claudio between April 17 and July 7 last year and killing Daniel between June 2 and July 7 last year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He has pleaded guilty to preventing the lawful burial of the two men’s bodies.

The trial continues.

News.title: Grandad, 75, found dead at block of flats is pictured as family pay tribute after woman, 49, charged with murder
News.content:
'HEART OF GOLD' Grandad, 75, found dead at block of flats is pictured as family pay tribute after woman, 49, charged with murder

A GRANDAD who was found dead at a block of flats has been pictured for the first time after a woman was charged with murder

The body of Trevor Hilton, 75, was found at Hargreaves House in Bolton on Friday morning and a murder investigation was soon launched.

Samantha Nuttall, 39, from Bolton, was charged and appeared at Salford Magistrates Court today.

Trevor’s family said in a touching tribute: “Trevor was a dear father, grandfather and brother to his siblings whose life was taken far too soon.





“Trevor was such a joker and we will miss the good times and will cherish the memories that we have.

“Trevor had a heart of gold and would help anyone in need, he will always be in our thoughts.

“The loss of Trevor has left a hole in our family which cannot be filled and we are heartbroken and would like to request privacy whilst we are trying to come to terms with what has happened.”

A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said: “Trevor Hilton, 75, was pronounced dead on Friday morning after officers responded to an incident at an address on Ormrod Street.



“His death is now subject to a murder investigation, with a woman now charged and in custody.”

Det Insp Louise Kelly has appealed for information and previously said: “I would like to express my deepest condolences to the victim’s family and loved ones as they navigate through this loss.

“They will continue to be supported by our specialist officers during this difficult time.”

News.title: Protests erupt as migrant dies after being pepper sprayed & hogtied by Italian cops in case likened to George Floyd
News.content:
PROTESTS have erupted after a migrant who was pepper sprayed and hogtied by Italian cops died.

Abderrahim Fakir, 42, died while handcuffed in Bologna on Sunday after police scrambled to reports of the Moroccan man behaving erratically.



His death has drawn comparisons to the death of George Floyd who died after a police officer knelt on his neck during an arrest in Minneapolis in May 2020.

Footage showed two police officers pinning Fakir, who ran a small cleaning business in the city, face-down to the ground as he screamed for help.



A third person, believed to be a resident of the Pilastro neighbourhood, was seen holding his feet down as the officers restrained him.

The video also shows two paramedics standing around them and three other people spectating as the struggle unfolded.



Fakir could be heard desperately crying out for the officers to stop restraining him as he pleaded: “Help, enough, enough.”

Local media reported police used pepper spray on the 42-year-old during the confrontation.

Fakir was heard begging for water as the encounter went on for several minutes.

His movements eventually stopped as he appeared to lose consciousness before officers and a local resident were seen tying his feet together.



Police had been called after residents reported a man shouting and acting agitated in the area.

Authorities said Fakir allegedly struck a police vehicle before officers arrived and attempted to contain him.

According to local police, officers were called by residents who had “reported an angry person… other residents assisted them in containing the individual after a car was damaged.”



They added: “After containment operations, which were carried out in the presence of paramedics, the man died.”

Police said bodycam footage from the incident would be made available to judicial authorities.

It remains unclear how Fakir died, with reports suggesting he may have suffered a severe asthma attack or cardiac arrest.

Prosecutors have ordered an autopsy to establish the cause of death.

As the investigation continues, Fakir’s family have spoken of their heartbreak and demanded answers over his final moments.



His sister Khadija told local media: “I demand justice. I want revenge. I will never find peace until my brother gets justice.

“We don’t know what happened; we only received a phone call saying he was dead. They handcuffed him, and he died. They attacked him… and they beat him. There are witnesses.”

Fakir, who lived with his brother, had a history of minor criminal offences and suffered from underlying health conditions, according to his family.

Speaking about the officers involved, his sister said: “If someone is agitated, you have to calm them down.”



The shocking footage sparked protests across Bologna, with hundreds taking to the streets demanding answers over Fakir’s death.

Demonstrators reportedly chanted anti-police slogans and knelt with raised fists, a gesture associated with the Black Lives Matter movement after George Floyd’s death.

A further protest was planned in central Bologna, backed by centre-left Mayor Matteo Lepore, the Cgil trade union and other left-wing groups.

The League party, part of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government, called for a full investigation but defended the officers, saying they were “doing their duty” after being called by “exasperated citizens”.



Fakir’s death is now being investigated by Bologna prosecutors, who have opened a manslaughter investigation into those involved in the “various phases” of the police operation.

The case includes two police officers and four ambulance workers, although prosecutors said there are currently no suspects.

Investigators said the probe would examine the full sequence of events, including the moments before and after the footage circulating online.

Fakir’s lawyer Barbara Spinelli described him as a “kind, polite, and respectful person” who cared deeply about his business and employees.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “He was an extremely kind, polite, and respectful person. A worker who cared about his company and his employees. He’s the last client I’d imagine would suffer such an end.”



Spinelli said Fakir had been living legally in Italy since childhood and was renewing his residence permit.

News.title: Gutwrenching moment bride-to-be knocks engagement ring out of her partner’s hand and into a LAKE as he proposes to her
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a bride inadvertently knocks an engagement ring out of her groom’s hand as he proposed on a paddle board.

Astonishing footage shows the couple paddling in Lake Barkhatovo, Russia, where the groom had planned to propose.



The sweet moment goes wrong very quickly when the bride, Alina Nikolaeva, turns around, accidentally knocking the engagement ring into the water.

The shocked groom immediately plunged into the lake but failed to find the ring.



In aftermath of the incident, the crestfallen couple called in local diver Vasiliy Cheban.

The expert diver was able to swiftly located the engagement ring in the murky water.

Footage shows Cheban rummaging around on the muddy lake floor before returning triumphantly to the surface.

“I arrived an hour later, found the ring and the happiness continued,” Cheban said.



The same footage shows the couple celebrating as Cheban holds the ring aloft.

The happy couple redid the proposal on dry land, as the groom got down on one knee and proposed to his bride.

This time, the proposal went to plan as the bride was captured saying yes.

Located 2,140 miles east of Moscow, Lake Barkhatovo is known for its stunning views and popular ‘Velvet Beach’, making it the perfect destination for the proposal.

Vasiliy Cheban is an experienced diver who travels throughout Russia, helping people to find lost items in lakes and other bodies of water.



Cheban shares his videos to his 12,000 followers on Instagram, with his bio reading ‘solving underwater problems is my speciality and I tailor my approach to each problem individually.’

Other items Cheban has retrieved from the water include a speargun, a watch, and several phones lost during water sports.

This comes after an American man found his wife’s engagement ring while on vacation in Italy – nine years after she lost it.



Margaret and Justin Mussel from New Jersey first visited Pompeii in Italy in 2006 on their honeymoon.

On their way back from the ancient site, her diamond ring slipped off her finger, but she didn’t realise until they got back to the hotel.

They turned their hotel room upside down but couldn’t find it anywhere.

When the couple went back to the country nine years later they were in luck, because Justin found the ring stuck in the pavement.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to Margaret, it looks almost as good as it did when Justin proposed.



She said: “If you saw it, you wouldn’t think it [had been] in a crack for nine years.”

News.title: Andy Burnham vows ‘this is a circuit breaker’ in first speech as PM – but we have to wait until later this YEAR for plan
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has promised to deliver a “circuit breaker for Britain” – but said the blueprint for his 10-year vision will not be unveiled until later this year.

The new Prime Minister pledged immediate help with the cost of living, saying families would get “some breathing space” from tomorrow when he unveils his first measures and explains “how we pay for them.”



But the country will have to wait months for the detail behind his 10-year Plan for Britain, which he says will deliver the biggest political and economic shake-up in more than 40 years.

The blueprint will set out “a path from where we are now to where I believe we all want Britain to be”, with plans to hand power out of Westminster, build more council homes and put “life’s essentials” under stronger public control.



Mr Burnham also revealed his first instruction after walking through the famous black door would be to end rough sleeping.

In his first speech outside No10, Mr Burnham admitted the public were “fed up with politics“, conceding: “We have not been good enough, and we need to be better. We will be.”

The Labour leader promised “a circuit breaker for Britain”, declaring his Government would bring forward “the biggest changes in the last 40 years” through “a new political model and a new economic model.”

Standing outside the famous black door after returning from Buckingham Palace, Mr Burnham ditched the traditional Downing Street lectern and instead addressed the nation from behind two microphones.

Moments earlier, he had arrived with wife Marie-France van Heel, embracing supporters and shaking hands with well-wishers gathered outside No10.

Mr Burnham blamed Britain’s problems on the “wrong turns” of the 1980s, arguing former industrial communities had never recovered after deindustrialisation.



He vowed to “take power out of here and carry it into every postcode in the land” and said public procurement would be used to back British industry.

The PM also promised education reforms, better mental health support for young people and more council homes.

He said: “We will help more young people into work by changing the education system and giving them more support, more mental health support, and we will build more council homes.

“That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules, and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.



“We will help people to live well, building a more preventative state, investing in people’s success rather than paying for failure, and that work starts now.

He added: “I will put the care of people at the heart of everything I do.

“I will give this my all, and I ask you all to pull with me. Let’s build a new national sense of unity, of common purpose, and positivity.

“Let us make this the moment when Britain starts to believe again, the moment we bring back hope.

“Thank you very much, everybody.”

News.title: It’ll take more than warm words & Andy Burnham’s ‘vibes’ to fix UK… clock is already ticking for the man with no plan
News.content:
ANDY Burnham isn’t wasting any time showing the British people he is on their side as they battle the cost-of-living.

The new Prime Minister was quick out of the blocks outside Downing Street to offer the public some “breathing space” as they grapple with rising bills.



He has been accused of being all about ‘vibes’ but there may be finally be a bit of meat on the bones when it comes to policy.

Speculation has been rife that there may be help coming on bus fares, energy bills and also a change in tax rules to give people a bit more cash in their pockets.



The move is in sheer contrast to when Sir Keir Starmer came to office just over two years ago.

Within weeks, the former PM told millions of pensioners that they were going to lose out on their winter fuel payments.

Mr Burnham used his showcase moment – minutes after leaving Buckingham Palace to meet the King – to show that he is on their side, saying he will give the people “his all”.

Voters will only have to wait 24 hours until he offers some help and explains how it will be paid for.



Before he walked through the famous black door he said he would end rough sleeping.

It was the first time for many years that an incoming Prime Minister delivered his speech without notes in front of dozens of supporters.

Close aides and the Labour faithful created a party atmosphere in the country’s most famous streets.

But convincing the public out in the country and driving up their living standards will take more than just warm words.

The PM will offer a “circuit breaker” to what has come before with more power devolved to the regions.



He vowed to win over voters who are “fed up with politics”. He said his generation of politicians need to “raise our game and rise to the new challenge”.

But anyone thinking that a big, bold radical plan for the country will be enacted today must think again.

A ten-year plan for the country won’t come until later this year. Time will only tell how much of that decade Mr Burnham will preside over.

The true test will be whether Brits feel better off in their pockets and time is short. The clock is already ticking.

News.title: 'I never thought a simple spider bite could leave me fighting sepsis'
News.content:
'I never thought a simple spider bite could leave me fighting sepsis'

Anna Whitehouse, better known as Mother Pukka, was hospitalised earlier this year after a false widow spider bite became infected and developed into sepsis.

View 3 Images Anna Whitehouse was hospitalised after a false widow spider bite became infected (Image: Charlotte Gray/Cover Images)

If you think UK spider bites are harmless, you may need to think again. The belief that Britain's spiders can't cause serious harm is one of the top 10 bug bite myths still circulating in the UK, according to new research by Asda Pharmacy.

‌



And it’s one that content creator, broadcaster and journalist Anna Whitehouse knows is untrue. Anna, better known as Mother Pukka, was hospitalised earlier this year after a false widow spider bite became infected and developed into sepsis.

‌



Initially sent home from A&E with a course of penicillin, her condition deteriorated over the following days, ultimately requiring hospital admission, IV antibiotics and treatment for the wound.

‌



Sharing her experience with followers at the time, Anna urged others not to ignore a bite that gets worse instead of better.

View 3 Images Anna has urged others not to ignore an infected bite (Image: Anna Whitehouse/Asda Pharmacy/Cover Images)

Anna said: "If I could go back, I'd tell myself to trust my instincts sooner. I waited 72 hours hoping it would just get better on its own. By the time I went to A&E, I was sent home with penicillin, but it had already escalated further than that could fix."

‌



Her wound became increasingly bloodied and ulcerated over the following days, leaving Anna seriously ill in hospital and in intense pain.

The research from Asda Pharmacy found that four in 10 Brits still believe myths and old wives' tales about bug bites, with some treating them using toothpaste, vinegar or other ineffective home remedies.

Almost a quarter (23%) wouldn't be able to recognise the signs of an infected bite, while 35% admit they have left a bite untreated because they didn't want to "make a fuss".

‌



Meanwhile, 69% of GPs say they regularly see patients with insect bites that could have been treated at a pharmacy instead.

With two in five Brits (40%) unaware that pharmacists can assess and treat infected bites, including prescribing antibiotics where appropriate, Asda Pharmacy has launched a simple acronym to help people know when to choose Pharmacy First over their GP.

View 3 Images 69% of GPs say they regularly see patients with insect bites that could have been treated at a pharmacy instead (Image: Asda Pharmacy/Cover Images)

‌



BITE is a straightforward guide to preventing and treating insect bites:

B – Be prepared: Apply insect repellent before heading to known hotspots.

I – Itching spreads infection: Resist the urge to scratch.

‌



T – Treat it early: Asda Pharmacy can provide expert advice and prescriptions including antibiotics.

E – Extreme reactions? Head straight to A&E.

Faisal Tuddy, head of pharmacy at Asda, said: "Every summer we see the same myths doing the rounds, and the same painful mistakes.

‌



“Toothpaste won't soothe a sting, and trying to suck out venom can do more harm than good. Most bites are nothing to worry about with the right first aid, but some need prompt treatment to avoid infection - and that's exactly what Pharmacy First is there for.

“You can walk into any Asda Pharmacy, no appointment needed, and we'll assess it, treat it, and prescribe antibiotics on the spot if needed.”

Anna added: "If something doesn't feel right, don't wait it out. Get expert advice early because a bite that seems minor can become serious much more quickly than you'd think.

‌



“That's exactly why what Asda Pharmacy is doing matters - giving people a quick and easy way to get bites checked properly before they become anything like as serious as mine did.”

THE NATION'S TOP 10 INSECT BITE MYTHS

Antihistamine cream can treat an infected bite - 34% Most bites will heal on their own without any treatment - 30% Alcohol disinfects a bite or sting - 20% Vinegar neutralises a sting - 18% Tea tree oil effectively disinfects a bite - 16% Bites only become dangerous if you're allergic - 14% UK spiders are never dangerous enough to need treatment - 11% Sucking out venom helps treat a bite - 9% Toothpaste helps soothe a bite or sting - 8% Bicarbonate of soda paste removes the sting - 7%

News.title: Ebola outbreak sees soaring daily death toll as fatalities in Democratic Republic of Congo near 1,000
News.content:
Ebola outbreak sees soaring daily death toll as fatalities in Democratic Republic of Congo near 1,000

At least 930 people have now died after the Bundibugyo virus caused an outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo as frontline workers and health centres in Ituri were targeted by violence

View 4 Images Over 900 people have now died since the Ebola outbreak began around two months ago (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

In the space of just 24 hours, a further 37 Ebola deaths were recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo - one of the highest totals since the outbreak began.

‌



It comes as the country's Ministry of Health said that at least 930 people have now died as the killer virus sweeps across the nation with safety fears hampering aid efforts in one of the worst-hit areas.

‌



The 37 deaths recorded in the 24 hours spanning Friday into Saturday came out of the 2,344 cases that had been confirmed as of Saturday.

‌



The outbreak began two months ago, on May 15, and is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. Part of the reason the virus has carved such a devastating path through the Central African nation is because the virus responsible for the outbreak, the Bundibugyo virus, is less common than other causes and has no approved vaccination or treatment.

View 4 Images The Bundibugyo virus behind the Ebola outbreak has no vaccination or treatment currently (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Ebola hope as British scientists make major vaccine breakthrough READ MORE :

The virus is highly contagious and can be passed to people from wild animals. In the human population, it spreads through contact with bodily fluids of an infected person, such as vomit, blood or semen, as well as through contact with contaminated surfaces and materials such as bedding and clothes.

‌



In its latest update, the Democratic Republic of Congo's Health Ministry said that 724 patients are currently in isolation and in hospitals, and that it is intensifying response efforts in impacted health zones. The ministry said: "Patient care and support capacities are consolidating, with 22 new recoveries recorded in 24 hours."

While the disease is rare, it is severe and often fatal. The latest spike in deaths come as the response in the worst-affected province of Ituri were hampered by safety fears. In total, five of the country's 26 provinces have been impacted, all in the eastern region where rebel violence also runs rampant.

View 4 Images Safety fears have hampered responses in Ituri province (Image: AP Photo/Constant Same Bagalwa)

‌



Since the outbreak was declared in mid-May, at least 12 attacks - largely fuelled by skepticism and rumours - have been recorded aimed at health facilities and teams, according to authorities.

At the same time, health workers have walked away fro their jobs in protest over unpaid salaries. So far, at least 36 health workers who became infected with the virus have died.

Many of the attacks on healthcare centres and workers have been carried out by angry mobs who have stormed treatment centres or targeted response teams working in the field, according to Pierre Akilimali, incident manager for the Ebola response.

‌



According to Dr Adelard Lufongola, operations manager for the Ebola response, the attacks are not limited to healthcare teams with frontline workers such as burial teams also targeted.

View 4 Images Healthcare centres, staff and other frontline workers have been targets of violence (Image: AP Photo/Constant Same Bagalwa)

"Members of the various response teams have been held captive in some health zones. Teams responsible for safe and dignified burials have been threatened and continue to be threatened in some cemeteries and within several communities," said Dr Lufongola. Traditional funerals, where loved ones wash and prepare bodies, have been restricted, angering some residents.

‌



According to locals in Ituri, which accounts for about 90% of all cases, health and aid workers have been seen leaving remote communities which are considered hotspots, heading instead to Bunia.

On Thursday, UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric told reporters that humanitarian actors are "deeply concerned by escalating violence" hindering the Ebola response, and that access to treatment centres and surrounding communities remains limited.

"The worsening security situation has forced several humanitarian partners involved in the Ebola response to temporarily relocate staff to Bunia which is relatively safer," he said.

Article continues below

The World Health Organization last week expressed concerns that 80% of new Ebola cases were emerging from unknown chains of transmission, a sign the outbreak is spreading faster than health officials can track despite an expanding response.

News.title: Donald Trump's war on Iran expands despite fears US is 'running out of military targets'
News.content:
Donald Trump's war on Iran expands despite fears US is 'running out of military targets'

American President Donald Trump is expanding the war in Iran at huge cost and towards non-military targets which have little or no strategic purpose as he steers crisis towards all-out war

View 3 Images Donald Trump is expanding the war in Iran (Image: Saul Loeb/Pool AFP via AP)

The American military has carried out its ninth nightly attack on Iran in a row as the US broadens its targeting to civilian infrastructure amid claims it is “running out of targets.”

‌



It is feared the US campaign on Iran is now steaming towards all-out war with peace talks lying in tatters and growing concern Tehran is becoming more entrenched. Experts suggest the US campaign against Iran is forcing Tehran to adopt a more “horizontal” approach by spreading the war to attacks on Gulf State neighbours.

‌



And that has led to increasing concern Iran will deploys its proxies to target US facilities globally or pivot more towards its allies such as the UK or elsewhere in Europe.

‌



A western security source told the Daily Mirror : “The change in the US attacks shows that they may be running out of military targets and attacking civilian infrastructure which have no military applications. The US will try to present this as shaping the battlefield, however it seems a hollow boast. “Tactical attacks without an obvious strategy continue and are always a recipe for failure.

Volodymyr Zelensky's major revenge on Russia after Kyiv suffers massive ballistic attack READ MORE :

View 3 Images US Marine Corps F-35B fighter on board USS Boxer (Image: X)

‌



“As Iranian military options degrade then it’s expected they will retaliate in more imaginative and asymmetric ways, using the Yemeni Houthis, cyber attacks , maybe attacking US interests outside the region. The latest US service deaths have not gone down well in the US, probably more worrying is that there is no real release of information about injuries.” It follows the deaths of three service personnel - two from Iranian attacks on their Jordanian base and a third who died whilst tackling an explosive device in Iraq.

A fourth is still recorded as “missing” feared dead from an attack last week on the base in Jordan as the US is increasingly under pressure from its own rising death toll. US-based thinktank The Soufan Centre, run by respected former FBI man and Middle East expert Ali Soufan said in a report released today: “President Trump is increasing pressure on Iran to return to negotiations by expanding U.S. airstrikes to civilian infrastructure — particularly bridges that connect Iran’s Persian Gulf coastline to its major cities — but Iran’s continuing lethal missile barrages call U.S. strategy into question.

View 3 Images US Marine operation to storm vessel near Oman (Image: US MARINE CORPS/AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

“In an effort to pressure the U.S. to accede to its demands to control the Strait of Hormuz, Iran is not only making maximum use of its missile technology, but it is also escalating horizontally, targeting Gulf state infrastructure and directing its non-state allies to join its attacks.” The Soufan report also confirmed fears , first revealed in the Mirror last week, that Iran will encourage proxies to close down the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. It continued: Iranian leaders have given the Houthis in Yemen a green light to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, another key energy chokepoint, to increase pressure on energy markets and the global economy.”

As US strikes got underway early this morning and overnight a ship caught fire in the strait of Hormuz near the coastline of Oman, the British military said. It was unclear what sparked the blaze off Oman, in the southern corridor the US military has encouraged ships to use to avoid Iran’s control. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps later claimed two oil tankers were blown up after attempting to transit through the southern route of the strait.

US President Donald Trump says “Iran was hit very hard,” as strikes were reported across Iran. But Iran has reacted forcibly against the attacks. Iranian foreign minister Esmail Baghaei said an attack by the US on a watchtower in the southeastern city of Chabahar were similar to the conduct of “terrorist groups like ISIS ”. He said US tactics were “completely incompatible with international law and the principles of civilised humanitarian conduct.”

News.title: UK weather maps show 41C heatwave and hottest day ever as 10 counties reach 40C
News.content:
UK weather maps show 41C heatwave and hottest day ever as 10 counties reach 40C

Met Office forecasters say conditions could soon turn ‘very warm again’ in the UK, and weather models suggest we may see the hottest day on record during a new heatwave

View 3 Images Areas of deep red and black show where temperatures will surge above the seasonal average later this month (Image: WXCHARTS)

Brits could soon face the hottest day the UK has ever seen as weather models show temperatures potentially rising as high as 41C.

‌



The current record is 40.3C, which came during the scorching heatwave of July 2022, but now data suggests temperatures may rise as high as 41C as yet another heatwave looms.

‌



The Met Office says conditions could turn “very warm again by the start of August”, and the GFS weather model shows temperatures rising steadily from July 29 when highs of 31C are possible in the south-east of England.

‌



Highs of 30C are possible in southern England on July 30, with maps then showing potential 31C highs in south-western areas on July 31. Temperatures could reach 30C in Wales too on July 31, according to the GFS model.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 29 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Europe weather maps show 50C heatwave as tourists in Spain face hottest day ever READ MORE :

UK weather maps show most intense heatwave yet is coming as 15 counties hit 38C READ MORE :

The model then shows a massive spike in temperatures on August 1. Staggering highs of 41C are shown in the east of England, with a chunk of the country from Sussex up to Lincolnshire - including London - potentially seeing 40C.

‌



Highs of 38C are possible in the Midlands, with 37C on the cards in Yorkshire. Parts of Wales - close to the border with England - could see 31C or 32C, although peak temperatures are expected to remain below 30C in Scotland and below 25C in Northern Ireland.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on August 1 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Temperature anomaly maps for August 31 show England and Wales shaded in deep red and black. This indicates where temperatures are expected to rise well above the seasonal average.

‌



In total, the GFS model suggests 10 counties could see highs of 40C or more. They are all in the east of England.

UK counties facing 40C or more

Lincolnshire

Cambridgeshire

Northamptonshire

Norfolk

Suffolk

Hertfordshire

Middlesex

Surrey

Kent

Sussex

Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office’s forecast for the rest of July says conditions are expected to be “warmest in the south”. It adds that temperatures could potentially become “very warm again by the start of August”.

Article continues below

More of the same is on the cards later in August too. The Met Office forecast for August 2 to August 16 states: “Temperatures will very likely remain above normal, with potential for further hot spells, particularly in the south.”

However, there will also be a risk of storms. It adds: “Although most areas may see dry weather for much of the period, occasional summertime thunderstorms are possible on some days given the right ingredients.”

News.title: NHS 'serious illnesses' vaccine reminder to anyone born after 2007
News.content:
NHS 'serious illnesses' vaccine reminder to anyone born after 2007

The health service is offering advice on how to get the 'best protection'

View 2 Images People could be entering the 'second-highest risk window' for these diseases (stock image) (Image: Getty)

The NHS has issued a reminder to millions of young people born between 2001 and 2008 to check if they need protection against a wave of "serious illnesses". It comes as people aged between 17 and 25 could be entering the "second-highest risk window" for contracting these diseases.

‌



Posting on social media, the NHS said: "If you're eligible, you can now get your free MenB vaccine. MenB can cause serious illnesses like meningitis and septicaemia. You'll need two doses, given at least four weeks apart, for the best protection. Search 'NHS MenB vaccine' to check if you're eligible and learn how to book."

‌



What is the MenB vaccine? Who is eligible?

The MenB vaccine helps protect children against bacterial infections caused by meningococcal group B bacteria (MenB). These infections can cause serious illnesses, including meningitis (an infection in the brain and spinal cord), septicaemia (blood poisoning) and sepsis (a life-threatening reaction to an infection).

‌



The vaccine is also offered separately to help stop the spread of gonorrhoea. This version of the vaccine is not age-restricted - more information is available here.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Children are offered three doses of the MenB vaccine as part of the NHS vaccination schedule before their first birthday. But by the time people reach adulthood, the initial protection will have faded. The NHS website says that the MenB vaccine is offered to young people who are:

‌



Aged 17 to 18 - born between September 1, 2007 and August 31, 2008

Under 25 and starting university or moving into residential further education for the first time (born on or after July 21, 2001)

People in this age range are offered this vaccine because they are entering the second-highest risk window of their lives for contracting bacterial meningitis, according to the University of Reading. To get the free vaccination, find a pharmacy that offers MenB vaccination for young people.

View 2 Images People could be eligible for this vaccine booster (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Are there any side effects of the MenB vaccine?

Like all medicines, the MenB vaccine can cause side effects, but not everyone will get them. According to the NHS, common complaints after getting the vaccine include:

swelling or pain where the injection was given

a high temperature

feeling tired or irritable

loss of appetite

diarrhoea

These side effects usually get better within a few days. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are very rare and the person who vaccinates you will be trained to deal with allergic reactions and treat them immediately.

News.title: Andy Burnham live: New PM vows to END rough sleeping with biggest changes in 40 years
News.content:
Andy Burnham's speech in full as new PM pledges to end rough sleeping

Andy Burnham has delivered a hugely hopeful stump speech from the steps of No 10.

He said:"I have just come from Buckingham Palace, where I have accepted His Majesty the King's invitation to form a government. In doing so, I am acutely conscious that I am the sixth person in the last ten years to walk up this street, the seventh Prime Minister since 2016 - making this a moment for reflection and new resolution.

"It requires my generation of politicians to raise our game and rise to the new challenge. Britain needs to show the world that we can regain our stability once again, and that is our challenge - to make politics work, to make it work better.

"I know people at home are fed up with politics. I hear you and I want to be honest with you, we have not been good enough and we need to be better. We will be.

"We will make this moment a circuit breaker for Britain, bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years. A new political model and a new economic model. In the 1980s, Britain took some wrong turns. Political power was centralised, economic power privatised large parts of the country deindustrialized, and they still haven't recovered.

"Many feel as though they're still in decline, and they don't have the ability to turn things around. And that's why we will change politics, to make it more collaborative, more about problem solving than point scoring.

"And we will take power out of here and carry it into every postcode in the land so that they can do more and in doing more, build a new economy where we put life's essentials back under stronger public control to make them affordable to you again.

"Re-industrializing Britain using public procurement to back British industry. Later this year I will bring forward a new plan for Britain, a ten year plan laying out a path from where we are now to where I believe we all want Britain to be, wherever we're coming from, whatever party we support.

"But I can do something to give people some breathing space now, some help with the cost of living. And I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them.

"We will help more young people into work by changing the education system and giving them more support, more mental health support, and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down to meet our fiscal rules and to honor our commitments on defense to our international partners.

"We will help people to live well, building a more preventative state, investing in people's success rather than paying for failure. And that work starts now.

"I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction to end rough sleeping in our country. It's about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government.

"I will put the care of people at the heart of everything I do. I will give this my all, and I ask you all to pull with me.

"Let's build a new national sense of unity, of common purpose and positivity. Let us make this the moment when Britain starts to believe again, the moment we bring back hope. Thank you very much, everybody."

News.title: Dads arrested as fight erupts at Liverpool primary school ‘in front of kids’
News.content:
Dads arrested as fight erupts at Liverpool primary school ‘in front of kids’

Merseyside Police were called this morning after a dispute involving two men outside Wellesbourne Primary School in Liverpool - two dads were arrested

View 2 Images Police outside Wellesbourne Primary School this morning (Image: Jamie Greer/Liverpool ECHO)

Two dads have been arrested following a fight outside a primary school in Liverpool, which was witnessed by some of the pupils.

Merseyside Police said officers called to Abbotsford Road in Norris Green after a dispute involving two men outside Wellesbourne Primary School today.

Two men, aged 32 and 39, were arrested on suspicion of affray. One man has been taken to hospital to be checked over, however there were no reports of serious injuries according to police.

Wellesbourne Primary School confirmed two parents were involved in the incident. A spokesperson said: “We can confirm that there was an incident this morning involving two sets of parents which was witnessed by a small number of pupils.

“Such behaviour is completely unacceptable and will not be tolerated by the school. We expect all members of our wider community to act with respect and consideration.

View 2 Images Wellesbourne Primary School confirmed two parents were involved (Image: Jamie Greer/Liverpool ECHO)

“The incident was dealt with promptly by school staff and the police, and we will continue to work closely with the relevant authorities to address the matter appropriately.”

Two police cars were parked up outside the school and another was parked nearby this morning, Liverpool Echo reports. Officers were spotted leaving the school just before 11.30am.

People who live on Abbotsford Road said police descended on the area at around 9am and cordoned off part of the road at the junction with Fairmead Road.

Article continues below

One woman said: “I heard shouting and screaming but didn’t see what happened. I thought it was something to do with the school. I went to take my dog out and there were police everywhere, an ambulance was there too.”

Another woman said: “I didn’t see exactly what happened but it was chaos. There were loads of police, shouting and screaming. This was at about 8.30am.”

A third woman said: “I saw police cars going towards (Fairmead Road). I have no idea what happened. It’s really quiet around here.”

News.title: FIFA launch investigation into Argentina after 'disgusting' World Cup final scenes
News.content:
FIFA launch investigation into Argentina after 'disgusting' World Cup final scenes

FIFA are launching an investigation into the behaviour of the Argentina players after they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in the World Cup final on Sunday

View 2 Images FIFA is set to investigate the conduct of Argentina players after the World Cup final (Image: Getty)

FIFA are set to investigate Argentina's behaviour after the final whistle at the World Cup final. Lionel Scaloni's side sparked widespread outrage for the way they handled the 1-0 defeat to Spain at the MetLife Stadium, as players were seen getting violent and even allegedly punching some of their opponents.

‌



Leandro Paredes was shown a red card following the full-time whistle after placing his hand around Spain defender Eric Garcia's throat before kicking him to the floor. The Argentina midfielder then got into a heated confrontation with Gavi, appearing to have a swipe at his head before pushing him to the ground.

‌



Also involved in a post-match scuffle was Argentina defender Nahuel Molina, who appeared to take a swipe at Rodri as the Spain captain ran to celebrate his side's win. Molina seemed to punch Rodri's stomach which caused a furious reaction from the Manchester City star, who came rushing over to confront him.

‌



Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

As well as that, a furious Nicolas Otamendi, the 38-year-old Argentina defender, then himself had a word with Rodri to speak about his and Aymeric Laporte's pre-match comments around the referee.

It came before Argentina coach Roberto Ayala, who had a glittering playing career, appeared to throw a punch at Spain attacker Dani Olmo with Garcia then forced to step in and split them apart.

But now, in response to Argentina's behaviour, FIFA have launched an investigation, according to Sky Sports.

‌



View 2 Images Paredes was sent off for an angry clash with Eric Garcia (Image: Getty Images)

It's safe to say Argentina's behaviour wasn't well received in England, with former Newcastle United forward Alan Shearer lambasting La Seleccion as "terrible" when co-commentating for the BBC.

"Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them," Shearer said. "There is no place or space for that. We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

‌



Ex-Manchester United right-back Gary Neville, meanwhile, was clear with his verdict on ITV.

"It's a disgrace," Neville said. “I love the competitiveness of the Argentines, fighting and scrapping for their lives, Messi has propped them up, but it’s been a disgrace the last few games."

Joe Hart, the former Manchester City goalkeeper, gave a blunt verdict to Argentina's behaviour while working for the BBC. "There was one man on the pitch who did have class and that was Lionel Messi, who shook hands with every one of those Spanish players," he said. "The game's done. They could have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour."

Article continues below

Ferran Torres was the eventual match-winner for Spain in the 106th minute after Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card and sent Argentina down to 10 men. In truth, Luis de la Fuente's men were deserved winners in the end, having had 20 shots, 12 shots on target and FOUR big chances across normal and extra-time.

News.title: Burnham promises help with your money. How could it affect you?
News.content:
In his first speech as prime minister, Andy Burnham has promised to give people more "breathing space" to help with the cost of living.

Policies will be announced on Tuesday - his first full day in the job.

Cost of living is a key issue for Burnham. Many people, he has previously said, can't go out for a pint on a Friday, can't take the kids out and can't go on holiday owing to the pressure on their finances.

The cost of living has dominated people's lives in recent years, and - to some extent - our politics too. Easing that pressure hasn't been easy.

So, if Burnham chooses to support people on issues such as energy bills and the cost of transport, allows people to earn more before being taxed, and makes care and somewhere to live more affordable - he'll face tough choices on funding those moves and managing the trade-offs that come with them.

And his chancellor will often be the one who has to deliver any changes, and outline how to pay for them.

News.title: Watch: Starmer resigns, Burnham becomes PM... the day so far
News.content:
Andy Burnham has become the UK's prime minister today, replacing Keir Starmer.

The day began outside a busy 10 Downing Street where Starmer made his final address as PM, before he and Burnham visited King Charles in Buckingham Palace.

The new prime minister then gave his own speech in Downing Street saying he wants a "circuit-breaker for Britain" and bring some of the biggest changes that country has seen in 40 years.

News.title: Burnham makes ending rough sleeping his first policy pledge as prime minister
News.content:
The government said the first steps will involve helping those sleeping rough for a long period of time to move into secure housing, and includes the "acquisition of suitable homes".

Burnham, in a statement after his first speech in Downing Street, said: "On my first day as prime minister, I'm announcing this government's commitment to finally end long-term rough sleeping across the UK at the earliest opportunity.

"We'll get to work immediately, bringing together national and local government with the investment needed to get it done."

The latest annual national statistics, published by the government in February this year, estimated there were 4,793 people sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025 in England.

This was a new record high and the fourth annual increase in a row.

The number of people seen sleeping rough on a single night in Greater Manchester was recorded as 268 in 2017, 149 in 2023 and 154 in autumn 2024.

The Manchester Mill reported, external that the figure had increased to 197 in 2025.

Burnham visited homelessness charity The Passage in Victoria, London, hours before he made his first speech in Downing Street.

Challenged about his record, Burnham said the "problem was down significantly" from when he first became mayor of Greater Manchester.

He told broadcasters: "We ran a scheme every night, 600 beds, called 'A Bed Every Night' and we funded it through various different ways. But we were the only place that was doing it.

"And you won't be able to get the numbers down if you're the only place and other cities, people are coming to Manchester.

"So it taught me that the only way is to do this together."

Burnham referenced the Everyone In scheme during the Covid-19 pandemic, when thousands of rough sleepers across England were helped with housing.

He said: "Everybody pulling in the same direction, everyone in, as we did in the pandemic, because we did bring people inside in the pandemic.

"And that's what I'm saying as I go into government today. We did it then, we can do it now, get the basics right, put a care for people at the heart of everything that we do and just get this country working as it should again."

Burnham's pledge echoes one made by former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, who committed to providing 8,000 homes "immediately" to house people with a history of rough sleeping in the event of the party winning power.

News.title: Who is Andy Burnham's wife, Marie-France van Heel?
News.content:
She was described as the "coolest girl in college" when she first started dating Andy Burnham.

More than three decades later, Marie-France van Heel has walked into Downing Street alongside her husband to take on one of the most powerful unofficial roles in government - the prime minister's spouse.

Burnham has replaced Sir Keir Starmer in No 10, and he met Dutch-born van Heel, known as Frankie, when she started studying at Fitzwilliam College at the University of Cambridge in 1989.

He was in his second year of an English Literature degree, and Burnham's former lecturer, John Mullan, wrote in the Times that other students thought he had scooped the pools when they began dating.

News.title: Broadcaster and journalist Edward Stourton dies aged 68
News.content:
Broadcaster and journalist Edward Stourton, whose career spanned more than 40 years including a decade on Radio 4's Today, has died aged 68.

Stourton, who had been diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2014, died on Saturday surrounded by his family, the BBC announced in a statement.

The presenter's friend and former Today co-host James Naughtie praised Stourton's "warm intelligence and wit", adding he was "one of the best colleagues".

Another former Today presenter, Evan Davis, said Stourton was "a very important figure for all of us on the daily news programmes on Radio 4".

"One of those people you're really glad to have around," Davis reflected. "All substance, minimum ego, deeply knowledgeable, totally reliable.

"And he was one of the nicest of colleagues as well. He'll be missed."

Presenter Mishal Husain described Stourton as "a true gentleman and a broadcaster of immense capacity and intellect", while Justin Webb remembered him as "funny, self-deprecating and unpompous".

News.title: Fire crews battle blaze on Arthur’s Seat in Edinburgh
News.content:
Fire crews have spent the night battling a large blaze on Arthur's Seat in Edinburgh.

Small plumes of smoke could still be seen on Monday morning along Salisbury Crags after the fire broke out the previous evening.

Six fire engines were sent to tackle the grassfire with firefighters seen dousing the flames.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) said there were "no reported casualties" but Police Scotland said Queen's Drive, the road that encircles the Holyrood Park hills, remained closed to all vehicles.

It is the second fire in the last three months at the landmark, an ancient extinct volcano that offers panoramic views of the Scottish capital.

Edinburgh University student Mahek Jayantilial, who lives near Arthur's Seat, said she could see the fire from her window.

"I was a bit worried because I thought the fire would come this way, but thankfully there's enough concrete here to stop it," the 24-year-old told the Press Association.

News.title: My fitness tracker knew I was pregnant before I did
News.content:
Dr Stuart Lavery, consultant of reproductive medicine at University College Hospital in London, said: "People are understandably using this technology to try to get a greater understanding, and to try and pick up things as early as possible because it has such a profound impact on your life if you're planning a pregnancy."

However, "we might be running before we can walk," he cautioned.

"We probably need a lot more data on the reliability, we need a lot more researchâ¦ otherwise what happens is your levels of anxiety will just skyrocket," he said.

"I have no doubt that more people will be using technology, an app-based approach or a wearable-based approach, to try and pick up these things. But I think it should come with quite a big health warning about how much we can rely on them for accuracy."

When asked about the anxiety women reported feeling early in their pregnancy as a result of checking their ring data, Dr Chris Curry, Oura's clinical director of women's health, told BBC News: "With or without biometric tracking, pregnancy can be an uncertain time where many women, particularly those pregnant for the first time, are in the dark about the range of what's normal."

She added that if women feel overwhelmed, the company "encourages members to take a break from the app experience, whilst Oura Ring continues to collect data and gather insights", adding: "The ring is a support tool, not a replacement for your care team."

Ravika sadly did miscarry. She's hoping to start trying to conceive again soon - and when she does, her experience has made her rethink wearing her tracker again.

"I didn't really see myself as being an anxious person, butâ¦ I think going forward if it came to a point where I had an inkling that I was pregnant and my stats were low, as soon as that positive pregnancy test was there, I do think it would be the best thing for me to take the ring off."

News.title: Prisons minister Lord Timpson quits government
News.content:
The prisons minister has resigned from the government, the BBC has been told.

Lord James Timpson was appointed to the role in July 2024 after leaving his job as CEO of the Timpson group, a business which provides key cutting and shoe repair services and employs hundreds of former prisoners.

His arrival in government was greeted with much fanfare by some in the Labour Party and described as "radical" and "innovative".

But in a departing statement on Monday, seen exclusively by the BBC, Lord Timpson said he was stepping down and it was an "honour" to serve in the post.

His statement did not give a specific reason for resigning, but it is understood he feels he has done as much as he can in the role.

Prisons in England and Wales were at crisis point, reaching almost full capacity, when he first entered Sir Keir Starmer's government.

He oversaw the controversial early release scheme which saw tens of thousands of inmates let out to create more space in jails.

His critics will argue prisons continue to be violent, drug infused and overcrowded, while probation officers still report being overworked and unable to cope.

But figures do show assaults against staff and self-harm in prisons are falling.

Lord Timpson said in his resignation statement that he had left "our prisons and probation service in a much healthier and happier state than two years ago".

He added: "I'm proud to have become the longest-serving minister in this role for 15 years. I'm also proud that 75% of prisons and 90% of probation teams are now performing better than when I started.

"Self-harm, violence and assaults on staff are all down, and fewer people are leaving prison without a home to go to, a measure of dignity I care about deeply."

He also pointed to the Women's Justice Board he established, saying he "believe[s] most women should not be in prison at all" and "diverting them away from custody, helping them with often chaotic, damaged, and addicted lives, is one of the changes I'm proud to have achieved".

His critics may question why he is leaving before the Sentencing Act 2026 is enacted in September, when more people are expected to be released early and further criminals will serve their sentences in the community.

A source in the Ministry of Justice told the BBC: "We're gutted he's going but the new person is going to have their work cut out to get their head round what's round the corner."

News.title: Drug dealer exploited 14-year-old boy into selling drugs for him
News.content:
Siddiqi met the boy in Glasgow's St Enoch Centre during the school summer holidays in 2025 and asked if he "wanted to start making money".

The boy initially refused as he believed the dealer was talking about drugs.

But the High Court in Glasgow heard Siddiqi eventually persuaded the child to team up with him by suggesting he could use the cash to help his mother.

The youngster was given Siddiqi's Instagram account and later a mobile phone.

The boy lied to his mum that he had a "summer holiday camp" to go to after Siddiqi messaged him, and in mid-July the teenager was taken to a known drug den in Glasgow.

He ended up staying there for a number of days and was shown how to "bag up" crack cocaine.

Prosecutor Jennifer Nicholson-White said: "Siddiqi would attend the flat for only a couple of hours each day due to having an electronic tag. He would give the boy Â£20 to buy food."

The child was then taken by taxi to a dirty, rubbish-strewn property in Paisley in Renfrewshire.

He was told to hand out "testers" to local addicts - small samples of cocaine.

The boy ended up staying at the flat for the rest of the week.

The prosecutor said the child handed out about 60 testers and was given the phone numbers of drug users.

She added: "He estimated Siddiqi made about Â£700 each day in sales."

News.title: Ryanair profits drop as Iran war puts off passengers and lifts fuel costs
News.content:
Ryanair's profits have fallen sharply as war in the Middle East sent jet fuel prices soaring and customers reluctant to book flights.

The Irish airline's pre-tax profits dropped 34% to â¬593m (Â£503m) between April and June while sales were flat as the company was forced to cut fares to stimulate demand.

Ryanair also said it expects summer fares to be slightly lower than last year due to "consumer hesitancy" around air travel.

The price of fuelling a plane has jumped since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February and while Ryanair said it had "hedged" or struck deals for the most future fuel costs, those not included in these arrangements had more than doubled.

Crude oil prices hit $90 (Â£67) a barrel for the first time in a month on Monday, before falling back slightly, after a weekend of intense exchanges of fire between the US and Iran.

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz â an essential route for global oil and gas supplies â has ground to a halt.

An interim peace deal last month brought some respite to oil and energy prices, but they spiked again as negotiations broke down and fighting resumed.

The airline warned that its results for the year will be "highly sensitive" to external factors such as conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine as well as the price of unhedged jet fuel.

Fares for for the key summer period between July and September are on track to be "modestly" lower than last year, with many passengers booking closer to departure than normal.

The firm's finance chief, Neil Sorahan, said flights on its popular Mediterranean routes were still full. "People [are] as keen to get away as ever, albeit booking just a little bit later," he said.

Between April and June, Ryanair's revenue ticked up 1% to â¬4.4bn.

While passenger numbers rose 6% to 6.1 million- helped by the Easter holiday in April - fares fell by 6% as the airline reduced fares to entice flyers concerned about the Iran war.

Ryanair's share price fell 5% on Monday.

Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, said Ryanair was in a better position than many of its rivals, but nonetheless "visibility is worse than San Francisco airport when the fog sets in".

"The renewed escalation in hostilities in the Middle East is unhelpful and without a lasting resolution, challenging times for the airline and travel space look set to continue."

News.title: Residents told to pay £7,000 each to fix water pipe outside their homes
News.content:
Residents say they could face prosecution if they do not pay thousands of pounds to repair a water pipe outside their homes.

The residents of five houses in Pontycymer, Bridgend county, said they were told by Welsh Water that a leak from the shared pipe supplying their homes needs to be repaired at their own cost, which they estimate could cost more than Â£7,000 each.

The Garw Valley locals claim they have been given no evidence of where the leak is which their insurance companies need to cover the cost, causing sleepless nights.

A Welsh Water spokesperson said it does not own or manage the pipe so it's the responsibility of property owners, and residents have 11 days to fix it.

Welsh Water added that the leak needed to be repaired as it was wasting water, and it could issue a potential prosecution under Section 75 Notice under the Water Industry Act 1991, external.

The estimated cost of more than Â£7,000 would go towards replacing the rear water pipe in their back gardens with a new pipe at the front of the terraced row, they said, along with connecting it to each house individually.

Resident Nerys Walters said the dispute had brought her massive amounts of stress over the last two years.

She said they initially thought the cost of repairs could be covered through insurance, but with no evidence of the leak being provided, insurers have said they would not pay out.

Walters said: "It's been a nightmare situation for us that has really caused us all a lot of stress.

"Welsh Water have said they would pay for a new line that runs parallel to the front of the property, but we would then have to fund the cost of it coming in from the gate, and through the house to our rear stopcock.

Walters said she had spoken to "numerous contractors" who quoted the residents more than Â£1,000 a metre for the work.

"This has been going on for about a year and a half now and we've been asking for that evidence ever since but have been given nothing", she said.

"No evidence of the leak, and no reason as to why they adopted other pipes in the street but not ours. All the while the deadline they have given runs down. It's been very difficult and we just want to get it sorted."

News.title: Going with the flow: Renewable energy battery breakthrough
News.content:
A 3D-printed battery developed at Queen's University Belfast could "make a genuine impact" on the road to net zero, say the researchers behind it.

Flow batteries are seen as key to scaling up renewable energy, allowing it to be stored for when the wind is not blowing and the sun is not shining.

But they are expensive and typically use a metallic element - vanadium - that is only produced in a few places round the world.

Now, scientists at QUB have developed one based on iron, which is much easier to source, and have sent it around the world to help standardise research.

It is hoped it will accelerate the renewable energy revolution, making research more reliable and its findings more scalable.

News.title: 'I'm petrified my rapist could be released early'
News.content:
When Jade Belgrove finally saw the jailing of the man who raped her as a child, she thought her fight was over.

After waiting a decade to report the abuse she suffered as a 14-year-old, she believed justice had finally been served when Simon Tyler was jailed for nine years in 2024.

Now, after being told her attacker could be released years early under government plans to ease prison overcrowding, the 30-year-old from Coventry - who spoke to the BBC having waived her right to anonymity - said victims were being "let down all over again".

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said it understood "the distress victims will feel" but added prisons could run out of spaces in November "without this action".

News.title: 'No more families should endure this' - parents of student who died from MenB back new vaccine advice
News.content:
The parents of a university student who died from meningitis B (MenB) say new vaccine advice represents a "poignant moment" and will save countless lives.

Helen and Lee Draper from Pontypool, Torfaen, lost their 18-year-old daughter Meg to the disease in October 2025, just weeks after she started at the University of Bournemouth.

Last week, official advice changed, telling governments they should offer a free jab from age 15 - despite previously saying this was not cost effective.

The Welsh government said implementation took time and it must consider affordability, feasibility and the effect on the wider NHS.

News.title: Tate brothers arrested in US as further UK charges take total to 59
News.content:
Controversial influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan have been arrested in the US after British authorities issued 38 new charges against the pair.

The UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Andrew was being charged with seven further counts of rape, as well as charges relating to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child.

Tristan's charges include two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.

The total number of charges against the brothers is now 59, police said.

The alleged offending is said to have taken place between July 2010 and August 2017. The Tates have previously denied any wrongdoing.

Following their arrest, prosecutors will begin legal proceeding to extradite the brothers, who are dual British-US citizens, to the UK, the CPS said.

"These charging decisions followed receipt of a further file of evidence from Bedfordshire Police and bring the total number of alleged victims in this case to seven," Malcolm McHaffie, Head of the Special Crime Division at the CPS, said.

Bedfordshire and Hertfordshire police have been investigating a number of offences in what it called a "complex investigation".

As a result, 38 new charges were authorised against the brothers, meaning Andrew, 39, faces a total of 42 charges in the UK and Tristan, 37, faces 17.

The US Marshals confirmed to the BBC that the Tates had been taken into custody, while a US Department of Justice spokesperson said the arrests were "pursuant to extradition proceedings".

A lawyer who represents the Tates, Joseph McBride, said "the world knows Andrew and Tristan are innocent" in a statement released after their arrest on Saturday evening.

"Their enemies know it best of all. That is exactly why they have been attacked," McBride continued, describing the new UK charges as a "political hit".

He said the new charges were designed to counter a defamation action filed by the brothers in the US.

"We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free. America does not do Britain's political dirty work," he continued.

News.title: The 1975's Matty Healy marries model Gabbriette Bechtel in Los Angeles
News.content:
The 1975's frontman Matty Healy and model Gabriette Bechtel have tied the knot in Los Angeles.

The couple announced their engagement in 2024, after dating for nine months, and got married on Saturday.

A statement shared from the couple's representatives said the pair were married "at a private ceremony in Los Angeles, attended by their family and close friends".

According to several US media outlets, they were married at Madonna's former estate in the Hollywood Hills and celebrities including Charli XCX were in attendance.

Bechtel, 28 and Healy, 37 were first linked months after he split from Taylor Swift, whom he dated briefly in 2023. Their relationship reportedly inspired some of the tracks on Swift's acclaimed album, The Tortured Poets Department.

In June 2024, Bechtel shared a photo of her wearing a large black diamond ring on her ring finger on Instagram.

She wrote: "Marrying The 1975 is very brat."

Healy's mother, Loose Women star Denise Welch, later confirmed the engagement on a podcast.

Videos of Healy reportedly at his stag-do performing with The 9075 - a tribute band to The 1975 - have also been circulating online.

Bechtel also shared photos from her Las Vegas hen-do, showing the model being handcuffed and carried onto a plane by a man dressed as a police officer.

Other snaps showed fake 100 dollar bills spread across the floor, her posing with burlesque star Dita Von Teese, and dancing with an Elvis impersonator.

The American model is also a musician, known for being the lead vocalist and songwriter of the punk rock band Nasty Cherry, which was formed by Charli XCX. Her husband, George Daniel, is The 1975's drummer.

The 1975 are known for their songs Chocolate, Somebody Else, and Girls and have had five UK number one albums including their 2013 self-titled debut, 2020's Notes On A Conditional Form and their most recent album, Being Funny In A Foreign Language, which was released in 2022.

They also headlined Glastonbury last year. The band have since gone on an "indefinite hiatus" from performing live shows.

The BBC has contacted Healy and Bechtel for comment.

A patient receiving treatment for multiple ailments at a major government hospital in India died on Saturday night after a ceiling fan fell on him, according to his family and health officials.

Md Akbar, 42, was admitted to the emergency ward at Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital with hypertension, meningoencephalitis and aspiration pneumonia, local newspaper Hindustan Times reported.

He died just hours later after a ceiling fan fell on him, according to health officials familiar with the case.

Photos and videos shared by his family members showed an old, rugged ceiling fan with detached wires around his right knee as family members held his hand.

The incident occurred in the presence of hospital staff who were administering treatment to the man.

“The fan fell directly onto the patient’s bed while treatment was being administered. The nursing officer attending to him also sustained injuries in the incident,” an unnamed hospital employee told the newspaper.

The patient died at around 12.16am, less than three hours after the incident.

The death certificate for the man stated that he died from hypertension, meningoencephalitis and aspiration pneumonia.

It was not immediately clear if injuries from the ceiling fan were mentioned in his death certificate.

The Hindustan Times reported that family members of the patient protested against the quality of the treatment given to the man and the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The hospital was yet to issue a statement.

News.title: Mystery after dead body found at home owned by husband of congresswoman Ayanna Pressley
News.content:

Boston police are investigating after discovering a body inside a rental property that belongs to Conan Harris, husband of U.S. Representative Ayanna Pressley.

Law enforcement was called to the home on Malta Street, in Boston’s Mattapan neighborhood, Saturday afternoon. Upon arriving, a person was found deceased.

The two-story, seven-bedroom home where the person was found belongs to Harris. It is a rental property and is currently for sale. Pressley and Harris do not live there and never have, a person familiar with the matter told The Independent.

The deceased person has not been identified. Boston Police are conducting a death investigation, a spokesperson for the Boston Police Department said in a statement.

"The Congresswoman extends her deepest condolences to the impacted family,” Pressley’s office said in a statement.

open image in gallery A deceased person was found at a Boston home that belongs to Conan Harris, the husband of Rep Ayanna Pressley ( AFP/Getty )

The Independent has asked Rep. Pressley’s office for comment.

Police received a call around 1:52 p.m. Saturday that a person was shot at the home owned by Harris, according to a police report shared with The Independent.

Upon arrival, officers found the victim, already deceased, in the rear bedroom.

The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner determined the cause of death was a single gunshot wound.

The realtor for the property told WCVB in a phone interview that the people currently living in the rental have resided there for a while but did not specify exactly how long.

No other information is available at this time because it’s an ongoing investigation.

Pressley, who was elected to Congress in 2019, represents Massachusetts’ 7th congressional district – which encompasses some Boston neighborhoods.

She is a member of “The Squad,” a group of progressive Democratic women in the House. Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar and Rashida Tlaib are also members of the group.
