Passengers on cruise ships are paying almost half as much in tourism and other taxes compared with staying in a hotel, research suggests.

A report by clean travel think tank Transport & Environment (T&E) estimates that a night on a European cruise is taxed at 40 per cent less than staying in hotel.

Researchers claim this fails to account for the environmental costs and contribution to overtourism from cruise ships.

The report also highlights that cruise ships benefit from tax exemptions granted to commercial cargo fleets including reliefs on corporate income tax, VAT and marine fuel taxes.

The analysis looked at the taxes for €100 a night hotels in France, Italy and Spain, and compared them to cruises with similar prices. On average, it found that people who stay in hotels will pay 23 per cent of the price in taxes, while cruise passengers will only pay 12 per cent.

The report claims that in the western Mediterranean basin alone, including France, Spain and Italy, air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions from cruise ships cost local communities between €557 million and €930 million in 2025 due to the impact on the climate, public health and coastal ecosystems.



T&E is calling for a €15 tax per passenger per port call to address these differences, which it said would raise €335m a year in Italy, France, and Spain combined.

These revenues could go back to national budgets, be earmarked for the protection of ecosystems in coastal areas, or used to finance green infrastructure such as onshore power supply, the report said.

Fanny Pointet, shipping manager at T&E, said: “We are treating floating hotels like they are essential maritime infrastructure.

“Cruises are not a mode of transportation but the destination itself, yet we are giving them the same benefits as freight transport. Taxing cruise ships properly would help cities to tackle the pollution and to address concerns of overtourism.”

Industry body the Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA) has hit back at the claims.

A spokesperson said: "Cruise cannot be accurately assessed through a selective tax comparison with hotels that fails to account for the sector’s full regulatory framework, operational complexity, environmental commitments and economic contribution.

"Cruise lines pay substantial port dues, passenger charges and other local fees that support port operations, infrastructure and local services, in addition to meeting wider tax and regulatory obligations as a form of ocean-going transportation.”

CLIA also highlighted other economic benefits provided by cruise ships. The spokesperson added: "Cruise also supports a vast value chain extending far beyond the ships themselves, generating employment and economic activity across shipbuilding, ports, maritime services, local suppliers, tour operators, hospitality businesses, transport providers and destination communities around the world.

"It is an industry that supports more than 69,000 jobs across the UK, while delivering significant economic benefits to the destinations it serves."

An ex-wife of the ICE agent accused of fatally shooting a Colombian immigrant in Maine this past week — who was in the U.S. legally, according to his family — believes the tragedy could have been avoided entirely if the federal officials tasked with vetting new hires had simply contacted her before issuing the 37-year-old rookie a badge and a gun.

Ashley Brouillette said ICE’s background investigators never got in touch while considering her ex-husband and high school sweetheart David Brouillette, who joined ICE late last year, for the job.

When she heard that he had been named as the agent behind the deadly encounter, Ashley said she “was shocked, but I wasn't shocked.”

“For years, I told people he was going to hurt somebody,” she told The Independent. “I told everyone that if I ever ended up dead, that David would be the one to look at. We’ve been divorced for 17 years and he still calls me and leaves threatening messages and stuff.”

Yet, the nation’s immigration enforcement agency never bothered to ask the first of David Brouillette’s three wives whether or not she thought he had the temperament to work in law enforcement.

open image in gallery A makeshift memorial in Biddeford, Maine, after 25-year-old Colombian immigrant Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero was shot and killed during an ICE traffic stop. The ex-wife of the officer in the shooting is now speaking out about ICE’s inability to check his background ( Getty Images )

“They didn’t reach out at all,” she said. “When David told me back in November that he accepted a job with ICE, and that he wasn’t going to start for a couple of months, I thought, honest to God, he was bullsh***ing me. I’m used to him saying wacky things when he calls me drunk.”

She said she didn’t think anything more of it, until the morning of July 14, when she woke up to a call from CNN inquiring about reports that her ex had shot and killed 25-year-old Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero a day earlier during an ICE traffic stop in Biddeford, Maine.

Durán Guerrero, who reportedly had permission to work in the U.S. and had been issued a Social Security number, was not the “intended target” of the ICE operation

Had ICE done more robust due diligence, Durán might still be alive, according to Brouillette.

“This could have been 100 percent preventable,” she said.

She isn’t his only former partner speaking out.

On Saturday, David Brouillette’s second wife Lucinda Brouillette sent a message to reporters recounting what she described as her ex’s history of violent behavior.

“If you were to ask me whether I believe David Brouillette is capable of this level of extreme violence, my answer is unequivocally yes,” she wrote.

open image in gallery ICE agent David Brouillette, who shot and killed a Colombian immigrant during a traffic stop in Maine, has a violent past, according to his ex-wives ( Portland Herald )

“Throughout our marriage and in the years that followed, I have feared for a long time that his anger, aggression, and escalating behavior would eventually result in severe, life threatening violence, and I often believed I would be the one on the receiving end of it,” she said.

In court this week, she sought a protective order against him and for temporary sole custody of their 11-year-old daughter.

She had previously accused her ex-husband of kicking down her door and alleging that he routinely and falsely accused her of having substance-use issues to undermine her credibility in court, according to court records obtained by the Portland Press Herald.

Lucinda Brouillette, who was married to David while he was in the military, has also claimed that her ex sent videos of her in intimate settings to other people and was verbally and physically abusive to his daughters, according to the newspaper.

“Throughout the years, I brought my concerns to law enforcement, the courts, and the Department of Health and Human Services,” she wrote Saturday. “I tried to explain what I believed was a long-standing pattern of abuse, intimidation, manipulation, and controlling behavior because I genuinely feared where those behaviors could lead. From my perspective, those warnings did not receive the attention I believed they deserved.”

Ashley shared a voicemail with The Independent that David left her after she took out a restraining order against him in late 2025, in which he said he wanted her to die and that she and others in her “bloodline” should have their “f****** throats cut.”

open image in gallery Ashley Brouillette said ICE never contacted her and she learned about her ex’s role in the shooting from the media ( AP Photo/Mike Householder )

In an email, an ICE spokesperson declined to address the shooting, Brouillette specifically, or his hiring.

“We will never confirm or deny attempts to dox our law enforcement officers,” a spokesperson said. “Doxxing our officers put their lives and their families in serious danger. Our law enforcement officers are on the frontlines arresting terrorists, gang members, murderers, pedophiles, and rapists. Now, thanks to the malicious rhetoric of sanctuary politicians, they are under constant threat from violent agitators.”

David and Ashley Brouillette dated throughout high school, which Ashley described as “really great.”

“You couldn’t ask for a better boyfriend,” she told The Independent.

They married in 2007, and the problems began soon after he joined the Maine Army National Guard that same year, Ashley said.

David Brouillette served in the Maine National Guard from 2007 to 2010 and the Army from 2010 to 2015. He was deployed to Afghanistan from May 2012 to February 2013, leaving with the rank of sergeant.

In 2009, Ashley filed for divorce. She now lives in Michigan, more than 1,000 miles away.

open image in gallery Lucinda Brouillette said her ex husband is ‘unequivocally’ capable of lethal violence in the the wake of Guerrero’s killing ( Getty )

When President Donald Trump retook office in January 2025, he pledged to add thousands of new agents to ICE’s roster, as quickly as possible, to help carry out his campaign promise of deporting 1 million people a year.

ICE then brought on more than 12,000 fresh hires by dropping its standards — lowering a minimum age from 21 to 18 and no long requiring a college degree, among others — and accelerating the hiring process, more than doubling its workforce.

Generous signing bonuses and other financial incentives drew a deluge of applications, many from military veterans and recruits who had already worked as cops, correctional officers or security guards. But weeding out the otherwise unqualified applicants has proven challenging amid such a rapid onboarding process, an Associated Press investigation found in April.

The new ICE recruits with purportedly checkered pasts included a onetime Georgia police officer who had twice declared bankruptcy — a red flag for potential susceptibility to bribery — and had held six different law enforcement jobs over six years; a former deputy sheriff in Kansas who joined ICE after leaving his previous job amid allegations he framed an innocent woman by lying in a police report; and a police academy washout from Colorado who was eventually allowed to graduate, then turned in his shield three weeks later and never worked as a cop again, according to the AP.

open image in gallery Community outrage erupted in the aftermath of the fatal shooting by ICE of 25-year-old Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine. The ex of the agent involved said it was preventable ( Getty Images )

David Brouillette had cycled through jobs as a Department of Veterans Affairs police officer, a correctional officer, and trained to become a firefighter but was forced to drop out after a steel beam struck him in the head and left him with vertigo, light sensitivity, and cognitive defects, the AP reported and Ashley confirmed. He has also worked as a truck driver, delivered food for DoorDash, and earned a real estate sales license last year.

As a child, David Brouillette was diagnosed with severe bipolar disorder, among other things, and attempted suicide twice when he was 12, an immediate family member told the AP, describing their relative as “extremely mentally ill.” The family member broke off contact years ago for fear David would harm their family, the AP reported.

David Brouillette does not have a criminal record, but family court documents in Maine reviewed by the AP include allegations of stalking, physical abuse and cruelty directed at his second wife and teenage daughter.

On July 13, David Brouillette opened fire into a car during a stop in Biddeford, Maine, killing Durán, who lived in the area with his wife and their young child.

ICE defended Brouillette’s actions, saying that the “vehicle attempted to flee the scene and, fearing for public safety, an officer discharged his weapon.”

In the aftermath, Brouillette, according to reports, told at least three people, including Ashley, that the shooting had been justified.

Ashley told The Independent that David seemed “unusually calm” about it all, and pleaded with her to say positive things about him in public.

“It was really scary, in a way,” she said.

“I just want people to know, I tried to speak out about this years ago, but I wish that I had pushed harder,” she emphasized on Friday. “Don’t just let people silence you the way I did. Speak up, because it could save somebody’s life.”

Additional reporting by Alex Woodward

Oasis frontman Liam Gallagher has joined the chorus of voices criticizing the World Cup’s inaugural halftime show.

The final between Spain and Argentina Sunday was punctuated by a Super Bowl-style medley of performances from the likes of Madonna, The Muppets, BTS, Jason Sudeikis as Ted Lasso, Justin Bieber and Shakira.

In total, the half-time break lasted 27 minutes and 19 seconds, delaying the restart of the match and leaving many fans fuming.

On X, Gallagher reacted to the spectacle, writing: “This is like a bad trip.”

Responding to a fan who said Oasis would have “smashed” the halftime show, he added: “It’s not about us well it is but still it’s absolutely insane behavior it’s cuckoo with a capital K.”

open image in gallery Oasis’ Liam Gallagher joined the voices speaking out against the inaugural World Cup halftime show ( Getty )

open image in gallery Gallagher compared the halftime show, curated by Coldplay frontman Chris Martin, to a ‘bad trip’ ( X )

“It’s a good job I’ve got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge”, he continued in another tweet.

However, he defended pop star Bieber’s acoustic rendition of his song “Everything Hallelujah” after a fan asked: “Who thought Justin Bieber playing some acoustic Hallelujah song was going to slap??”

“ME,” Gallagher replied to the tweet enthusiastically, before adding in another post: “Justin rules.”

open image in gallery Justin Bieber was among the performers at the World Cup final halftime show, performing an acoustic rendition of his song ‘Everything Hallelujah’ ( Getty )

His comments follow those of former England soccer star and pundit Wayne Rooney, whose blunt review of the halftime show quickly went viral.

“I thought it was crap,” said Rooney live on the BBC’s broadcast of the final.

“It just didn’t get me going and I wanted the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira, but that was too flat,” he added.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino announced plans for the show, which was curated by Coldplay frontman Chris Martin, in March last year.

It included Madonna being driven onto the pitch by Brazilian footballing greats Ronaldo and Ronaldinho, before The Muppets and Los Angeles Philharmonic conductor Gustavo Dudamel performed a version of The White Stripes’ “Seven Nation Army.”

The halftime show has created controversy for Fifa, which also added in-game hydration breaks that created extra advertising opportunities, prompting criticism from fans who argued the changes prioritized entertainment and revenue over the sport’s traditions.

Before the match, a string of stars appeared for the tournament’s closing ceremony, including Hollywood actor Tom Cruise, Robbie Williams and Jennifer Hudson.

Pussycat Dolls singer Nicole Scherzinger, Italian singer-songwriter Laura Pausini and streamer IShowSpeed also performed before kick-off, along with Post Malone and rapper Swae Lee.

The search for survivors continued in Guyana Monday after a ferry, believed to be overloaded, capsized over the weekend, with the government noting that at least 35 of the 67 people rescued were not on the manifest list.

Hopes of finding missing passengers and crew are beginning to fade, as Prime Minister Mark Phillips told reporters late Sunday that officials believe there were many more than the documented 116 passengers and 17 crew members aboard the decades-old ferry.

Phillips also noted that the rescued captain and at least one other crew member tested positive for marijuana and remain in police custody pending a criminal investigation.

The MV Barima capsized off the Essequibo coast late Saturday while en route from the capital, Georgetown, to Port Kaituma in northwest Guyana, near Venezuela. Only two bodies have been found.

The prime minister said the government is launching an urgent and comprehensive probe, concentrating on the accuracy of the manifest, cargo loading, compliance with safety rules and the conduct of the captain and crew before sailing, among other issues.

“Let me be absolutely clear: Where negligence, misconduct or criminal wrongdoing is established, those responsible will face the full force of the law,” he said. “There will be no exceptions and no tolerance for actions that placed innocent lives at risk.”

Public Works Minister Juan Edghill said he is devastated about the worst marine disaster in decades and the latest developments.

“We have a zero tolerance for members of the crew drinking or smoking while at work. And for us to have positive tests from the captain, this is serious,” he said. “People’s lives are at risk, and those matters will be dealt with.”

Edghill acknowledged that officials don’t know how many people were aboard the ferry because the manifest list is not accurate.

“Nobody for the want of a few extra dollars can cheat a system and compromise the entire search-and-rescue operation,” he said. “To be confronted with a reality that despite an official manifest given to us, persons who were rescued were not manifested, that is a criminal action.”

Passengers have complained for years that clerks unofficially sell seats to friends and associates for cash while not listing them on the manifest, a scheme that has been ongoing for decades at state piers.

Boats and ferries are commonly used across Guyana, a heavily forested country with scant road systems in its interior. Many who use ferries do so because cargo rates are cheaper compared with air freight charged by domestic airlines offering daily flights to interior communities.

Several passengers said on social media that water had been seeping into the cargo area as the MV Barima limped along the North Atlantic coast on its now ill-fated voyage to Port Kaituma.

The vessel, built more than 80 years ago, was last dry docked for major repairs in 2024 and was due for additional major repairs in October.

With the BBC under more pressure than ever to prove its worth, the broadcaster has come out fighting in a celebrity-packed new advert showcasing the best of what it has to offer. And, naturally, the starry commercial has divided the nation.

Following Tim Davies’ exit, which came after the Trump-Panorama debacle proved to be one controversy too many, the Beeb is attempting to usher in a new era. Doing so isn’t proving easy though, and its new director-general Matt Britten was last month forced to kick off his stint at the top by announcing up to 2,000 job losses due to budget cuts. It’s since been revealed that some 500,000 UK households cancelled their TV licences in the past year.

Aired during Sunday night’s World Cup final, “What has the BBC ever done for me?” is less an advert and more a rallying cry for continued funding – with plenty of surreal moments packed into just three minutes and 45 seconds. The reaction has been... mixed. While some have argued the commercial is an emotional and powerful defence of one of the most important public institutions, others have suggested it’s a patronising lecture from people who we know, thanks to last week’s salary report, get paid handsomely to work for the BBC. Whichever side of the fence you sit on, there’s one thing everyone can agree on: it’s certainly sparked conversation.

The advert is actually a remake; John Cleese took the lead in the 1985 original, asking a pub barman: “Fifty-eight quid for the privilege of sitting in your own home, watching your own television set. It’s diabolical. I mean, what’s the BBC ever given us for 58 quid?” The Monty Python’s Life of Brian star was then schooled by an impressively starry range of punters, with the likes of David Attenborough, Terry Wogan and David Jason (yes, it was also quite blokey) pointing out the many services the BBC provides.

This time around, Romesh Ranganathan takes centre stage and the new version, perhaps wisely, doesn’t mention that the cost of the licence fee now stands at £180 a year for most households (thanks, inflation). The random pub has also been swapped for EastEnders boozer the Queen Vic, and Rangathan (a man who has, as the advert points out, benefited massively from multiple gigs on the BBC) starts by holding a Walford Gazette front page emblazoned with the headline: “Is the BBC really worth it?” Turning to the Queen Vic’s most overworked and undervalued bartender, he says: “It’s a good question, Tracey, but you have got to ask, what has the BBC ever done for me?”

open image in gallery Ranganathan takes centre stage in the rallying cry ( BBC )

The question is soon answered by an eclectic mix of stars making blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearances. There’s Ian Beale waiting to be served, Chris Martin proving he really does get everywhere by playing piano and Claudia Winkleman in full Traitors mode pulling a pint. “Who cares if they’ve raised two and a half billion for charity?” Romesh points out, bumping into Children in Need mascot Pudsey, as it becomes clear that subtlety is not on the agenda. That’s all before the Weakest Link host has even stepped out into Albert Square – where Alan Carr is playing EastEnders’ iconic “duff duffs” on the drums, naturally.

Ranganathan then takes us on a whistlestop tour of some of the Beeb’s most-loved and best-known studios and sets, stumbling into a kitchen where Gavin and Stacey’s Nessa speaks Welsh to plug BBC Radio Cymru, before being chased down by a pair of Daleks and crashing onto a Casualty ward, where Mr Tumble is being treated (this is what I meant by surreal).

There’s an interrogation scene with Wallace and Gromit’s nemesis Feathers McGraw, a classroom of kids chanting “BBC Bitesize helps kids learn” in a slightly aggressive manner and Clive Myrie sat at the BBC News studio’s desk, before a trip through the BBC Radio studios, Graham Norton’s chatshow set, Wimbledon and Glastonbury.

open image in gallery Theroux and his lever of doom threaten to spoil the fun ( BBC )

Things get serious with the help of Louis Theroux (whose most recent documentary, Inside the Manosphere, was released on, um, Netflix and whose podcast is produced by Spotify) as he stands by a giant BBC lever and threatens to switch it off. “None of this has to exist if we don’t want it to,” he tells Ranganathan, who is helpfully handed a folder with some vital stats. “It says here that the money we pay for the BBC creates over six and a half billion pounds for the economy,” he tells us, stepping onto a Strictly Come Dancing-esque stage where an orchestra is playing and dancers are twirling. It gets a ‘10’ from Strictly judge Anton du Beke – who is delightfully told to “bog off” by Ranganathan.

It’s all undeniably heavy-handed, but perhaps coming out all guns blazing is the best thing the BBC can do right now. The charter that sets out the corporation’s funding is currently up for renewal, and with viewing habits having changed drastically in the past 10 years, the licence fee model is facing increasing scrutiny. The fight isn’t just about money either – in order to justify its need for millions in public funding, the BBC has to prove its cultural relevance. Why not draft in the director behind John Lewis’s tearjerker Christmas ads for a big swing at proving your worth? Sure, one advert isn’t going to save the BBC. But it’s got to have been worth a shot.

News.content:

Belgium have confirmed they will not renew the contract of head coach Rudi Garcia, who bows out from the role after the 2026 World Cup.

Garcia took Belgium to the quarter-finals of the competition, where they lost to eventual winners Spain after a late error from substitute goalkeeper Senne Lammens proved costly.

His future nevertheless remained in doubt after an unconvincing tournament, which saw the Red Devils top the group but only after playing out underwhelming draws with Egypt and Iran.

They then required late heroics to avoid a last-32 exit to Senegal, coming from two down to win 3-2 in extra time, before overcoming the disadvantage imposed on them by the Folarin Balogun saga to dump out co-hosts USA.

Rudi Garcia will part ways with Belgium after the expiry of his contract ( Getty )

The 62-year-old Frenchman’s deal runs out at the end of July and will part ways after 18 months in the role.

"After discussions with the RBFA, we have decided not to extend the excellent journey we have shared over the past 18 months,” Garcia said in a statement.

“I leave Belgium in League A of the Uefa Nations League and among the top eight teams in the world.

“I would like to thank my outstanding group of players, sports director Vincent Mannaert, and the fans who supported us throughout this World Cup. I wish Belgium every success as they continue the generational transition that I was proud to help initiate."

Mannaert added: “Rudi Garcia has unquestionably played a key role in restoring the Belgian Red Devils.

“He was appointed national coach in a challenging sporting and financial context. Thanks in particular to his commitment and experience, team cohesion was restored and a strong result was achieved at the most recent Fifa World Cup.

“On behalf of the federation, I would like to warmly thank Rudi and his assistants for the past 18 months.

“Together with my team, I am currently preparing for a new cycle, including the appointment of a new national coach.”

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

News.title: How to have the perfect holiday in France’s gastronomic capital
News.content:
Calling all bon vivants. This is your city. Within seconds of tucking into a traditional andouillette (tripe sausage) or modern vegetarian cuisine in a jam-packed bistro, admiring fine art in a Renaissance abbey, or getting delightfully lost in a traboule (secret passageway) used by 19th-century silk weavers, you’ll quickly realise that Lyon is a city that knows how to live well.

Enthralling, cinematic and richly storied, after living here for 10 years, I still find myself being surprised by a walled garden I never knew, a fresque (wall mural) suddenly popping up on a riverfront wall, a new museum or river boat route.

Street-smart Romans first spotted the city’s extraordinary topography, founding Lugdunum (Lyon’s predecessor) in 43BC on the sunny slopes of Fourvière. And to this day, this basilica-crowned hill above Lyon’s quaint Unesco-listed Old Town (Vieux Lyon) is the perfect perch for clocking the mighty Rhône and Saône rivers that wend their way so gracefully through the centre.

The city’s quays, landscaped with peaceful water gardens and floating bars, buzz night and day – while culture lovers can explore a bounty of museums. Then there’s the gastronomy: among France’s finest, thanks to the unfaltering creativity and sass of city chefs, both past and present.

News.title: The 16 best things to do in Lyon
News.content:
Few dedicated foodies make the pilgrimage to Lyon without dining once chez Paul Bocuse, be it at the late chef’s mythical, out-of-town gastronomic temple in Collonges-au-Mont d’Or (which lost one of its three stars in 2020, having held three since 1965) or at the more affordable Comptoir Paul Bocuse inside landmark covered market Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse. Across the street, admire a larger-than-life portrait of the iconic chef, frescoed onto the side of a building. Inside the market, the moules glacées (cold mussel ‘soup’) at oyster and shellfish specialist Maison Merle and a gooey round of Saint Marcellin cheese from Fromagerie La Mère Richard are other local legends. Avoid buying fruit and veg here unless you have to – weekly outdoor food markets elsewhere in the city are cheaper.

To sample future talent in the Lyonnais kitchen, mingle with students over lunch, dinner or drinks and live music at La Commune – an innovative food court that hosts chefs aspiring to open their own restaurant in Lyon. Resident chefs cook up a storm at La Commune for maximum six months, meaning an ever-changing rollcall of epicurean excitement at this unique culinary incubator.

To extend the experience further afield, consider a road trip along a section of the Vallée de la Gastronomie, stretching 620km (385 miles). In Lyon, the gourmet route delves into the secrets behind chef Joseph Viola’s award-winning duck foie gras and sweetbread pâté en croûte (think French-posh pork pie) and the city’s distinctive offal-based bouchon (Lyonnais bistro) cuisine.

News.title: Spain win World Cup in triumph of football over Argentine thuggery
News.content:
Spain should have won far more comfortably, but the European champions lived up to the claim made by their coach Luis de la Fuente and proved they are the best team in the world, having beaten the favourites France in the last four.

Spain won this tournament for the second time, 16 years after the first. Now there is just one nation chasing a “second star”, the one beaten by Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday.

If England ever want to win this again then here is the blueprint. This is how the game should be played. Get the ball, keep the ball, love the ball, move the ball. Try to play. Be brave and stay brave. It is not complicated, but it requires a re-education.

Maybe one day English football will grow up and cherish ball-players of their own, rather than Manchester City signing Rodri, who was magnificent here until he tired, or Arsenal with Martín Zubimendi, who successfully replaced him.

Rodri was named player of the tournament, in recognition of the football his nation played and the 30-year-old’s importance to to their system. He is their heartbeat and metronome. England do not just need to find a Rodri, but cherish whoever that is.

News.title: Hamilton takes out Russell as Antonelli stretches lead with Belgian GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

Sports.title: Zlatan Ibrahimovic makes shock Fox exit announcement in final seconds of World Cup live TV broadcast
Sports.content:
ZLATAN Ibrahimovic made a shock Fox exit announcement in the final seconds of their World Cup final broadcast.

Ibrahimovic, 44, has been a very popular addition to Fox’s coverage of the entire tournament.



So much so, Fox wanted to bring him back alongside anchor Rebecca Lowe and co-analysts Thierry Henry and Alexi Lalas for the 2030 World Cup.

However, the Swedish soccer legend has ruled himself out of any further broadcasting jobs with a definitive statement live on tv.



“I’ve been talking a lot the last one and a half months, so I want to take this moment to say, Alexi, thankyou, Thierry, thankyou, Rebecca, thankyou,” he began.

“You made it easy for me, I hope America you enjoyed it as much as I did,” he said after thanking Fox and the whole production crew.

“This is also my farewell to the studio, this was the first and last time for me, so thankyou,” he then declared in a shock statement.

It came as a surprise to Lowe and likely the rest of the broadcast crew as she responded, “It is?”

The moment summed up what was an emotional goodbye for all after a World Cup to remember on Fox’s coverage.

Anchor Rebecca Lowe was fighting back tears at the end having done a tremendous job all summer long.



Fox’s coverage in the early stages was dominated by tension between Ibrahimovic and Lalas.

The two are clearly quite outspoken figures with strong opinions that clashed a fair amount.

Lowe made clear in an interview, however, that there was an underlying respect between the pair despite all the drama.

‘These stories do make me laugh and we do laugh about them. We’re like, ‘another one?’ And it is getting a little out of hand,” she had said to talkSPORT.

“‘We are going through every newspaper now. Like, okay guys, maybe let’s pivot and write about something else, that would be good. The football, maybe?”



On that very point, the soccer came to its ultimate conclusion when Spain beat Argentina in the World Cup final 1-0 to lift the game’s ultimate prize.

Who they will get to replace Ibrahimovic for the 2030 World Cup remains unclear, as does whether they will even get the rights.

But should they do so, there will undoubtedly be a strong effort to get Lowe, Henry and Lalas back in the studio.

Sports.title: David Raya narrowly avoids dangerous medal accident during Spain World Cup celebrations
Sports.content:
DAVID RAYA narrowly avoided a nasty accident after his medal got tangled in the goal net following Spain’s World Cup victory.

Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game in the 106th minute, denying Argentina the opportunity to retain the title.



As the party began for the Europeans, the Arsenal keeper had climbed up the posts to celebrate and snip off what was left of the net as a memento.

But as the Spaniard – who did not make an appearance at this World Cup – attempted to come back down, his gold medal snagged in the netting.



The Spain No1 was left hanging awkwardly for a split second as the ribbon around his neck tightened, with the medal refusing to come free.

Raya quickly realised what had happened and managed to unhook it before dropping safely back onto the turf to continue the celebrations.

The 30-year-old could then be seen laughing off the incident as Spain’s players soaked up the moment after becoming world champions.

The European champions created by far the better chances throughout.

Meanwhile the holders spent much of the game trying to break up play before Enzo Fernandez was sent off moments before extra-time.

Torres finally made Spain’s dominance count in added extra time.

He latched onto Nico Williams’ flick-on before drilling a close-range finish past Emi Martinez to seal the win.

Spain completed a stunning double after following up their European Championship triumph under Luis de la Fuente.

But much of the celebrations on the pitch have been shrouded in ugly scenes of violence from losers Argentina.

Sports.title: Benidorm goes wild as England and Spain fans come together to celebrate Argentina World Cup final loss
Sports.content:
IT’S no surprise that the streets of Spain were party central after they won the World Cup final with a 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina.

But Spaniards may have been mildly surprised to see themselves flanked by jubilant English fans, too.



The two sets of supporters were united as England’s disdain for beaten finalists Argentina gave the tourists plenty to celebrate too.

Videos have been posted online of the fans singing in unison “f*** Argentina” in the streets.



And unlike the match itself, the Spanish press reported that the Benidorm streets celebrated in a state of euphoria without any serious incidents at all.

On the pitch, that was not the case.



Leandro Paredes was sent off after the final whistle for attacking Gavi among others.

Footage has also emerged of Nahuel Molina punching Rodri in the stomach at the game’s climax.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Both are strong examples of the kind of behaviour that has led to what appears to be universal disdain for the Argentina team and their thuggish tactics.



There was already a feeling that Lionel Messi and co. might be feeling the benefit of Fifa‘s affection throughout the tournament.

Nobody completed more fouls without a yellow card than Argentina at this tournament and many believe they were very lucky to get past Egypt in the round of 16.

But their aggression and dark arts went up a notch as soon as they faced England and it only got worse against Spain.

Still, Spain managed to win their second World Cup and, potentially, Messi’s fairytale is coming to an end at 39.

Sports.title: Rodri in shock Donald Trump photo moment as fans say Spain captain ‘dictating tempo even after World Cup final’
Sports.content:
FANS have heaped more praise on Rodri for how he dealt with Donald Trump after he was presented with the trophy.

The Player of the Tournament patiently waited for the president to get out the way before lifting the trophy, with fans saying he dictates the tempo on and off the pitch.



In order to avoid Trump being at the centre of Spain‘s second-star celebrations, captain Rodri helped the lurking US leader along before lifting the trophy.

And it has gone viral on social media, with fans loving it.



One wrote: “Rodri, Spain’s captain, doesn’t just settle for controlling the timing of the midfield—he also manages to handle Trump’s exfiltration out of the winners’ trophy presentation photo.”

Another said: “Rodri has controlled the pace of the match to the point of scaring off Trump. Everything calculated.”

While a third posted: “I love how Rodri just shoves him aside!”

Ferran Torres was the hero for Spain as he smashed home from Nico Williams‘ header in the 106th minute.

A defiant Argentina held out until extra time, but the writing seemed to be on the wall after the dismissal of Enzo Fernandez in the final minute of normal time.

The South Americans didn’t manage a shot on goal until nearly two hours of football had passed, as Messi leathered it straight into the face of Mikel Merino.

The Arsenal man recovered quickly and even started doing the Trump dance during the presentation.

The bitter Argentinians made their own headlines immediately after the game as they started a mass brawl.

Boca Juniors man Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the scrap as he went for Gavi.

And footage has now emerged of an Argentina coach attacking Spain star Dani Olmo.

Sports.title: Argentina hatchet man Leandro Paredes’ wildest moments – from World Cup final brawl to double dissent and Van Dijk melee
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA hardman Leandro Paredes was at the centre of a heated bust-up after Sunday’s World Cup final – but he is no stranger to tension on or off the pitch.

Paredes, 32, saw the Albiceleste surrender their world crown after losing 1-0 to Spain at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey following Ferran Torres’ extra time winner.



Lionel Messi and Co only managed two shots – both off target – during the 120-minute affair and lost Enzo Fernandez to a second yellow card just before extra-time.

And Paredes lost his temper at full-time as he got into a row with Spain players and made headlines once more for all the wrong reasons.



But it is not the first time the Argentina international has landed in trouble. SunSport takes you through five occasions the Boca Juniors ace has lost his head:

1. July 20, 2026 — Argentina 0-1 Spain

Paredes lost his cool this weekend, as did Argentina team-mates Nahuel Molina and Nicolas Otamendi, who had an intense confrontation with Rodri.

But none of them got as wild as Paredes, who sprinted towards celebrating Spain players, grabbed Eric Garcia by the neck, floored Gavi and reportedly threw punches into the crowd.

2. May 19, 2024 – Roma 1-0 Genoa

Paredes spent two years playing for Roma before his return to Argentina in 2025.

And it was in 2024 when he blew his top against Genoa as he got two yellow cards in just a few seconds for dissent.

3. December 9, 2022 – Argentina 2-2 Netherlands (4-3 on penalties)

Tempers flared in the 88th minute of a tense 2022 World Cup quarter-final when Paredes committed a wild, sliding tackle on Nathan Ake.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And immediately after the hard foul, Paredes deliberately drilled the ball at full force straight into the Netherlands’ bench.

That sparked a bench-clearing melee on the touchline where Holland captain Virgil van Dijk ran over and forcefully flattened the Argentina ace.

The now 32-year-old escaped with a yellow card in a match that set a World Cup record with 18 bookings.

4. September 13, 2020 — PSG 0-1 Marseille

Paredes played a pivotal role in a full-pitch brawl during stoppage time following an off-the-ball foul on then Paris Saint-Germain team-mate Neymar.



Paredes was knocked over by Dario Benedetto before shoving him, knocking him to the ground and engaging with multiple Marseille players.

The midfielder was shown a red card alongside fellow PSG aces Neymar and Layvin Kurzawa, while Marseille’s Jordan Amavi and Benedetto were also given their marching orders.

5. November 4, 2018 — Zenit St-Petersburg vs Akhmat Grozny

Then Zenit St-Petersburg star Paredes picked up two quick and unnecessary yellow cards within minutes and got sent off in the 83rd minute.

Russian media and furious Zenit fans then accused Paredes of intentionally getting a red card as he would have been suspended for the next Premier League match.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The midfielder’s critics claimed that would allow him to fly back to Argentina and watch his beloved Boca Juniors play rivals River Plate in the Copa Libertadores final.

Paredes was forced to go on Argentinian television to deny sabotaging his team and claimed the Russian giants had already authorised his trip.

Sports.title: Fans spot bizarre ‘tribute’ in BBC closing credits after World Cup final montage
Sports.content:
BBC viewers were puzzled after spotting a bizarre tribute hidden in the closing credits following the World Cup final.

As the Beeb wrapped up its tournament coverage, fans noticed a nod to pundit Danny Murphy’s infamous childhood cat Bob.



It comes after The Sun reported the BBC had received many complaints about Danny’s rambling about the pet cat during the tournament.

The surprise message appeared after Spain’s dramatic 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in Sunday’s fiery final.



Alongside credits for the BBC‘s co-commentators, including Murphy, Charlie Adam and Pat Nevin, viewers spotted a separate line dedicated to the tournament’s “Commentary Mascot”.

It simply read: “Bob the Cat (RIP).”

The tongue-in-cheek tribute – a reference to Murphy’s unlikely running storyline – gained many shocked responses on social media.

The X account for Larry the Cat, 10 Downing Street’s Chief Mouser, welcomed the tribute: “Fitting that Bob the Cat got a spot in the BBC’s World Cup credits.”



Another user commented: “What has the BBC done for me. Had Rooney say half time entertainment was c**p and included Bob the cat in credits. Top work all round.”

While others reacted with surprise to the tribute.

One puzzled user commented: “He must have used all his lives up . . . . . RIP Bob.”

Another added: “Why’s bob the cat been mentioned in the BBC world cup credits?”

Another said: “Look if you are not from the UK just don’t ask.”



Somebody else remarked: “Good banter tbf.”

The former Liverpool and Fulham midfielder’s rambling about Bob became one of the World Cup’s strangest talking points.

Murphy first stunned viewers during Ivory Coast’s clash with Norway when he unexpectedly revealed that Bob once disappeared after jumping into a Royal Mail van.

The bizarre tale quickly went viral, with many fans comparing Murphy to Steve Coogan‘s hapless radio presenter Alan Partridge.

Murphy later returned to the subject while commentating on Spain’s match against Austria.



He explained that Bob eventually found his way home weeks later, but had become too wild to live with the family.

“Unfortunately he had gone feral and we couldn’t re-integrate him into the home, and he ended up living with my friend’s parents in Preston,” Murphy said.

“That was the life he had and now he has passed away, unfortunately, many years ago.

“Thanks for all the concern those who have been messaging us.”

The cat saga did not end there.



During Portugal’s defeat to Spain, Murphy revealed his family had ultimately been forced to give Bob “the red card”.

“We did try and settle Bob back into the house, but he started bullying and fighting his sister, Mary,” he said.

“We made decision to give him the red card and send him up the road to Preston.

“I think it was the right decision.”

Some viewers were left fuming after the BBC aired a big-budget licence fee ad and payment reminder during the World Cup final.



The “nauseating” four-minute clip has sparked fury online as the Beeb were blasted for the shameless new advert after a goalless first half between Spain and Argentina.

In a toe-curling four minute clip, presenter Romesh Ranganathan attempts to flog the broadcaster’s biggest shows including The Traitors and EastEnders.

To make matters worse, the BBC then showed their usual TV licence fee notice which enraged football fans during England’s semi-final clash with Argentina.

Viewers quickly took to social media to vent their rage and slammed the clip as “dreadful” as the commercial was used to ask “what has the BBC done for me?”

One user wrote: “So when we are not being bombarded by a QR code for a BBC TV licence, we were subjected to a dreadful AD. Oh dear how desperate!”



Another said: “This desperate BBC ad is beyond nauseating.”

A third added: “What did I just witness? BBC spending our money to tell us they’re wonderful and we’re ungrateful?”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Murphy has worked as a BBC football pundit since retiring from playing in 2013.

His playing days included spells with Liverpool, Tottenham, Fulham and England.

Sports.title: ‘My nan could do better’ – Fans sickened by botch job as video of centre circle being painted for World Cup final shared
Sports.content:
FANS have slammed a video posted by Fifa of the centre spot being painted ahead of the World Cup.

Many claimed it was a botch job and felt it was simply a ridiculous thing to post anyway.



The Fifa staff member explained the process in painting the spot, which includes the use of string and nails.

However the explainer video didn’t seem to receive the desired reaction, with fans jumping to criticise it.



One fan wrote: “My nan could do better”

Another posted: “This guy make it seem that you need a 4 year college degree to paint a dot in the middle of the pitch.”



A third said: “Anyone interested in a watching a 2 minute FIFA video on “preparing” the centre spot for the World Cup final?”

While a fourth wrote: “Ever wondered how groundskeepers paint a perfect centre circle? Well… you need to find another video because this ain’t one!”

It’s not the first time Fifa have been criticised this tournament, having made headlines after controversially lifting USA star Folarin Balogun’s ban following a phone call from Donald Trump.

Some pundits called for President Gianni Infantino to resign after the scandal.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Following the painting of the centre spot, Spain and Argentina played out the World Cup final.

It was a largely uneventful clash, with Spain controlling things for the majority and even more so after Enzo Fernandez was dismissed following two bookings in 11 minutes.

Luis de la Fuente’s team made the breakthrough in the 106th minute as Barca ace Ferran Torres smashed home after Nico Williams‘ head back.

And having not had a shot on goal, the opener forced Argentina to attack and they recorded their first attempt in the 117th minute.



Spain came out worthy winners but the scenes turned ugly almost immediately after the final whistle.

The Argentina players took their frustrations out on their opponents as they started a mass brawl, Boca Juniors man Leandro Paredes was at the centre of the scrap as he went for Gavi.

Sports.title: England wag Megan Pickford stuck on runway for six hours as flight home from World Cup delayed almost a day
Sports.content:
JORDAN PICKFORD’S wife Megan had the trip home from hell as she attempted to leave New York.

England finished the World Cup in third place after beating France 6-4 in the “Bronze Medal Game” in Miami on Saturday.



But it seems a lot of the Wags and families actually stayed in New York for the majority of the tournament, obviously flying to wherever England played their fixtures.

With England finished on Saturday night, Mrs Pickford attempted to depart JFK with her three children: seven-year-old son Arlo George, two-year-old daughter Ostara Haze and one-year-old daughter Misty Celine.



But that task proved far harder than expected.

Their first flight was stuck on the runway for SIX hours waiting behind 30 planes.

Then that flight had to be cancelled because the staff had exceeded their flight limits.

So then after reclaiming their baggage and being left in the airport through the night, they then booked on to another flight that then had another SIX hour wait.

After treating herself and the kids to some New York souvenirs, Megan was ready to put her 18-hour ordeal behind her.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



But when she finally got on her next flight, she was left waiting on the tarmac AGAIN, this time for two hours as the plane had a missing part.

That would be the worst day ever if it was just happening to you – let alone the stress of entertaining three kids.



She has nearly 300k followers across her social media platforms and has an estimated individual net worth of £250,000 to £400,000 from her influencing career.

OK! Magazine estimates she commands between £5,000 and £12,000 per sponsored campaign from major family-focused brands.

Her husband Jordan grew into the tournament after a rocky start.

He now has 91 caps for the Three Lions and his performance in the Azteca against Mexico will go down as one of his very best.

However, he was not used for the third-placed play-off game with France as Dean Henderson got the nod.



Pickford joined names like Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham on Thomas Tuchel‘s bench.

Sports.title: Richarlison risks wrath of teammates with reaction to Argentina losing World Cup final
Sports.content:
Richarlison risks wrath of teammates with reaction to Argentina losing World Cup final

Spain were not the only ones left celebrating on Sunday evening after their World Cup final success over Argentina with Tottenham striker Richarlison making sure he joined in with gusto

View 2 Images Richarlison slid across his lounge floor (Image: https://x.com/footballontnt)

Tottenham star Richarlison could be in for an awkward reunion with a couple of his teammates after wildly celebrating Argentina’s World Cup final heartbreak. The South American nation were aiming to become back-to-back world champions as they took on Spain in New Jersey on Sunday.

‌



But Lionel Scaloni’s men were second best throughout the game, with Ferran Torres’ goal in extra time eventually securing the title for Spain. Luis de la Fuente’s men of course celebrated their success on the pitch.

‌



But Brazil and Spurs striker Richarlison couldn’t resist getting involved from his living room after Torres' goal. His partner Amanda Araujo shared a video of the forward sliding across his lounge floor on his stomach, before he then jumped up and leapt into the air.

‌



Of course, there is a bitter footballing rivalry between Brazil and Argentina so it’s no surprise to see Richarlison toast Spain’s success. But he might now be in for an awkward chat with a few teammates.

Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

The striker plays alongside Argentina defender Cristian Romero in North London, while the pair have also been joined by Marcos Senesi, who signed on a free transfer from Premier League rivals Bournemouth.

Richarlison of course also has history with Spain midfielder Rodri, who was named player of the tournament. He previously hit out at the decision to hand the Manchester City man the Ballon d’Or in 2024 instead of Brazil teammate Vinicius Jr.

‌



He wrote: “All of us who live football eagerly await the individual awards each season. Today, all Brazilians who love football woke up expecting to see another player from our country win an award for the best in the world after so long.

“Unfortunately, for reasons that no one can understand, the award did not come. And don’t get me wrong, Rodri is a great player who deserves to be among the best.

View 2 Images Richarlison was left jumping in the air after Ferran Torres' goal (Image: https://x.com/footballontnt)

‌



“But Vini not winning the Ballon d’Or was embarrassing, and the only one who lost today was football. I remember Vini saying that his dream was to see the whole of Brazil cheering for him. And that day was today!

“You are a giant and the best in the world, kid! And no trophy will change that. Keep going and never shut up! We’re together.”

Richarlison scored 12 goals in 43 appearances for Spurs last season but the 54-time capped Brazilian international was not named in his nation’s squad for the World Cup by Carlo Ancelotti. The Selecao only managed to reach the last 16, having been beaten by an Erling Haaland inspired Norway.

Sports.title: Argentina president makes surprising announcement immediately after ugly World Cup final
Sports.content:
Argentina president makes surprising announcement immediately after ugly World Cup final

Argentina came up short against Spain and reacted poorly at full-time as players threw punches, but the nation's president, Javier Milei, has made a surprise announcement

View 2 Images Javier Milei has announced a public holiday following Argentina's World Cup defeat (Image: Tomas Cuesta/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Argentina's president, Javier Milei, has announced that the nation will have a public holiday when Lionel Messi and co return from the World Cup. La Albiceleste fell short in their final against Spain and saw ugly scenes at the full-time whistle when members of their team threw punches at the victors.

‌



Ferran Torres' goal separated the teams in extra time but Argentina struggled to lay a glove on Spain and did not manage a shot on target. Instead, their efforts will be remembered for a number of fouls, Enzo Fernandez's red card and the unsavoury scenes upon the final whistle.

‌



Milei, nevertheless, wants to celebrate his country's achievement, having reached a second final in succession after Argentina won the tournament in 2022.

‌



"Thank you so much, players!!! "All the way to the end, with our boots on. Argentina, always on top," he said.

"WORLD CELEBRATION," Milei posted. "Given the concerns about the celebrations for the achievement of the Argentine National Team, I inform the public that, depending on what the players and coaching staff decide regarding the day to celebrate, it will be declared a national holiday."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Milei accepted it will be a difficult time for Argentina's squad but wanted to highlight the magnitude of what they had achieved. "The lessons this group has learned are enormous," the president said on Radio Mitre.

"This must be a very difficult time for the players and coaching staff, but when the initial excitement dies down, they'll realise the magnitude of what they've accomplished.

Not all of Argentina's squad are set to return to Buenos Aires, however. Many plan to head straight on holiday from the United States, or to return to their clubs immediately.

‌



View 2 Images Paredes was sent off after the game for an angry clash with Eric Garcia (Image: Getty Images)

The AFA announced in a statement: "After the final, some players from the squad will depart directly from the United States to different destinations to rejoin their clubs or begin their rest period. Meanwhile, part of the delegation, made up of players, coaching staff, and other personnel, will return to Argentina tomorrow, with an expected arrival around 5 PM."

Following the match, Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni struggled to hold back tears. His contract is set to expire at the end of the year.

‌



"I will talk to the president," he said. "I have an idea of what I would like to do. I will see out my contract and I feel the need, I don't know if something as big can be done. We need to speak this through.

"I am thankful to the president for bringing me this chance of being in this place where I am at the moment. It was a dream place for everyone. We have tried up until the very last minute to give our utmost, the staff and players. I believe it's only fair that I can take this time for myself to think this through."

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney's dramatic body transformation and alcohol ban as wife 'fancies him more than ever'
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney's dramatic body transformation and alcohol ban as wife 'fancies him more than ever'

Wayne Rooney took the World Cup by storm as a BBC pundit and the Manchester United legend's candid takes were accompanied by a trim figure

View 4 Images Wayne Rooney was exceptional as a BBC pundit at World Cup 2026 (Image: BBC Sport)

Wayne Rooney impressed as a pundit for the BBC at the World Cup and did so whilst looking stylish. The slimmed-down Manchester United icon also claims he didn't have a sip of alcohol across the five-week tournament in North America, which has been an issue in the past.

‌



After 104 matches, ups, downs and endless drama, the World Cup has concluded and Spain are your champions. Those who consistently tuned into the BBC's coverage of the competition were guided through the action by a crack team of ex-pros and broadcast royalty.

‌



For the finale in New Jersey, the Beeb's crew, who had been based in Salford until the semi-finals, presented live from inside New York/New Jersey Stadium and it was the usual trio of Micah Richards, Joe Hart and Rooney joining Gabby Logan on the panel.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gabby Logan escapes wrath of annoyed viewers after BBC makes change for World Cup final READ MORE :

Viewers have lauded Rooney's honesty and confidence across this tournament and as the BBC's final show wound down on Sunday night, a comment from co-star Richards highlighted his commendable body transformation.

Mirror Football takes a look at the new Rooney, including his five-week alcohol ban, Beeb salary and the influence of ever-present other half Coleen.

‌



New look

As soon as Rooney began his World Cup punditry role, those watching on television noticed his altered appearance. The United hero looked sleek, wearing polished clothing, rocking a clean haircut and trimming down his once very prominent beard.

During the final, his immaculate grey suit forced Richards into some praise. He said to Rooney: "I think you should have a great time, you've been great all tournament, Wayne.

View 4 Images Rooney looked dapper during the World Cup final (Image: BBC Sport)

‌



"Not a drink of alcohol. Are you going to celebrate tonight?" Rooney replied: "Listen, I'll enjoy the evening, of course I will." Richards then added: "Look at him. He looks absolutely magnificent. The hair looks great, the fit is really good. He's full of confidence. And he's had a great World Cup, so congratulations."

Coleen to the rescue

The Sun reports that this change was masterminded by wife Coleen, who now "fancies her husband more than ever." It is claimed that in the build-up to the World Cup, she knew he wasn't happy with his look and put him on a diet and an exercise regimen.

Rooney was reportedly encouraged to use their home gym and a personal trainer was hired to help him. These workouts were followed by various other treatments, including facials, to ensure he looked his best for his BBC gig. A shopping trip for some new clothes was also on the agenda.

‌



View 4 Images The United icon has been married to his wife Coleen for 18 years (Image: Instagram/@waynerooney)

This transformation is not all Coleen can be held responsible for. Rooney's admission that he hasn't touched alcohol during the World Cup comes after his struggles with drinking. Speaking on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast last year, the 40-year-old admitted he would be dead if it weren't for his wife of 18 years.

"I honestly believe if she weren't there, I'd be dead," he said. "I've made mistakes in the past which are well documented and whatever, but I'm a little bit different at times and she keeps me on that path and she's done it for 20-odd years.

‌



"I wanted to go out and enjoy my time with my friends and have a night out. It got to a point where I went too far – that was a moment in my life where I was struggling massively with alcohol. I didn't think I could turn to anyone. I didn't really want to because I didn't want to put that burden on anyone.

"I just drank for two days straight. Come training and at the weekend I'd score two goals and then I'd go back and go and drink for two days straight again. She's helped me control that massively. She's managed me because I needed managing."

BBC salary

All this managing has paid off for the reformed Rooney, who, after unsuccessful stints in management with the likes of Derby County, Birmingham City and Plymouth Argyle, has now found his feet as a pundit.

‌



View 4 Images The 40-year-old reportedly penned a contract with the Beeb in 2025 (Image: BBC Sport)

In 2025, he reportedly signed a two-year contract with the BBC that is worth £800,000. This salary is paid through BBC Studios, the corporation's commercial arm, rather than from the license fee, so his exact salary is not made public.

Nevertheless, after calling FIFA president Gianni Infantino's footwear during the World Cup trophy presentation ceremony "stupid" and dubbing the final's half-time show "c**p," Rooney has announced himself as an expert who isn't afraid to speak his mind.
