Sports.title: Trump is right – USA deserves next World Cup after putting on biggest and best tournament ever
Sports.content:
The USA knocked the 2026 World Cup out of the park and could be a host country for the 2038 tournament, which is the next one up for grabs. Donald Trump wants a new World Cup 'immediately.'

Trump is right – USA deserves next World Cup after putting on biggest and best tournament ever

England continues to show no interest in hosting the World Cup, despite being one of the greatest football countries in the world.

The United States of America just successfully pulled off the biggest sports tournament in history – and President Donald Trump already wants another USA World Cup.

7 The USA could be next in line to host the World Cup Credit: getty

"Based on the numbers, we will be requesting it again immediately,” Trump told FOX Sports.

Of course, Mexico and Canada also deserve credit for co-hosting a 2026 World Cup that set an all-time attendance record with 6,810,966 fans packing stadiums from Seattle and Miami to Monterrey and Toronto.

But the massive 104-team, six-week tourney was heavily American from the start, and that point was hammered during Sunday’s final as a Super Bowl-like halftime show was inserted into the middle of Spain’s 1-0 victory over Argentina.

“The American dream, Mr. President, came to reality," said FIFA President Gianni Infantino, while standing next to Trump. "We united the world."

Football is always the winner

There were several major controversies, and Infantino should never again allow FIFA to overturn a red-card suspension after a friendly phone call from a host nation.

But I’ll go back to what I said early in Group Stage play: You’d have to be a serious hater to still be hating on the 2026 World Cup.

The matches were fantastic from Mexico vs South Africa on June 11 to Spain making a bitter Argentina cry on Sunday at New York New Jersey Stadium.

Even that NFL venue passed its World Cup test, overcoming initial concerns about a dry playing surface to produce more than 120 minutes of sharp international football that temporarily turned soccer into America’s biggest sport this summer.

"FIFA was incredible," Trump said. "There has never been anything like it in terms of an event, let alone soccer or football. ...We're very proud of our country. We're very proud of the job that was done by everybody."

It will take years to process the financial impact of a tournament that could allow FIFA to make $9 billion on ticket sales and another $1bn in TV rights, with a projected $13bn in total revenue.

7 Donald Trump wants America to 'immediately' host another global tournament Credit: getty

7 Lionel Messi showed the passion of the World Cup Credit: Getty

But facts are facts, and all of the predictions of disaster or embarrassment that preceded the 2026 World Cup were answered with stadiums filled to almost 100 percent capacity and a reassuring lack of off-the-pitch problems.

“We have to do this again, and we have to do it while I’m around,” Trump said. “You hear that, Gianni?”

The next World Cup in 2030 will primarily bounce between Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay also hosting matches as the World Cup celebrates its 100th birthday.

The 2034 World Cup has already been awarded to Saudi Arabia.

Then we get to 2038, and that’s where it immediately gets interesting for the USA.

Trump is 80-years-old, so simple math has the current US President at 92 when the next potential American World Cup rolls around.

7 Cape Verde helped make the 2026 World Cup a two-month success Credit: Getty

7 England is focused on winning the 2028 Euros on home soil Credit: Getty

No matter what you think about Trump or the huge country that he represents, securing the hosting rights to two World Cups would give Trump a big-picture sporting legacy unmatched by all past US presidents.

Nothing is bigger than the World Cup, and the World Cup keeps getting bigger -- an expansion to 64 teams could be on the agenda.

The USA will also host the Summer Olympics in 2028 in Los Angeles.

Acting like the United States doesn’t ‘deserve’ another World Cup is laughable, especially when you remember that Qatar was shadowed by human rights questions before the 2022 World Cup – which was praised upon completion – and the 2018 tournament was held in Russia.

Yes, ticket prices were too high this summer.

But that’s much more of a FIFA issue than a USA problem.

By the end of the biggest sports tourney in the history of planet Earth, there was far more negativity surrounding Argentina’s ‘dirty’ play than the United States as a host notion.

From NFL stadiums and new grass playing surfaces to fan safety and a worldwide buzz, the USA knocked the 2026 World Cup out of the park.

7 Ticket prices were sky high but thousands of fans still turned out to support their country Credit: AFP

7 Even the halftime show wasn't that bad Credit: Getty

The real question right now is what we're all going to do now that this wonderful, crazy and must-watch World Cup is finally over?

I'll be catching up on lost sleep, shedding a few extra beer pounds and trying to remember who's supposed to win the Super Bowl next February.

England should be raising its hand and yelling ‘Next!’ after watching Los Angeles, Kansas City, Miami, Boston and Philadelphia be proudly taken over by football fans from across the globe.

Europe already has dibs on 2030, and the thought of bouncing between Spain and Portugal for potential Round of 16 matches is already making me drool.

It’s impossible to host a perfect World Cup, especially in our social media age where negativity so often reigns supreme.

But the USA wanted the World Cup back on home soil after a 32-year drought, and the United States made the initial success of 1994 look like the foundation of a skyscraper in midtown Manhattan.

The 2026 World Cup brought out the best in the United States of America, from California to New York, while a country founded on freedom and independence celebrated its 250th anniversary on the world’s stage.

The haters can hate.

But there’s really nowhere better in the world to host the World Cup than the USA, and 2038 isn’t that far away.

Sports.title: Where is World Cup 2030? Host countries, stadiums and final location for next showpiece event
Sports.content:
Where is World Cup 2030? Host countries, stadiums and final location for next showpiece event

Preparations are already underway to celebrate the World Cup's 100th anniversary across three continents in 2030.

FIFA announced in 2023 that Spain, Portugal and Morocco will co-host the 2030 men's football World Cup.

10 Majority of the tournament will be held in Spain, Morocco and Portugal Credit: Getty

However, the opening three matches of the tournament will take place in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay.

This summer's event has been a tester for the tournament to be spread across multiple hosts, with Canada, America and Mexico all putting on games in North America.

The only other time it has happened was in 2002 with South Korea and Japan.

Four South American nations initially submitted a joint bid early in 2023 but FIFA confirmed a few months later that they were only considering Morocco, Portugal and Spain.

Spain will host the next World Cup as reigning champions following their win over Argentina in New York.

Why are the first games being played in South America?

The 2030 World Cup will be held from Saturday, June 8 to Sunday, July 21 and will include 48 teams at 21 venues.

It has been 100 years since the first World Cup and FIFA is commemorating the anniversary.

The first ever tournament was hosted in Uruguay in 1930 with the nation winning the Jules Rimet as the first time winners.

Argentina was the beaten finalists in the competition while Paraguay is where CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation is based.

10 Fans have suggested that Infantino and FIFA included the South American countries in this edition in order to give the World Cup 2034 to Saudi Arabia Credit: AFP

It is the oldest confederation in the world and the only existing one at the inaugural tournament.

At the announcement, FIFA president Gianni Infantino said: "In today’s divided world, where it seems that nobody can agree any more on anything, to be able to agree on something like that is definitely an incredible message of unity and positivity.

"And we need these messages today.

"The FIFA World Cup is unique, and it is a unique catalyst as well for positive social change and unity because these tournaments, 2030, the celebration, 2034.

"They are tournaments to unite, not to divide. They are tournaments, of course, to discuss, to debate and to act.

"But most importantly, today, today is a day of unity and a day of celebration.

"Seven countries have won their World Cup today. Congratulations to Uruguay, Argentina, Paraguay, Morocco, Portugal, Spain and Saudi Arabia.

10 Lionel Messi and Argentina lifted the World Cup Trophy the last time out Credit: GETTY

"This is your day. So you should celebrate and we, we celebrate, of course, with you.

"And you, the 211 FIFA Member Associations that I can see on a giant screen in front of me, you are uniting the world.

"You are uniting the world truly, through football, because, of course, football unites the world."

Which stadiums are hosting the World Cup in 2030?

The opening three games are being staged in South America.

The Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, Argentina, which has a capacity of 100,000 people, will host as will the Montevideo in Uruguay and the Estadio Osvaldo Dominguez Dibb which will be brand new in Paraguay.

When the tournament moves to the northern hemisphere, there will be 18 stadiums between the three countries, with Spain staging the most with nine.

Madrid is home to Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid's stadiums, the iconic Bernabeu and Metropolitano Stadium.

Stadiums will span to the Canary Islands, with Las Palmas Estadio Gran Canaria also another option.

10 The Nou Camp will eventually host 105,000 people after construction Credit: AFP

10 Benfica's home has the highest capacity out of all of Portugal's stadiums, hosting 80,000 after construction. Credit: Getty

10 The 115,000 seater stadium, Hassan II Stadium, is currently under contruction and set to open in 2028 - it will become Morocco's men's team new home Credit: AFP

World Cup 2030 stadiums Morocco Adrar Stadium, Agadir - Capacity: 46,000

Hassan II Stadium, Casablanca - Capacity: 115,000

Fez Stadium, Fez - Capacity: 55,800

Marrakesh Stadium, Marrakesh - Capacity: 45,860

Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium, Rabat - Capacity: 69,500

Tangier Grand Stadium, Tangier - Capacity: 75,500 Portugal Estadio da Luz, Lisbon - Capacity: 80,000

Estadio Jose Alvalade, Lisbon - Capacity: 52,095

Estadio do Dragao, Porto - Capacity: 50,033 Spain Camp Nou, Barcelona - Capacity: 105,000

RCDE Stadium, Barcelona - Capacity: 40,500

San Mames, Bilbao - Capacity: 53,331

Estadio Gran Canaria, Las Palmas - Capacity: 44,500

Bernabeu, Madrid - Capacity: 83,186

Metropolitano Stadium, Madrid - Capacity: 70,692

Anoeta Stadium, San Sebastian - Capacity: 42,300

Estadio de La Cartuja, Seville - Capacity: 70,000

Nueva Romareda, Zaragoza - Capacity: 43,110

Barcelona's newly renovated Camp Nou is also an option which seats 105,000 people.

In comparison, Portugal have two host cities with Lisbon and Porto.

Sporting Lisbon, Benfica and Porto's grounds will all be used throughout the tournament.

In the proposal, Morocco listed six stadiums that included Hassan II Stadium which is currently under construction and will hold 115,000 people - the biggest stadium in the tournament and eventually the world.

How will the tournament work?

The format replicates 2026 and will feature 48 teams again, split up into 12 groups of four and the top two, plus the eight best third-placed teams all progress to the knockout stages.

The expansion that happened for this year's tournament means 104 matches will be played at the World Cup.

10 Marketing has already began despite the tournament being four years away

FIFA have said they will take into consideration that the teams playing in the opening games in South America will need a different match schedule in order to travel, rest and prepare.

However, there has been controversies surrounding the Centenary Matches with many concerned about the environmental impact caused by the high amounts of pollution due to construction and air travel.

The football organisation defended themselves and said the majority of the tournament is spent in neighbouring countries.

What will the weather be like?

In total, 14 of the 16 host cities are expected to be subject to extreme heat conditions.

FIFA has suggested scheduling kick-off times to evenings rather than throughout the day due to the weather.

About the weather at the event, Infantino said: "We are discussing all the time, and I think it's not just about one World Cup - I think it's a general reflection.

"Even to play in some European countries in July, it's very, very hot. So maybe we have to think.

"There are ways we can optimise the calendar. But we are discussing it and we will see when we come to some conclusion.

"We just have to have an open mind."

10 Heat exhaustion could affect the athletes and the fans Credit: Getty

10 Kick-off times ranged across 11 hours in a day, from 1pm to 10pm

10 Curacao are set to make history at the World Cup this summer as the smallest nation to qualify for the tournament Credit: AFP

Who has qualified for the 2030 World Cup

Six countries have automatically qualified already with the six home nations all gaining a place - Morocco, Spain, Portugal, Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay.

The other places are earned through qualifier games in each continental confederation.

Each continent receives a different amount of places with UEFA (Europe) receiving the most with 16.

After that, it is the Confederation of African football with the second most at nine, followed by the Asian Football Confederation with eight.

Concacaf and Conmebol both have six places, while the Oceania Football Confederation only have one place.

The final two spots will be decided through a play-off tournament featuring six teams.

Sports.title: Spain's World Cup heroes touch down in Madrid after enjoying £1K bottle of red wine and cigars in their New York hotel before late-night dash to airport!
Sports.content:
Spain's World Cup heroes touch down in Madrid after enjoying £1K bottle of red wine and cigars in their New York hotel before late-night dash to airport!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Spain have landed in Madrid after wasting no time in jetting out of New York in the immediate aftermath of winning the World Cup with the victory over Argentina on Sunday night.

Luis de La Fuente's side secured a second star for their nation with a dogged victory against a difficult Albiceleste at the MetLife Stadium just across the river from Manhattan.

But after lifting the trophy in front of a full house of their adoring fans, La Roja opted not to ring in their victory with a night of partying in the city that never sleeps.

Instead, Golden Ball winner Rodri got the party started in transit, leading a round of singing on the team bus as the jubilant players sped back to their hotel for a team meal, before moving on to Newark Airport.

Back at the hotel, noted oenophile Marcos Llorente enjoyed a bottle of Chateau Rayas Chateauneuf-du-Pape Reserve 2014 - which costs a festive £1,009 to uncork - in his room with team-mates Ferran Torres and Marc Pubil.

The stars then boarded the Airbus A350-941 waiting for them - clad in their team's livery - and took off shortly after 2am local time.

Captain Rodri lifted the World Cup as Spain touched down in Madrid on Monday afternoon

The country's most-likely weary players will now have a little downtime before their parade

Before leaving the tarmac however, the team posed for a group photo with their manager Luis de la Fuente

Join the discussion Should Spain have celebrated more publicly in New York, or was rushing home for a trophy parade the right move?

Spain's players landed at Madrid's Barajas Airport at 2.30pm local time, and stepped out onto the tarmac with the World Cup trophy held aloft.

The reasoning behind flying out immediately after winning the World Cup is thought to be that the team will be welcomed with a trophy parade in Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles - where Real Madrid often host their own celebrations.

The players are now believed to be set for just a little downtime, before heading to the picturesque square to kick-off the party on home soil.

According to Spanish outlet La Razon, officials from Madrid have organised a secure welcome for the players that is set to attract thousands of fans as the team travels to Plaza de Cibeles in an open-top bus.

Once on board the flight, Aymeric Laporte was among the players to pose with the World Cup trophy, giving it a tender kiss in his seat as he soaked up the once-in-a-generation feeling.

Spain had previously celebrated on the pitch with their friends and family, with crossover superstars including seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz also joining in on the fun.

Players were draped in flags from their regions in the country as they posed for photos and celebrated with loved ones.

But the show was thoroughly stolen by Spain's unofficial talisman Keyne Yamal - the little brother of teen starlet Lamine.

Dressed in a replica Spain jersey with his brother's No. 19 and his own first name emblazoned on the back, Keyne darted onto the pitch at MetLife Stadium, where he then ran straight into his older brother's arms.

Spain were in high spirits as they celebrated winning the World Cup on their bus home to Madrid in the early hours of Monday morning

Festivities in the hotel were limited to a bottle of £1,000 red wine drunk by Marcos Llorente, goalscorer Ferran Torres and Marc Pubill

Marc Cucurella and Gavi posed in front of the team's Airbus as they prepared to go home

The airplane arrived hours later as the city of Madrid readied a welcome home fit for heroes

Aymeric Laporte and Alex Baena both posed with the World Cup trophy onboard their plane

Rodri led a bus full of Spanish players in rounds of singing as they headed for Newark airport

Lamine Yamal had previously enjoyed a cigar in the lift as he began his journey back to Spain

The prodigal Barcelona star had celebrated earlier on the pitch with his girlfriend Ines Garcia

Yamal was all too happy to accept a hug from Keyne and quickly lifted his younger brother into the air before gently placing him back down on the field and putting a red 'Lamine' baseball hat on the toddler's head.

And that wasn't the only hat Keyne tried on while roaming around the MetLife pitch on Sunday.

A New Jersey State Trooper couldn't help but remove his cap to briefly share with Keyne, who tried it on before politely returning it to the officer.

Yamal also posed with his girlfriend Ines Garcia in a sweet photo on the pitch, with the influencer sharing it with the caption: 'You did it. Congratulations, my love - you're a world champion'.

Later, Yamal was snapped lighting a large cigar as he waited in a lift at the hotel on his journey home.

As high-spirited as Spain's celebrations were, they came in stark contrast to the ugly scenes on the pitch after the final whistle, when Argentina stars including Leandro Paredes attacked Spanish players Eric Garcia and Rodri.

Paredes throttled Garcia and pushed Barcelona star Gavi to the ground, while Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by.

Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi later complained to DAZN Spain that rival players had been complaining to the media in the build-up to the final.

Argentina players later turned their backs on Spain's trophy lift in their last bitter act following a blue-and-white campaign as noted for its thuggishness as its strong tournament play.

Sports.title: Angry Argentina fans clash with riot police in Buenos Aires after their players fought Spain rivals in ugly World Cup final scenes
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Riots broke out on the streets of Buenos Aires on Sunday night after Argentina lost out on the chance to retain the World Cup with their defeat to Spain in New York.

The national team had looked to become the first side to successfully defend their title since Brazil in 1962, and provide the talismanic Lionel Messi with a pitch-perfect international send-off at his sixth World Cup.

But cagey and attritional play meant that Argentina made just two shots during the full 90 minutes and extra time, with a late Ferran Torres goal netting a superior Spanish side their second star.

At home however, expectant crowds watched their plans for a party curdle, and instead, fans are believed to have clashed with local police in the capital shortly after full-time.

More than 15 people are believed to have been arrested in the fracas, with a number of both civilians and officers injured in the clashes according to the Sun.

Riot police brutally cracked down on dissenting fans on the streets of Buenos Aires

Trouble broke out in Plaza de la Republica near the city's iconic Obelisk after the final whistle

Police targeted supporters armed with batons and shields and fired rubber bullets in the melee

Trouble is believed to have started when fans attempted to break the protective ring surrounding the Obelisk in Plaza de la Republica.

As police tried to control the crowds, supporters at the scene flung glass bottles and other missiles - before officers retaliated with tear gas and rubber bullets.

The melee is believed to have lasted close to 20 minutes, with injuries including a man kicked in the face by a rioter and a woman receiving medical attention on the streets.

The crowds were pushed back to Avenida Belgrano, eight blocks from the national monument, after being stormed by riot police brandishing shields and batons.

Distressing scenes in Argentina came as the country's players disgraced themselves in the aftermath of their defeat to Spain in New York.

After a rough-and-tumble match, violence spilled over after the final whistle, with Leandro Paredes a particular offender.

The Argentina star throttled Eric Garcia and later pushed Gavi to the ground as he attempted to fight a raft of Spanish stars just moments after the 1-0 loss.

His team-mate Nahuel Molina punched Rodri in the torso as he was running past him, with Thiago Almada also involved in the fracas.

Head coach Lionel Scaloni attempted to defuse tensions, but focused his ire on the Spain players rather than his own.

During the match, Enzo Fernandez received a second yellow card for a reckless flying tackle on Pau Cubarsi, Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

Clouds of tear gas wreathed the city as Argentina failed to defend their 2022 World Cup

The Albiceleste had hoped that they would be able to reward Lionel Messi with a second title

In New York, Argentina players were unsettled after the final whistle with Leandro Paredes in particular lashing out

Players from both teams were caught up in ugly scenes moments after the World Cup final

Paredes was sent off after the fact but had been lucky to avoid an earlier punishment during the game

Messi attempted to get Marc Cucurella sent off by telling the referee he had covered his mouth

Even Lionel Messi didn't rise above the dark arts. The legendary forward was lambasted by Wayne Rooney after he tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the latter stages of the game.

The game descended into chaos when Fernandez received his second yellow card.

This led to a melee between both sets of players and Cucurella was spotted saying something to Messi.

The left-back then put a couple of fingers over his mouth and continued speaking, a move which the Argentine immediately reacted to and waved over the referee.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off.

This was seen with Miguel Almiron for Paraguay in the group stage and Piero Hincapie in the knockout stages for Ecuador.

However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and the referee, nor VAR, decided to intervene.

The BBC pundits were quick to hit out at Messi's behaviour as his team headed into extra time a man down.

Joe Hart said: 'Oh wow! Wow! Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

'You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.'

Micah Richards added: 'We don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.'

Wayne Rooney was similarly furious with Messi's behaviour as he said: 'It is desperation.

'Argentina play like that, we know that's what they do. But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.'

Sports.title: What my sources have confirmed to me about Bryson DeChambeau and Donald Trump, why he thinks his Open histrionics are 'good for business' and why that dangerous tactic could easily backfire
Sports.content:
What my sources have confirmed about Bryson DeChambeau and Donald Trump - and why his career in serious danger if these tactics backfire

Unlock more of the best of our golf coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

As night fell on Friday, around the time that Bryson DeChambeau was locked in remonstrations against a two-stroke penalty, a few of us were not above making the same joke.

It went a little like this: ‘How long before Donald Trump gets it overturned?’

It says near enough everything about two divisive men that it wasn’t so far from the mark – late on Sunday, after Ryan Fox had won The Open, the respected American course architect and author Geoff Shackelford reported DeChambeau had indeed floated the possibility of involving the US president in his mess.

Based on phone calls I have had with informed sources, that information is correct. The threat was made and perhaps the only surprise is that Trump did not wade in – after all, the rules of golf have always been a mysterious concept to the lord of the White House and DeChambeau is his mate.

But there was no presidential intervention. No Folarin Balogun part two, just a two-shot penalty.

We can state at the outset that DeChambeau has not commented on this – he has been walking away from the media all week. Nor has his agent responded to a request for clarification from Daily Mail Sport. But playing the Trump card would be entirely in keeping with the ever-growing delusions of a sportsman whose credibility is now under the microscope.

Bryson DeChambeau is driven to the scene of his 'crime', the fifth hole where he flattened the grass and made his backswing easier. He was later docked two shots

DeChambeau was incensed by the decision, threatening to withdraw from the Open or call his friend Donald Trump to intervene

To rewatch the footage of that incident during the second round is to conclude, in my view, that DeChambeau was lucky in the extreme – the decision by Open officials to impose a two-stroke penalty but to declare his actions accidental felt remarkably generous based on the evidence we have all seen.

Rory McIlroy spoke for more than a few of the field when he lacerated DeChambeau for his ‘performative’ antics after being called out, which is to say the buggy ride, the arm waving, and the presentation of a grave injustice. But McIlroy was more subtly damning on the subject of intent and that is the area of greater importance.

Asked if he felt DeChambeau knew what he was doing when he ‘inadvertently’ improved his swing path, the world No 2 said: ‘I'm not in his mind, but it didn't look good.’

Scottie Scheffler is among the cohort to state, unequivocally, that DeChambeau is not a cheat. And we know the stigma attached to cheating in golf – it is the immovable stain. As a label, it should not be applied lightly.

Of course, DeChambeau alone will know the truth. But it is entirely plausible that in his ever-expanding role as an influencer, he might not mind the heat, wild as that sounds. Framed another way, the attention will be good for business, which is one of the points McIlroy was driving at in his comments about the histrionics.

If that is where DeChambeau currently resides with his thinking, then it is truly grim. Then again, he has always been a contradictory sort. An enigma.

He is the outsider who always had a knack for grating on his peers and, simultaneously, he is the box-office star who brings eyeballs to his every step. Punters love him. Even in the wake of this incident, his support was overwhelming on the links of Royal Birkdale.

But, if we are to assume DeChambeau still has designs on being a serious athlete, on utilising his abundant talent, then he must know that he is approaching a cliff edge at speed.

His position in the game was shrouded in doubt long before he entered the rough on the fifth hole on Friday – his LIV contract expires at the end of this season and that tour might not even exist in 2027. But the PGA Tour have done nothing to indicate a desperation to have him back.

DeChembeau and his agent Brett Falkoff after the golfer was docked two shots. The American refused to speak to the media

Rory McIlroy spoke for more than a few of the field when he lacerated DeChambeau for his ‘performative’ antics

Even before the C-word came into the conversation, they were unwilling to grant DeChambeau a smooth off-road and we know that has affronted his ego.

Naturally, DeChambeau is within his rights to know his value as a pied-piper figure – he is immensely popular, shown by his YouTube following of almost three million. And it is true that he thinks a better living could be made in that space full-time between majors if he finds himself without a tour in the near future.

But if he is playing brinksmanship, if he thinks the PGA Tour will cave in their desperation for a showman, he will likely be left disappointed.

Just look at Phil Mickelson – both his profile and achievements dwarf by a factor of thousands anything DeChambeau has brought to golf and he is persona non grata after various scandals and acts of sporting arson. Based on conversations I’ve had this week, hell will freeze over before the PGA Tour will reunite with Mickelson.

For DeChambeau, that ought to serve as a warning. Railing against the authorities and calling for presidential favours might be good for clicks, or ‘performative’ as McIlroy put it in such withering terms, but his old rival might be surprised by how quickly the world moves on without him.

Sports.title: Revealed: Stroppy Bryson DeChambeau 'asked for Donald Trump to intervene' during his meltdown at The Open
Sports.content:
Revealed: Stroppy Bryson DeChambeau 'asked for Donald Trump to intervene' during his meltdown at The Open

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bryson DeChambeau threatened to call Donald Trump during the extraordinary rules row that broke out during The Open, it has emerged.

In a remarkable new twist to the episode, which saw the American docked two strokes in wild scenes on Friday, well-placed sources confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that the double US Open champion sought a presidential intervention at the height of the drama.

However, unlike the World Cup controversy involving USMNT striker Folarin Balogun, the White House did not get involved and the penalty was not overturned.

The detail that DeChambeau took the desperate step of playing the Trump card was first revealed by respected American course architect and author Geoff Shackelford late on Sunday, after Ryan Fox had won golf’s oldest major. While Fox’s win was a fine end to the tournament, the DeChambeau drama remained the dominant theme of the week.

Bryson DeChambeau reportedly tried to get US President Donald Trump involved in the dispute that saw him hit with a two-shot penalty at The Open

DeChambeau was hit with the penalty on the second day after 'inadvertently improving his lie'

DeChambeau was subsequently embroiled in a dramatic argument with officials at The Open

After appearing to trample the grass behind his ball in the second round, the 32-year-old was hit with a two-shot penalty by officials and demanded to be returned to the site of the incident, where he angrily protested his innocence. During his remonstrations, he threatened to withdraw and it was in the midst of this 30-minute strop that the LIV rebel raised the possibility of calling Trump, a close friend.

In losing the argument, DeChambeau toppled from one shot off the 36-hole lead to three back, before sliding further down the leaderboard on Sunday.

While Scottie Scheffler insisted DeChambeau was not a ‘cheat’, Rory McIlroy was scathing of his rival’s antics. Speaking on Saturday, the world No 2 said: ‘I was up in the players’ lounge watching it with a few other players and as soon as he made the step into the ball, we all sort of looked at each other and we were like, “That didn’t seem right”. Then when I heard that he was called in by the rules officials, it was pretty obvious for why.’

McIlroy added: ‘I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it is for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.’

Such an incident would usually be laughed off, yet given Trump's interventions at the FIFA World Cup, it could have been a hugely contentious issue.

This came when the USA suffered a blow in their last-32 World Cup win over Bosnia & Herzegovina when star striker Folarin Balogun was sent off, meaning he was set to be banned from their last-16 clash against Belgium.

However, Balgoun's ban was suspended by FIFA President Gianni Infantino, a close confidante of Trump, after the US President personally called him and urged the football supremo to allow the striker to play.

Despite Trump's interventions, the US were thrashed 4-1 by Belgium, yet the 80-year-old has repeatedly boasted about his involvement, including claiming things 'worked out much better' when speaking ahead of Sunday's final, where he was booed by many as he walked out onto the pitch.

DeChambeau's plea comes after Trump intervened to have a red card awarded to a USMNT striker suspended, allowing him to compete at the World Cup

DeChambeau's request for Trump's help also takes on added significance given the pair are close and class each other as friends.

Back in 2024 when DeChambeau won the US Open, he celebrated his success with the president's family, while the golfer is also a member of Trump's Council on Sports, Fitness and Nutrition.

The penalty ultimately proved to be inconsequential as DeChambeau struggled on the final round to end at four under par, six shots behind eventual winner Ryan Fox.

DeChambeau's attempts to involve Trump also come after legendary golfer Tiger Woods was picked up on police bodycam footage telling officers that he was on the phone with the US President following his car crash in March.

Woods, who is dating Vanessa Trump, the ex-wife of the president's eldest child Donald Trump Jnr, was arrested and charged with driving under the influence, something he pleaded not guilty to.

But in the footage, as Woods walked over to an officer at the crash scene, he could be heard to say: 'Thank you so much. All right. You got it. Bye. I was just talking to the president.'

Trump has previously described Woods as a 'very close friend' and an 'amazing man'.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Why football should fear what Gianni Infantino will do next after debasing himself for Donald Trump at this World Cup - it's no wonder conspiracy theories are running wild
Sports.content:
A vignette unfolded at the very end of the trophy presentation ceremony on the pitch at the MetLife Stadium on Sunday evening. I think we are allowed to call it the MetLife again now, by the way, because the World Cup is over and FIFA no longer need to worry about impinging upon the profits of their sponsors.

You will probably have seen it by now. Rodri is holding the World Cup trophy, ready to lift it. President Donald Trump is lingering in front of the Spain team, staying in shot. Gianni Infantino, the FIFA president, scampers across the stage like the president’s personal assistant and makes a meek attempt to usher him to the side of the Spain squad.

President Trump ignores him. Rodri snatches a glance to the side where Trump is standing and satisfies himself that Trump is just about far enough towards the periphery not to spoil the picture. Then he hoists the trophy aloft. In the wider lens shots, Trump looks like part of the winning squad. Infantino looks a little embarrassed.

That image sums up this World Cup. The players – Rodri, Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe, Erling Haaland, Lionel Messi – were so good, the Golden Boot race so thrilling, the matches so dramatic, the storylines so compelling, the brotherhood of fans so touching, that they almost banished the stench of how the tournament was debased by the FIFA president. Almost. But not quite.

Perhaps the way the tournament ended is partly to blame for that. It ended, not with a flourish but with a bitter, fractious, limping dirge of a final that was probably the worst since 1990. It was as if the tournament itself had grown exhausted by its bloated diet of 104 matches in six weeks.

It ended, too, with Argentina’s Leandro Paredes rampaging around the field at the final whistle as if he were auditioning for the next time President Trump plans to stage a UFC night at the White House. It ended with Argentina turning their backs on Spain as they lifted the trophy. It was a spectacularly graceless display.

President Donald Trump and FIFA president Gianni Infantino could not help but stick their faces into Spain's World Cup celebrations

In the wider lens shots, Trump looks like part of the winning squad. Infantino looks a little embarrassed

It was not the final that the tournament deserved. It was not the final that the fans who had paid king's ransoms to follow their teams across North America deserved, either. But it was the final that Infantino deserved. He deserved it because he debased it to a point where it was impossible for the players to outrun his deeds.

The quality of the football was as good as I can remember at a World Cup. Some of the matches that this tournament delivered were all-time classics. England’s match against Mexico in the Azteca, for the atmosphere, for the context, for the history of the stadium, for the adversity England faced on their way to a 3-2 win, was the best football occasion I’ve ever been to.

A couple of days before that, I was at Argentina v Cape Verde at the Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, where Cape Verde threatened to pull off one of the greatest shocks in World Cup history. That was also an epic encounter. It provided what, for me, was the goal of the tournament, Sidny Lopes Cabral’s brilliant curling drive over Emiliano Martinez.

There were countless others. Argentina’s comeback victory over Egypt, pretty much every game the swashbuckling French played until they ran into the finely-tuned team that was Spain, England’s heart-rending capitulation against Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta and Portugal’s win over Croatia in the last 32.

Sometimes, at World Cups, the tournament starts at a gallop and then fades away but this one kept going and going, drama after drama, all the way until the final, when it fell flat on its face.

But despite all the drama, despite all the brilliance of the players, despite the fact that first Messi and then Mbappe blew away the old World Cup scoring record held by Miroslav Klose, the World Cup could not quite outrun the voices in its head warning that something was wrong.

It had started back in December in Washington DC when Infantino, cravenly and cringingly, had awarded President Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize. This was shortly before Trump launched the USA into a series of wars, including one with Iran.

That meant the winner of Infantino’s Peace Prize had provoked a situation where, for the first time, a World Cup host was at war with one of the participants.

The quality of the football was as good as I can remember at a World Cup. Some of the matches that this tournament delivered were all-time classics, such as England's win in Mexico

Cape Verde threatened to pull off one of the greatest shocks in World Cup history against Argentina with the goal of the tournament, Sidny Lopes Cabral’s brilliant curling drive

But it was the level of servility involved in Infantino’s relationship with Trump that was concerning and embarrassing.

It raised difficult questions about quite how far Infantino would compromise football in his quest to ingratiate himself with the US president. And how much is football to be a tool of regimes in the future?

In the build-up to the tournament, Iran was told it had to move from its US training base and relocated to Tijuana in Mexico. Restrictions were placed on its movements before and after games.

Whatever the nature of the Iranian regime, it felt clear its football team was being asked to operate under different conditions from everyone else. That was the first sign of the tournament being compromised.

More seriously, it then became obvious that President Trump had intervened to try to overturn a red card shown to USA striker Folarin Balogun during the last-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. We know this because President Trump told us, and seemed rather amused by it.

Multiple FIFA officials had told media outlets the red card could not be appealed but a day before the USA faced Belgium at Lumen Field in Seattle, it emerged that Balogun would be available to play after all. FIFA’s disciplinary committee suspended the sanction and triggered widespread accusations of political interference in the World Cup, which Infantino denied.

Belgium were astounded by the move. UEFA were astounded by the move. Privately, many within FIFA were unnerved by the decision. There was talk of it being a scandal that might lead to Infantino’s hold on his football fiefdom unravelling. He has moved swiftly to head off that threat. Balogun played and the USA lost but the damage had been done.

The Balogun Affair led to accusations of corruption operating in plain sight. The World Cup struggled to regain its legitimacy after that. Once you start to doubt the veracity of what you see, then a sport is severely damaged. Look at what has happened to athletics and to cycling.

The Balogun Affair led to accusations of corruption operating in plain sight. The World Cup struggled to regain its legitimacy after that

It raised difficult questions about quite how far Infantino would compromise football in his quest to ingratiate himself with the US president

After the Balogun Affair, the conspiracy theories multiplied and suddenly they didn’t seem so far-fetched any more. Both Egypt and Switzerland claimed they had been victims of favourable treatment shown towards Argentina, because sponsors were desperate to have Messi in the final.

And when something like the issue with Balogun has happened, it doesn’t seem so outlandish.

So the football was beautiful and the performances of Mbappe, Rodri, Bellingham and Messi were beguiling but for all of that, it felt as if football took a step backwards at this World Cup.

Sports.title: Argentina and Tottenham defender Cristian Romero SNUBS Donald Trump after collecting World Cup runners-up medal
Sports.content:
Argentina and Tottenham defender Cristian Romero completely ignored US President Donald Trump after collecting his World Cup runners-up medal.

Trump joined FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to present various awards to players and match officials on stage following Spain's 1-0 World Cup final win over Argentina in extra time.

Before presenting the World Cup trophy to Spain captain Rodri, the pair handed out silver medals to runners-up Argentina.

After receiving his medal around his neck from Infantino, Romero snubbed Trump by not shaking his hand, instead he walked straight past him to join his team-mates.

The cold shoulder was spotted by fans with footage circulating on social media.

Argentina defender Cristian Romero snubbed President Donald Trump after collecting medal

Cristian Romero airing Trump.



Fair play.



pic.twitter.com/hn1jok7jUR — Out of Context Football Manager (@nocontextfm1) July 19, 2026

Trump then went on to ignore a call by Infantino to leave the stage at MetLife Stadium as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy.

The US President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they lifted the trophy and celebrated wildly.

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to perform the trophy lift, Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players - though the President remained.

He stood to the side of the squad as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

There were an estimated 1.5-1.8 billion viewers tuning in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, where Trump and Infantino took center stage once again.

Loud boos had come from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the duo undoubtedly clear.

The presentation came after Ferran Torres struck in the 106th minute with the decisive goal.

It was Spain who dominated the final and looked the most likely winners as disruptors Argentina committed 24 fouls and saw Enzo Fernandez sent off at the end of normal time.

Trump took center stage as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy on Sunday

It appeared as though FIFA chief Gianni Infantino attempted to usher Trump away - but the President remained

Join the discussion Should athletes use the world stage to make statements by snubbing political figures at major events?

But the European champions could not make the breakthrough until the second half of extra time when Torres smashed home from close range.

It was enough to seal the ultimate prize in football but when the final whistle blew the game descended into ugly scenes.

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their 1-0 win against the South Americans.

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Sports.title: Moronic Argentina fans run across TEN LANE highway in desperate bid to make World Cup final in time as travel hellscape bites
Sports.content:
Moronic Argentina fans run across TEN LANE highway in desperate bid to make World Cup final in time as travel hellscape bites

Desperate Argentina fans have been spotted running across a 10-lane New Jersey highway to make to the World Cup final as travel to MetLife Stadium became a hellscape.

A dozen fans were spotted trotting across busy lanes of traffic with MetLife in sight as some may have traveled from neighboring New York City, which became a nightmare to traverse after torrential rains flooded streets the night before.

Cars had to slow down and stop to allow the stragglers to safely cross.

Although traffic seemed fairly light outside of MetLife on Sunday, it is unclear what caused the fans to risked their lives to cross several lanes on the highway.

More than 80,000 fans are expected to descend on the New Jersey stadium to watch Argentina face Spain in the final at 3pm.

Much of the focus at the tournament has been on the weather, with France and England both seeing games delayed due to nature - be it extreme heat or lightning warnings.

And, for one final time, doubt has been cast over the kick-off time of the final this evening.

The streets of New York were flooded on the eve of the tournament's finale, with heavy rain causing mayhem. Cars were submerged and pedestrians were seen walking through chest-high water.

A dozen fans were spotted trotting across busy lanes of traffic on Sunday afternoon

More than 80,000 fans are expected to descend on the New Jersey stadium. Cars had to slow down and stop to allow the stragglers to safe cross

Between two and four inches of rain are said to have fallen, with a tornado warning also issued.

A flood watch covering eastern Bergen County, where MetLife is located, northeastern New Jersey and New York City remained in effect until 2am Sunday.

Although the heaviest rain had moved south and east by late Saturday afternoon, the National Weather Service warned that further storms could produce rainfall rates of one to two inches per hour.

The final showstopper between Spain and Argentina will be able to go ahead unaffected - but many fans may miss out.

While the worst of the horrific weather had passed by Sunday morning, leaving blue skies in its wake, the torrential conditions of the previous day left mayhem in its wake.

The dangerous conditions caused further turmoil at the region’s three major airports wrecking havoc for the thousands descending on New York and New Jersey.

Hundreds of flights into the New York area from across the United States were rocked by delays, or worse, cancellations as the downpours compounded travel problems.

Argentina fans are crossing the highway to get to MetLife pic.twitter.com/J2ATFbqA2q — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) July 19, 2026

Argentina plays Spain in the World Cup final at MetLife on Sunday

The stadium was within sight of the fans who raced to make the game

The Federal Aviation Administration ordered multiple ground stops at LaGuardia, JFK and Newark until at least 5pm ET on Saturday due to the thunderstorms.

Meanwhile, the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway was flooded, leaving drivers stranded on the washed-out roadway. Many sought safety on the roofs or bonnets of their vehicles as the water in some areas rose as high as car windows.

Sports.title: Ascot makes King George the richest race in Britain by lifting 2027 value to £2.5 million
Sports.content:
Ascot makes King George the richest race in Britain by lifting 2027 value to £2.5 million

After a successful set of financial results the track has boosted the signature middle distance prize to a value double what it was in 2024 in the week of its latest edition

View 3 Images Calandagan goes past Kalpana in the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Image: Getty Images)

Ascot has made the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes the richest race in Britain from next year.

‌



The latest edition of the track’s signature middle distance prize will be worth £2 million when it is run at the royal racecourse on Saturday. But from next year the prize-money will rise again, hitting £2.5 million, making the all-aged race more valuable than the Epsom Derby. It will mean the prize fund has doubled since 2024.

‌



With the first £2m edition of the race having attracted two runners from Japan to take on last year’s world’s best horse, Calandagan from France, plus the winner of the Irish Derby, Ascot believes the extra investment in purses has paid off.

‌



David Easterby wears lucky Sondad silks on latest leg of 326-mile charity bike ride READ MORE :

Director of Racing Nick Smith said: “In a week where the significant prize money boost to this year’s King George has resulted in two of the best horses in Japan and France being set to run as well as Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini, and eight Group One winners in total, we are delighted to confirm further significant momentum for Britain’s premier all-aged race with £2.5 million on offer next year.

“In a fiercely competitive international market, it is crucial that Britain’s flagship midsummer races are appealing to connections of the world’s best horses. The Elite Races Scheme, backed by the Levy Board and BHA in 2026, has played an important part in this venture as we continue to work with our racecourse colleagues at the Jockey Club, Goodwood and York to promote the midsummer highlights of British racing, namely the July Cup, the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth Stakes, the Sussex Stakes and the International Stakes.

View 3 Images Calandagan: named best racehorse in the world in 2025 (Image: PA)

‌



“Our whole programme is important to us, of course, as demonstrated by 52% of our races this year being run for more than 2025, and a full prize money announcement for 2027 will be made in December.”

Saturday’s race has drawn a star-studded cast of ten five day acceptors headed by Calandagan and Japan’s Masquerade Ball, who finished first and second in the Japan Cup.

Calandagan’s stablemate Goliath, winner of the King George two years ago, is also included plus last year’s runner-up Kalpana. Aidan O’Brien’s quarter features Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini, 2025 Derby winner Lambourn and Minnie Hauk, the triple Oaks winner who was runner-up in the Arc. Coronation Cup winner Bay City Roller needs rain to participate.

‌



View 3 Images Goliath: 2024 King George winner entered in 2026 edition (Image: PA)

Kalpana’s trainer Andrew Balding said: “She worked well on Saturday, I was very happy with her. She’s a very good horse on her day and loves Ascot – she’s not put in a bad turn there yet, so hopefully that will continue. I’m sure she’ll be there or thereabouts again.

“Calandagan is obviously a very good horse and we couldn’t match him last year, but we’ll take him on again and who knows.

Article continues below

“I think she’s a little bit fitter than she was last year and we were always sort of struggling to get weight off her last year. This year she has come to hand and stayed in a good place. It just seems to have occurred that way, but we are very happy with her.”

He added: “It’s one of the most important middle-distance races of the summer and has always been a main target for her.”

Sports.title: Argentine media slam Enzo Fernandez after 'one of worst matches of the World Cup'
Sports.content:
Argentine media slam Enzo Fernandez after 'one of worst matches of the World Cup'

Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez was part of the side that lost the World Cup final to Spain

View 2 Images Argentine media have reacted to Enzo Fernandez's performance in the World Cup final (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Argentine media have delivered their verdicts on Enzo Fernandez's performance in the World Cup final. The Chelsea midfielder was sent off shortly before extra time, leaving former champions Argentina reduced to 10 men and ultimately unable to defend the trophy.

‌



Argentina fell 1-0 to Spain, with the game decided by Ferran Torres in the 106th minute, following Fernandez's dismissal. The 25-year-old received his first yellow card for disputing a call by referee Slavko Vincic before being booked again in stoppage time.

‌



The final saw Spain dominate proceedings, with Argentina not registering a single shot until the 117th minute. The challenge of retaining the World Cup became even larger for Argentina after Fernandez received a second yellow card for a late tackle on Spain defender Pau Caubarsi ahead of extra time.

‌



"He might just have cost his team massively, because you know now that Argentina are going to try to take it to penalties," BBC pundit Alan Shearer said on commentary, "With him already being on a yellow card for something stupid - backchatting to the referee.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"And when you're on a yellow, you cannot, cannot make a challenge like that. That is stupid from him, it really is."

‌



Spain vs Argentina referee made two mistakes in chaotic World Cup final as FIFA informed READ MORE :

The Chelsea midfielder's performance against Spain has been heavily criticised, just days after he rescued Argentina from a semi-final exit to England. Here is how the Argentine press rated Fernandez's display.

La Nacion

La Nacion's player ratings handed Fernandez a four for his showing. The publication noted that the Chelsea star "never looked comfortable" and seemed to be "playing out of sync" with the game.

Similar criticism was directed at the rest of Argentina's midfield, though it was suggested that Fernandez became "too reserved to push forward". His challenge on Cubarsi was judged to have gone "too far", resulting in his dismissal at a "crucial moment" in the final.

‌



View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was sent off after a late challenge on Pau Cubarsi (Image: Bob Kupbens/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Ole

Ole's player ratings equally awarded Fernandez a four for his contributions. The publication insisted that the 25-year-old "lost his sparkle" against Spain after adopting a more defensive position, concentrating on "the dirty work role" he had taken on earlier in the competition.

Fernandez and midfield partner Alexis Mac Allister were identified as the players who "dropped furthest back". He was described as "tired and exhausted" when making his challenge on Cubarsi, which earned him a red card.

‌



Clarin

Clarin's assessment of Fernandez's performance opened with: "The sending-off capped off one of his worst matches of the tournament. " Awarding him a rating of five, Clarin maintained that Fernandez "failed to perform" in central midfield.

The report added that he "offered little in attack" after being deployed in a more advanced position following Leandro Paredes' introduction at the break. It was suggested that the protests Fernandez made for his first yellow card were "perhaps exaggerated by the referee", yet he was ultimately sent off following "a late challenge" on Cubarsi.

Sports.content:
Premier League 2026/27: How to watch, get tickets and every opening weekend fixture

The 2026/27 Premier League season gets under way on Friday, August 21, with a blockbuster opening weekend of fixtures

View Image Martin Odegaard of Arsenal lifts the Premier League. (Image: (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images For Premier League))

The World Cup is over and the Premier League is almost back. The 2026/27 season kicks off on Friday, August 21, with all 20 clubs in action across a mouth-watering opening weekend that runs through to Monday, August 24.

‌



The new campaign arrives with a new-look managerial landscape at several of the division's biggest clubs. Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea will all be led by new faces, with Andoni Iraola, Enzo Maresca and Xabi Alonso taking charge respectively, and all three sides face stern early tests.

‌



Title holders Arsenal get the season under way when they host Championship winners Coventry City on Friday evening, while newly-promoted Hull City face a baptism of fire when they welcome Manchester City in one of the weekend's most eye-catching clashes.

‌



Ahead of all the action, we have compiled everything fans need to know, from the full fixture list and how to watch on TV to how to get match tickets for the new season.

Friday, August 22

Arsenal vs Coventry City – 8pm

‌



Saturday, August 22

Hull City vs Manchester United – 12.30pm

Everton vs Crystal Palace – 3pm

Ipswich Town vs Sunderland – 3pm

When does the 2026/27 Premier League season start?

The 2026/27 Premier League season will begin on Friday, August 21. All 20 teams will be in action across the opening weekend through to Monday, August 24.

How to watch the 2026/27 Premier League season on TV

Sky Sports remains the home of Premier League football in the UK, with at least 215 games set to air live and exclusively throughout the season. Sky has already confirmed it will broadcast six fixtures across the opening weekend, including Arsenal vs Coventry City, Manchester City vs Bournemouth and Newcastle United vs Liverpool.

To watch these games and the many others on Sky throughout the season, fans will need a Sky Sports subscription. This is included as part of select Sky packages, such as the £44 Ultimate TV and Sky Sports bundle, which also comes with free subscriptions to Netflix, HBO Max and Disney+. Existing Sky TV customers can add Sky Sports to their package from £20 per month, though most Sky packages require 24-month contracts, during which time the price may change.

‌



TNT Sports will also show select Premier League games on TV and its new streaming home of HBO Max. TNT usually has the broadcast rights to one fixture each gameweek, with Hull vs Man United the first to be shown next season.

Fans will need a separate TNT Sports subscription to watch its coverage, which costs £30.99 via HBO Max or Prime Video’s TNT Sports channel.

Sports.title: Argentina players' families 'detained by police' after World Cup final chaos in stands
Sports.content:
Argentina players' families 'detained by police' after World Cup final chaos in stands

Police have reportedly detained members of Argentina players' families after chaos erupted in the stands following Spain's 1–0 win in the World Cup final

View 2 Images Chaos erupted in the stands where the families of Argentina players were sitting for the World Cup final

Several members of Argentina players' families were detained in the United States following the team's 1-0 World Cup final defeat to Spain. Ugly scenes erupted at the New York New Jersey Stadium after the final whistle, with Argentina star Leandro Paredes sent off for kicking Eric Garcia to the floor and grabbing the Spain defender by the throat, behaviour pundits branded 'disgusting.'

‌



Tensions didn't only rise on the pitch, they spilled into the stands where players' families were seated. According to Colombian TV channel Noticias Caracol, police were forced to intervene after incidents in the box occupied by relatives and arrested 'at least a dozen people' linked to players.

‌



The same report states that Argentina's players delayed their arrival at the trophy presentation as they headed toward the area where the disturbances had taken place. So far, American authorities have not issued an official statement on the number of arrests or the potential charges and the Argentine Football Association (AFA) has not commented on the reported events.

‌



Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

This is another negative episode for Argentina, especially after officials had reportedly warned that any misconduct would be met with the full force of United States law.

View 2 Images Police officers guard the Argentina family players' area at the end of the 2026 World Cup final match against Spain

On the pitch, Argentina were also criticised for another display of poor sportsmanship. Lionel Scaloni's side tried as many as 27 cynical tactics against Spain, but none paid off.

‌



Enzo Fernandez was dismissed in extra‑time for a wild challenge on Pau Cubarsi, earning a second booking. Spain made them pay with Ferran Torres striking the decisive goal.

At the final whistle, unsavoury scenes unfolded as Paredes was sent off and Nahuel Molina appeared to throw a punch after the match. Paredes was seen kicking Eric Garcia to the floor before pushing him back with a hand around his neck when the Barcelona defender confronted him.

He was also involved in a heated exchange with Gavi.

‌



Then during the trophy presentation, Argentina showed little interest in acknowledging the victors. As Spain's players made their way to the podium to collect their medals from US President Donald Trump, having already formed a guard of honour for Argentina, the defeated side turned their backs on the champions.

BBC pundits were stunned by the incidents after the final, with Micah Richards saying: "The first yellow card wasn't until 40 odd minutes in the first-half, but seeing that sort of stuff after the game's been played and someone's just been crowned World Cup champions, it's not good enough.

"It's quite embarrassing to be honest. Paraedes there, he doesn't need to do that, he's better than that. And it doesn't stop there, it keeps going, and going, and going. And we all know what it's like to lose a game, we can be very frustrated, we understand that. But this is not good enough, it's not a good look at all."

Article continues below

Ex-England goalkeeper Joe Hart added: "Disgusting. There was one man on the pitch who did have class, and that was Lionel Mess - shook hands of every one of those Spanish players. The game's done, they can have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour.

"Rodri, I don't think, needed to get in their faces, but when you've been wound up for 120 minutes, and you felt you've been wronged, and you've felt the referee's on your back, and you've got that win, referee's blown his whistle, leave it. And I think Argentina... Are you surprised they've gone over the line again?"

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's petulant and shameful World Cup final moment pours shame on his legacy
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's petulant and shameful World Cup final moment pours shame on his legacy

Lionel Messi's hopes of leading Argentina to back-to-back World Cup triumphs went up in smoke against Spain, with the world's greatest ever player embarrassing himself as he joined in with the dark arts of his team-mates

View 2 Images Lionel Messi of Argentina and his team-mates after the defeat to Spain (Image: ©Icon Sportswire All Rights Reserved)

Argentina went down fighting. While Lionel Messi went out pouring a little shame and ridicule on his astonishing legacy.

‌



There is a way to lose - and Messi is still not too old to learn it.

‌



The footballing genius has lit up this World Cup, defying age and logic in equal measure. He threatened to win the Golden Boot. He inspired his team to back-to-back finals and he smashed the scoring record previously held by Miroslav Klose. In short, he did everything expected of him, apart from lifting the biggest prize in sport once again.

‌



But what isn't expected of him is the kind of behaviour he showed to the watching world at the final whistle of what will go down as one the most ill-tempered World Cup finals in history.

Full list of Argentina's 27 dirty tricks in World Cup final as they ruin greatest match READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Messi has spent the past few weeks appearing to be above the law, when it comes to referees and officiating in general.

‌



The aura he carries with him leaves officials intimidated at times. No-one wanted to be that referee who sent off the greatest footballer of all time, right? In short, Messi does what he wants.

In the immediate aftermath of Enzo Fernandez’s red card for a second yellow card for his foul on Pau Cubarsi, players surrounded the Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic. And Messi used his interaction with Marc Cucurella as a chance to even the scores.

Cucurella could be seen attempting to communicate with Messi with his hand over his mouth. It wasn't even a hand really, a couple of fingers. So Messi reported him to Vincic.

‌



View 2 Images Lionel Messi points as he tries to get Marc Cucurella sent off (Image: AFP or licensors)

If this particular FIFA rule is absurd in the first place, then seeing someone of Messi's standing trying to use it to his advantage, is nothing short of shameful, embarrassing and humiliating.

In that one instance, Messi turned himself into a petulant child. You know the one, when he goes running to the teacher when another kid has stamped on his conker in the school playground.

‌



His self-respect and dignity was diminished. Quite frankly, it was pitiful to witness.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Messi has done astonishing things for football - and sport in general. But if this does prove to be his last World Cup, one of his final acts will be remembered with huge sadness.

Article continues below

He showed he was fallible. He showed he was vulnerable. He showed he was still human. And he also showed he cannot accept losing.

Time has proved that even the true greats are also flawed. And Messi has now added his name to that long list.

Sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau shows true colours with response to Rory McIlroy taunts at The Open
Sports.content:
Bryson DeChambeau shows true colours with response to Rory McIlroy taunts at The Open

Bryson DeChambeau endured a frustrating week at Royal Birkdale and also had to contend with The Open crowd giving him some stick after Rory McIlroy slammed his actions

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau remained in good spirits despite being given a tough time by The Open crowd (Image: Getty Images)

Bryson DeChambeau found himself at the centre of a storm at The Open Championship. The LIV Golf star threatened to withdraw from the tournament at the halfway stage after being given a two-stroke penalty for trampling on long grass and inadvertently improving his lie.

‌



Without that he would've been well in contention heading into the final round, which ultimately ended up being a disappointing two-over to finish on four-under for the week. Ryan Fox secured a shock victory with a birdie at the last to finish 10-under.

‌



DeChambeau's rule-break drama threatened to overshadow the action, with Rory McIlroy adding further fuel to the fire by condemning his rival's "performative" actions. The crowd were quick to poke fun at the American at the 18th green on Sunday.

‌



Spectators began booing and chanting: "He's in your head, Rory, Rory," as well as: "Where's your two shots gone?" But he showed his class after holing his par putt, taking a moment to sign a ball and glove for separate fans before removing his cap and waving farewell to the Birkdale faithful.

Marshals stationed around the green weren't happy with those taking part in the chants, with one remarking that the offending fans deserved to be ejected from the grounds. The moment DeChambeau made his way up the 18th fairway he was greeted with a thunderous reception, with both grandstands rising to applaud him and show their backing.

But certain fans shouted "cheat" at him, which had been a theme on Saturday too. McIlroy accused DeChambeau of "holding the tournament hostage" by threatening to pull out.

Tee times for Saturday were delayed while DeChambeau protested about his punishment. Spectators on Sunday were heard shouting about him during McIlroy's final round, which he completed at one-under for the tournament and nowhere near contention.

Sports.title: Stormzy leaks Manchester United's new adidas away kit during World Cup final
Sports.content:
Stormzy leaks Manchester United's new adidas away kit during World Cup final

Manchester United have already released their new home shirt for the 2026/27 Premier League campaign but the Red Devils have had their away kit leaked weeks before their first fixture

View 3 Images

Stormzy has appeared to leak Manchester United's new away kit during an appearance at the World Cup final.

‌



The Red Devils have already released their adidas home shirt for the forthcoming campaign, with supporters given their first glimpse of the new strip in the recent 1-0 defeat to Wrexham in pre-season.

‌



But the away kit remained under wraps. That was until rapper Stormzy shared snaps of the strip as he attended the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina.

‌



The rapper shared a slight teaser of the kit on his Instagram story, with supporters noticing that the Red Devils had opted for a bold blue colour with red and white trim, in what looks to be a tribute to a host of popular United kits from the 1980s.

Adidas had also opted for a classic look with their trefoil logo this time being used instead of the usual performance logo. A subtle wave pattern is also seen on the shirt.

Alongside his post, Stormzy added the caption: “@Man Utd you’ve seen it here first.” Fans were then treated to a more detailed look at the shirt on Mayowa Quadri's account as he filmed Stormzy showing off the shirt in the concourses of MetLife Stadium.

‌



Thomas Tuchel provides Kobbie Mainoo injury update after Man Utd star misses England game READ MORE :

It is not the first time that the rapper has been trusted with a few United secrets. He previously revealed that he was one of the first to learn of Paul Pogba’s record-breaking return to Old Trafford.

He said: "It was like the biggest secret on the planet at the time, and I was thinking how I could drop the bomb at any minute. Just the power of having a mad secret like that.

“It was hard to keep, a lot of my family are United fans, my little brother in particular. He was on to me like: 'Is he signing?!' I didn't tell anybody!"

Asked if he had to sign any contracts, Stormzy replied: "Yeah, secret locations and all of these things. He's a proper good guy."

Meanwhile, the rapper has previously explained exactly why he is a United fan. He said: "I always get stick.

"There's probably even people watching now saying 'hear his accent what’s he doing supporting United?' But that’s just how the stars aligned for me.

Sports.title: Boy, 13, dies as Spain's World Cup victory celebrations turn into tragedy
Sports.content:
Boy, 13, dies as Spain's World Cup victory celebrations turn into tragedy

Tragedy has befallen one area of Spain after a young boy died during the nation's World Cup celebrations, when a fountain collapsed as fans took to the streets after victory over Argentina

View 2 Images A boy died in celebrations at the Arbol Gordo fountain (Image: Google Maps)

Celebrations of Spain's World Cup win were marred as a 13-year-old boy died after a fountain collapsed in the north-west of the country. Two other young people were injured, with one child taken to the hospital with a possible broken leg, according to the BBC.

‌



Jubilant supporters were revelling in Los Rojos' extra-time victory over Argentina, as the nation enjoyed their second-ever World Cup win following Ferran Torres' extra-time strike. But tragedy struck at home when the Arbol Gordo fountain in Salamanca's Ciudad Rodrigo partially collapsed.

‌



The Ciudad Rodrigo local police, Salamanca Civil Guard, fire brigade, and Sacyl emergency medical services were called to the scene after receiving an alert in Spain past midnight. People celebrating in the fountain were injured after hundreds of thousands of fans took to the streets across Spain.

‌



The upper part of the fountain's structure is reported to have fallen onto several people, including the 13-year-old who received treatment at Ciudad Rodrigo's health centre before dying.

Mayor of Ciudad Rodrigo, Marcos Iglesias Carisaid: "I couldn't be more dismayed by this tragic news. I join in the grief of the entire family and friends over this loss. What was a day of celebration has turned into a tragedy for all of us in Ciudad de la Mirada. I hope for the swift recovery of the injured. R.I.P."

Argentina players show true colours with response to Spain lifting the World Cup READ MORE :

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni breaks down in tears during quit hint after World Cup final READ MORE :

Three days of mourning will be observed in the city. A statement read: “The City Council of Ciudad Rodrigo expresses its sorrow and condolences over the death of the 13-year-old child.

‌



“The entire city of Ciudad Rodrigo mourns this loss and stands with the child’s family and friends in their grief.

“What should have been a celebration of the Spanish national team’s victory in the World Cup has turned into a tragedy for the entire community of Ciudad Rodrigo.

View 2 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino presented the World Cup trophy to Spain captain Rodri in the US (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

‌



“The City Council also wishes a speedy recovery to the other people who were affected by the incident.

“As a sign of mourning for this loss, the City Council’s flags will fly at half-mast from July 20 to July 22.”

Local team Ciudad Rodrigo CF said: "The entire town and the club are dismayed by the news we have received on a very tough and very dark day in our history.

"We are at a loss for words on days as difficult as those that life puts in our path."
