Sports.title: Hamilton keeps F1 Belgian GP fourth-place finish as mechanic escapes unhurt
Sports.content:
The mechanic hit by Lewis Hamilton during Formula 1’s Belgian Grand Prix pitstop escaped without injury, Ferrari confirmed, with the team fined 30,000 euro for an unsafe release.

Hamilton came in under a virtual safety car on lap 20 to serve his only pitstop as well as a five-second hold for his role in the first-lap contact with George Russell.

After changing the tyres, a mechanic attempted to make a late front wing flap adjustment. But unbeknownst to the mechanic, the Briton had already been given the green light by the controller to depart from his box, leading to the mechanic being struck by the right-front of the car and falling to the ground.

Ferrari has since confirmed that the mechanic in question is doing perfectly fine and has not sustained any injuries, but Hamilton and the team still needed to visit the FIA race stewards for an alleged unsafe release.

The team has since been handed a 30,000 euro fine, 10,000 of which is suspended, with Hamilton keeping his fourth place in the result.

The FIA stewards' verdict read: "The competitor (Scuderia Ferrari HP) is fined €30,000 of which €10,000 is suspended for 12 months on condition that the competitor does not commit a similar infringement in the meantime and on the further condition that within 14 days the competitor submits a report to the FIA regarding the incident and protocols introduced to mitigate the risk of such an incident occurring in the future."

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

The stewards didn't feel a sporting penalty was warranted because Hamilton immediately stopped and actually lost time because of the incident. However, given the safety nature of the incident they still felt a fine was warranted, as well as a commitment from Ferrari to review its pit crew communication and procedures.

"The team acknowledged that for Car 44 to have been released in these circumstances was unsafe and attributed the error to an inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic’s failure to notice the green light. The team committed to undertaking a review of their pit stop procedures to ensure an incident such as this will not be repeated."

Hamilton said the incident reminded him of Kimi Raikkonen injuring one of his mechanics at the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix. "I'm looking at the lights, and I'm supposed to go when the car's dropping, and I went, and then I saw him to my right, and I stopped," he said. "All I could think at the time was back when Kimi did a leg. I'm just grateful that he didn't get hurt."

Sports.title: Ferrari criticises "mega harsh" penalty for Hamilton in F1 Belgian GP
Sports.content:
Both Lewis Hamilton and his Ferrari team boss, Frederic Vasseur, profoundly disagree with the five-second penalty he received for a collision with George Russell’s Mercedes on the opening lap of the Formula 1 Belgian Grand Prix.

"I think it's mega harsh," said Vasseur after the race. "If you have a look on the corner, Russell had enough space on the left-hand side, it's not that he was close to the wall.

"I think it's more a racing incident for me and this cost us a lot."

The contact eliminated Hamilton’s former team-mate from the race, but was fundamentally caused by the Mercedes power unit apparently suffering an electrical deployment issue through the first sector, causing Russell to lose position to both Ferraris on the run up the hill towards Les Combes.

Russell then tried to brake ultra-late on the outside line into the corner and looked as if he had reclaimed a place from Hamilton at least, only for the Ferrari’s front-left wheel to clout his sidepod and tip the Mercedes into a spin. At the time, Hamilton explained on the radio that he had "no front end" because he was in the turbulent wake of the car in front, Max Verstappen’s Red Bull.

"It was ultimately a difficult weekend," Hamilton said afterwards.

"I take all the responsibility for my incident yesterday [when he crashed in FP3], which then had a knock-on effect of the setup not being right, and then out of place in qualifying. Because I think with the setup right, I would have been probably, I think I could have been fifth or third or second.

"And then, that meant starting further back, and then I was in a position where George obviously looked like he lost power, and then he just swooped around on the outside, and we just sort of had a coming together.

"I got damaged, and then in the race, I did the best I could with the damage that I had, and then also the penalty.

"I think it was a racing incident, so I don't think there should be a penalty for that."

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Oscar Piastri, McLaren Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

Hamilton served the penalty at his first only pitstop of the race, during a virtual safety car deployment on lap 20, but he was signalled to go while a mechanic was still attempting to make a front wing adjustment. That consigned Hamilton to fourth place on the road at the chequered flag, with the Briton facing another investigation for an unsafe release.

In fact, 10 seconds is that standard penalty for "causing a collision", but the stewards decided that mitigating circumstances warranted a lesser penalty.

"Approaching Turn 5 on the opening lap, Car 63 [Russell] attempted an overtake around the outside of Car 44 [Hamilton] and had established sufficient overlap to be entitled to racing room. Car 44 remained on the inside," said the stewards’ verdict.

"During the corner, Car 44 experienced understeer and, despite attempting to avoid Car 63 by applying corrective steering, made contact with the right-hand side of Car 63 with its left-front wheel. The stewards determined that Car 63 remained with the available racing room and the the collision was caused by Car 44 being unable to maintain sufficient separation.

"The stewards recognised several mitigating circumstances. Car 44 acknowledged the presence of Car 63, attempted to leave appropriate racing room, and made a genuine attempt to avoid contact. The collision resulted from a loss of front-end grip rather than from an aggressive or deliberate manoeuvre. In addition, the incident occurred on the opening lap, where reduced grip and compressed racing conditions are recognised.

For these reasons, while Car 44 was wholly at fault for the collision, the stewards consider that a five-second time penalty, rather than the standard 10-second time penalty, is the appropriate penalty in accordance with the FIA Penalty Guidelines."

Sports.title: Why Leclerc wasn’t penalised for clash with Piastri in Belgian GP
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc avoided a penalty for a clash with Oscar Piastri during the Formula 1 Belgian Grand Prix after the stewards judged the Ferrari driver didn’t deliberately instigate the contact.

On lap eight of the Spa-Francorchamps race, Leclerc and Piastri were battling for third place down the Kemmel Straight and into Les Combes. Under braking for the corner, Leclerc defended his position forcing the McLaren driver to go around the outside, with the gap subsequently closing and causing a glancing blow, with Piastri suffering car damage.

Over the team radio, Piastri blamed Leclerc for the clash, having been forced into avoiding action for what he feared was going to be a “massive crash”, and the incident was duly investigated by the stewards.

After a review of the video and in-car footage, the stewards opted for no further action, having felt Piastri had “no possibility” of completing the overtake from his position on the outside of Leclerc and that the Ferrari driver didn’t deliberately push his rival off the track as he was on the racing line.

Leclerc was duly able to continue unaffected and profited from a timely virtual safety car to cycle into the lead. But Kimi Antonelli’s superior pace saw him reel in the Monegasque and overtake him for the win, with the Ferrari driver having to settle for second place.

“On the approach to Turn 5, Car 81 moved to overtake Car 16 on the outside,” the FIA stewards report read. “Car 81 had some overlap on Car 16 but the front axle of Car 81 was not ahead of the front axle of Car 16 and there was no possibility of Car 81 completing an overtake from that position.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

“In the stewards’ determination, Car 16 did not deliberately crowd Car 81 off the edge of the track. Car 16 followed the racing line before the entry to Turn 5 by moving slightly to the left to open up for Turn 5 and side to side contact occurred between the two cars.

“In the circumstances, the Stewards determined to take no further action.”

Earlier in the race, Leclerc’s team-mate Lewis Hamilton was given a five-second penalty for his clash with George Russell on the opening lap of the Belgian GP.

Hamilton is also under investigation for an unsafe release from a pitstop when he hit one of his Ferrari mechanics who was attempting to make a late front wing adjustment to his F1 car.

Sports.title: Ferrari summoned for Hamilton's Belgian GP unsafe release after hitting mechanic
Sports.content:
Ferrari has been summoned to visit the Formula 1 stewards' office following Lewis Hamilton's apparent unsafe release during the Belgian Grand Prix, in which he knocked down a mechanic as he left his pitbox.

In his lap 20 pitstop under the virtual safety car, Hamilton had just served a five-second penalty as the stewards deemed him to be at fault for the first-lap contact with George Russell - which led to the Mercedes driver's retirement.

All four tyres were changed on Hamilton's car, while the mechanic operating the front wing adjustment tool only attempted to make the change to the front wing angle as Hamilton was released from the box.

He was struck by the front of Hamilton's car and fell to the floor, but no injuries were reported in the incident.

Hamilton was thus left without the correct adjustments to the front wing, and he struggled with the front end of his car after switching from the medium tyre to the hard.

The car appeared to come back to him towards the end of the stint, allowing the Briton to make a move on Oscar Piastri for fourth - but it is uncertain whether he will keep the place.

Why Hamilton took a five-second penalty for Russell contact

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Sona Maleterova / Getty Images

The stewards had already decreed that Hamilton should take a five-second penalty for his clash with Russell on the opening lap, stating that there were enough mitigating circumstances to shrink this from the standard 10-second deduction for avoidable contact.

In that instance, the stewards' report read that "approaching Turn 5 on the opening lap, Car 63 attempted an overtake around the outside of Car 44 and had established sufficient overlap to be entitled to racing room. Car 44 remained on the inside.

"During the corner, Car 44 experienced understeer and, despite attempting to avoid Car 63 by applying corrective steering, made contact with the right-hand side of Car 63 with its left-front wheel. The stewards determined that Car 63 remained within the available racing room and that the collision was caused by Car 44 being unable to maintain sufficient separation.

"The stewards recognise several mitigating circumstances. Car 44 acknowledged the presence of Car 63, attempted to leave appropriate racing room and made a genuine attempt to avoid contact. The collision resulted from a loss of front-end grip rather than from an aggressive or deliberate manoeuvre. In addition, the incident occurred on the opening lap, where reduced grip and compressed racing conditions are recognised.

"For these reasons, while Car 44 was wholly at fault for the collision, the Stewards consider that a 5-second time penalty, rather than the standard 10-second time penalty, is the appropriate penalty in accordance with the FIA Penalty Guidelines."

Sports.title: F1 Belgian GP: Antonelli reels in Leclerc to win, Russell out after Hamilton clash
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli put a pass on Charles Leclerc to secure victory at the Belgian Grand Prix, as his Mercedes Formula 1 team-mate George Russell retired on the opening lap after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

Aside from the briefest of stints in the lead from fellow front-row starter Max Verstappen, who took the lead on the exit of La Source, Antonelli found his way back past on the Kemmel Straight run to ensure the lead remained in his custody in the early stages of the race.

Two laps after Antonelli had made his switch to the hard tyre, a virtual safety car was called on the 20th lap to clear debris at Blanchimont, which offered a wide enough window for Ferrari to pit both cars at a significantly cheaper cost. Leclerc, who had been behind both Antonelli and Verstappen, used this opportunity to switch to the hard tyre and cycled out ahead for the lead.

The Monegasque was able to build a lead gap once he'd cleared the off-strategy Lando Norris, who was yet to pit after starting on the hard tyre, as Antonelli also needed a few laps to clear the McLaren.

There was about three seconds between them once Norris was cleared, but Antonelli demonstrated the strong pace characteristic of his weekend and closed in on the Ferrari, helped when Leclerc was baulked by Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac through Turn 15. Antonelli broke past at Turn 5 on the following lap after stalking the Ferrari up the hill.

Leclerc stayed with Antonelli for a few tours of the Spa-Francorchamps circuit, just about holding on in overtake range, but had been unable to eke out an opportunity to return to the lead. Instead, Antonelli maintained enough pace in hand to open the gap beyond the requisite one-second barrier needed to evade a potential Leclerc fightback.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

The Italian teen continued to manage his lead, ultimately finishing 1.9s ahead of Leclerc to extend his championship lead as Russell failed to score following his first-lap contact with Hamilton's Ferrari.

Russell had been battling Leclerc through the first couple of corners. Misfortune struck when he ran out of battery half-way along the Kemmel Straight on the opening lap, which led to the Mercedes driver being swamped by the cars around him on the entry to Les Combes. He was side-by-side with Hamilton; the Ferrari driver's snap of oversteer led to contact between the two, pitching Russell into the gravel.

Verstappen finished third, albeit somewhat distant to the leading pair after being overlapped by Leclerc during the VSC pitstops. The Dutchman had put pressure on Antonelli in the opening laps, but fell back as Leclerc began to find pace ahead of the pit phase.

Hamilton took fourth, despite serving a five-second penalty for the contact with Russell. Another potential penalty looms through an unsafe release; the seven-time champion had the green signal from his pit gantry post-stop, and hadn't seen a mechanic attempting to implement a last-minute wing adjustment.

He'd passed Piastri to reach fourth, but the Australian had been able to hang onto the Ferrari's tail in the event of a penalty; Piastri had suffered contact earlier in the race with Leclerc, causing minor damage to his car which hurt his race pace.

Isack Hadjar worked his way up to sixth after using the early safety car to conduct his mandatory tyre swaps, later using the VSC to pick up a lightly used set of hard tyres in the middle of the race. Arguably, this helped the Frenchman evade a late fightback from Norris, whose alternate strategy was undone by a very slow pitstop. A slow left-rear wheel change put the Briton behind Gabriel Bortoleto on-track, but he soon passed the Brazilian for seventh.

Bortoleto finished eighth ahead of Arvid Lindblad, who at one point was investigated for potential contact with team-mate Liam Lawson, while Franco Colapinto pulled off a two-for-one move on Pierre Gasly and Lawson along the Kemmel Straight to take the final point.

Sports.title: Russell slams "dangerous" battery issue before Hamilton Belgian GP clash
Sports.content:
George Russell suffered his latest gut punch in the 2026 Formula 1 season after contact with Lewis Hamilton ended his Belgian Grand Prix on the opening lap, but he was more "angry" at the lack of battery charge that left him a sitting duck on the Kemmel straight.

Russell started third at Spa-Francorchamps, but was swallowed by the chasing pack on the long uphill blast from Raidillon to Turn 5's Les Combes.

After being easily passed by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, Russell also came under threat from Hamilton, who took the inside into the right-hander. But the Ferrari driver understeered into Russell's right rear corner to tip the Briton into the gravel and ended his race on the spot.

A frustrated Russell explained his Mercedes battery failed to recharge as he braked into the La Source hairpin at the start, which left him vulnerable to challenges from behind in the first place.

"I made a good start. I made a great first corner and I was tucked up right behind Verstappen, but for whatever reason, the battery decided not to recharge at Turn 1," Russell told media, including Autosport.

"The battery didn't charge and I exited the first corner 35% down. And because it didn't charge, I also had a boost problem. The turbo didn't sort itself out, so I had no power. I got to the top of Eau Rouge with 0% on the battery. Quite frankly, it was dangerous. I got swamped by three cars.

"I shouldn't have been in that position in the first place. That's why I'm the most angry."

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Hamilton received a five-second penalty for causing the collision, but Russell was less upset by the contact than by the power unit trouble that led up to it.

"Me and Lewis, honestly, I think it was a race incident," Russell said. "He didn't do it on purpose. He was more to blame than I was. But he didn't do anything reckless.

"That was one of those things I was most angry about, that I was in that position in the first place. I was in a great position after Turn 1. I was ready to fight the two guys ahead of me up to Turn 5. Instead, I got swamped by three drivers."

When asked by Autosport how he is dealing with his latest setback after a rollercoaster 2026 campaign thus far, he replied: "I'm numb to the disappointment now. When it happens so often, you just get used to it."

Sports.title: Hamilton says Spa practice shunt compromised his race pace | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for the victory in the Belgian Grand Prix had he not crashed in third practice.

The Ferrari driver finished fourth at Spa-Francorchamps after an eventful grand prix. He collided with George Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap, which led to Russell’s retirement and a five second penalty being handed to Hamilton, before running into a Ferrari mechanic during a pit lane mishap.

Russell admitted after the accident that he saw the clash as a racing incident that both of them had contributed to. But Hamilton apologised for his part in the collision.

“Ultimately, I’m sorry for George because that obviously ended his race,” Hamilton told the official F1 channel. “But I do agree that it was a racing incident.

“It’s not like I went in aggressive and was misplaced or anything like that. I think it was just an unfortunate scenario, which happens in racing. Then I had damage as well, so I carried that through the race. It was a tough one. I’m hugely grateful for the points given the damage and given the crash yesterday.”

Hamilton had given his Ferrari mechanics a busy few hours on Saturday afternoon after crashing his car at the exit of the Fagnes chicane at the end of the final practice session, but his SF26 had been fixed in time for him to participate in qualifying. However, Hamilton believes that accident compromised his performance for the remainder of the weekend and his final result and he could have joined team mate Charles Leclerc in fighting for victory without the crash.

“Ultimately, it was not a good weekend from my side,” he said. “I think my race pace was strong today and I think without the damage, and probably without yesterday, I think we could have been fighting for the win today.

“Even with the damage I was challenging Charles [Leclerc]. It is what is, we move on, and hope we can have a better weekend next weekend.”

Sports.title: Rise from 21st to sixth “probably my best race” – Hadjar | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar described his performance in the Belgian Grand Prix as “probably my best race” for the team.

Hadjar started all the way down in 21st position on the grid after receiving a ‘back of the grid’ penalty for multiple power unit component infringements. However, he rose up the order through the race to finish in sixth place, extending his run of top six finishes to six races.

Hadjar pitted twice under the early Safety Car to satisfy his two tyre compound requirement, then ran two long stints on hard tyres after the restart to make his way up the order. The Red Bull driver said that long runs on the hard tyre had always been the intention, heading into a weekend where he knew he would be starting down the order.

“We knew that was part of the plan, starting nearly last, and we worked on it quite a lot through the free practice sessions,” he told Sky.

“Our one-lap pace was not the target and, today, it paid off. So I’m glad we really put the work in on the long runs. I think it really helped. And moving forwards, maybe change the approach, because it worked really well.”

After rejoining the track after his final pit stop, Hadjar was around 15 seconds adrift of team mate Max Verstappen ahead, but finished the race around 12 seconds behind the multiple world champion. Hadjar says he is very satisfied with the pace he showed during the race at Spa-Francorchamps.

“I think our one-lap pace, I showed what I needed to show,” he said. “Today I think is probably my best race.

“Race pace-wise. I’m right up there with the leaders, so I’m very glad with my first ten races. To be honest, I’m really looking forward to the race, because there are a lot of things we need to tidy up as a team – in a good way. I think there’s a lot more to come.”

Sports.title: Leclerc “confident I’ve made a step forward” after back-to-back podiums | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc believes he is finding form after taking second place in the Belgian Grand Prix and fighting Andrea Kimi Antonelli for the victory.

The Ferrari driver passed Max Verstappen and George Russell on the opening lap of the race to move into second behind Antonelli, then gained the lead of the race after pitting under a Virtual Safety Car.

He would later be caught and overtaken by Antonelli, but still finished second, just under two seconds adrift of the Mercedes driver. It was Leclerc’s second consecutive podium after winning the British Grand Prix in the last round following a start to the season where he seemed unable to match the performance of team mate Lewis Hamilton.

“I’m confident in saying that I made a step forward,” Leclerc said after the race. “Whether I’m at the level where I want to perform, not yet.

“There are still things in the car that I need to drive around. I cannot drive completely naturally, and that is slowing me down in some parts of the race. So, there are still things that I’ve got to work on in order to be better. But surely it was a step forward, and for that I’m happy. I’ll continue with the one-race-at-a-time approach because, with these cars, it’s very difficult to be confident that if one race weekend goes well, the other one will, because it relies on such small details. With what you do with your driving, it’s never a given that you get the same deployment from one lap to the other, and that’s maybe the frustrating bit about these cars.”

Leclerc admitted at the start of the weekend he expected to be “very far back, maybe to the extent of four or five tenths” a lap around Spa-Francorchamps.

“In qualifying, that was true, but in the race we were a bit closer than we thought,” Leclerc said. “So, it’s been positive.

“I think on two tracks which, on paper, were quite bad for us, we won and we finished second, with a little bit of luck, but still, I think it was a good effort from the team. On two tracks that didn’t fit our car particularly well, we’ve scored good points.”

Asked if he believed he could carry this momentum into next weekend’s race at the Hungaroring and be in contention for victory once more, Leclerc says it’s to difficult to be sure how good his team will be heading into any given weekend.

“We could be, but we could also not be, and we’ll never know until we go there,” he said. “I think it’s very difficult to predict the level of performance of every team.

“I recall very well what the overall feeling was before Monaco, and we arrived in Monaco and were under-performing compared to what everybody thought we would. So, I think we need to be cautious. We just need to do our homework, just like we do at every different track. I think what we did particularly well over these last two weekends was to really make sure that we maximised our package, and that’s the mentality we should keep for Budapest, without thinking about expectations.”

Sports.title: Wolff says Russell not alone in Mercedes power woes, was “team mistake” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff claims all Mercedes-powered cars were down on power during the Belgian Grand Prix.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli won the race for Mercedes, but team mate George Russell crashed out on the opening lap after contact with Lewis Hamilton at Les Combes.

Russell later said that while he felt the contact with the Ferrari driver was a racing incident, he implied that a battery deployment problem – which he had been complaining had been affecting his straight-line performance all weekend at Spa-Francorchamps – was more responsible for causing the clash. Wolff accepted that a power unit deployment problem had been a contributing factor.

“I think there’s two situations here,” he told Sky after the race. “First, the racing accident – that happened. Unfortunately, for us, we lost a lot of constructors points and, George, a lot of drivers’ points.

“George tried on the outside, braked late, and that corner should have been his, but it was a racing incident. These things can happen, whether you’re at the front, in the middle, or at the back of the pack. George had a tough weekend. Probably half of that can be attributed to the power unit, which wasn’t as good as it should have been in his car, and the other half perhaps to the driving.

“But we’re in this together. We all make mistakes. Today it was a team mistake on another day it’ll be a driver’s mistake. We just need to minimise those mistakes and support each other.”

Wolff says that Russell was not the only Mercedes-powered driver who was experiencing lower than expected power deployment during the Belgian Grand Prix.

“We had an issue on all Mercedes engines that we lacked the power out on the straights,” he admitted. “That bit him [Russell] badly and it goes one-hundred-percent on us.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We’re trying our best as a team. We have the most powerful power unit – we have a strong car that is capable of winning. Everybody gives their maximum to minimise their mistakes and still it happens – because we are humans at work. We let Kimi down at Silverstone where George got a podium – that was maybe better than the result should have been – one driver DNF’d in Canada, the other DNF’d in Barcelona. That’s a little bit the story of our season, here. It’s a technical sport, it’s a mechanical sport.

“I’m proud to be a part of the organisation at HPP and Mercedes Grand Prix. Those groups of people give it all they have and we came out with a product this year that is so strong and I’d rather fix the reliability than try to accelerate a slow engine or a slow car. We’re giving it one-hundred-percent and we need to give it one-hundred-percent, because we have lost a lot of points through reliability. We should be much further ahead than we are.”

Russell had been slower than than Antonelli throughout the weekend. Wolff suggested that Antonelli may have learned how to maximise the performance from the new-generation power units for 2026 compared to his more experienced team mate.

“I think, first of all, it’s very different and I think this is probably an advantage that Kimi has, because it reset for everyone,” he said.

“Then the components of energy harvesting and energy deployment plays a role. Even the way you go on the throttle – whether you give it full throttle or half throttle and when you lift off – can have consequences in terms of the energy delivery. And that’s another dimension that has been handed to the driving – some drivers may not like it, others may say ‘okay, we just need to get used to it’. But it’s another component that makes it more complex.”

Wolff said he would talk to Russell to console him following his latest setback in the championship, which has seen him drop to third in the standings behind Hamilton.

“I haven’t seen him yet, but it’s completely understandable that the moment you’re out of this race it’s so frustrating and the emotions boil. That’s why I completely understand. He has our one-hundred-percent support. We are trying to solve all the issues, he’s doing everything he can to get on top of his driving. So I haven’t spoken to him, but I’m going to try and put my arms around him.”

Sports.title: Antonelli passes Leclerc to win Belgian GP, Russell out after Hamilton clash | 2026 Belgian Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the world championship to 45 points after winning the Belgian Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver had led early on after starting from pole, but a Virtual Safety Car had allowed Charles Leclerc to take the lead in the pit cycle.

Eventually, Antonelli was able to chase down the Ferrari and pass for the lead with 11 laps to go. Max Verstappen completed the podium in third.

At the start, pole winner Antonelli held the lead into La Source, but Verstappen in second managed to get ahead of the Mercedes into Eau Rouge. Verstappen’s time in the lead was shortlived, however, as Antonelli passed the Red Bull back down the Kemmel Straight, with Leclerc also following through into second place.

Behind, a three-way fight for fourth between George Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Oscar Piastri ended in tears when Russell and Hamilton collided through Les Combes, sending the Mercedes spinning into the gravel trap and out of the race. Hamilton was able to continue, but was later handed a five second time penalty for being deemed responsible for the collision.

After a Safety Car to recover Russell’s car, the race resumed on lap five with Antonelli leading from Leclerc and Verstappen. Antonelli headed the field until a brief Virtual Safety Car on lap 18 to clear debris, which turned green by the time Antonelli had pitted for Hard tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Leclerc remained out a handful more laps than Antonelli, until a second debris-related VSC was triggered on lap 20. This allowed Ferrari to pit both Leclerc and Hamilton, to serve his penalty, and enabled Leclerc to rejoin the circuit still under VSC ahead of Antonelli, taking what was effectively the lead of the race.

After Lando Norris pitted, Leclerc took the overall race lead, but Antonelli began to slowly reel him in. Eventually, on lap 34, Antonelli tucked up behind the Ferrari along the Kemmel Straight and overtook Leclerc to take the lead.

While Leclerc tried his best to remain in touch with with the championship leader, Antonelli was able to keep ahead of the Ferrari until the chequered flag, heading him by just under two seconds. Verstappen was around ten seconds behind the pair in third, with Hamilton taking fourth place after passing Piastri in the later laps.

Isack Hadjar moved from 21st on the grid to finish sixth, ahead of Lando Norris, Gabriel Bortoleto and Arvid Lindblad. Franco Colapinto took the final point in tenth for Alpine, ahead of team mate Pierre Gasly.

Hamilton will be investigated after the race for an unsafe pit release after one of the Ferrari mechanics was struck by his right-front wheel as he was released from his pit stop. Ferrari confirmed to Hamilton over team radio that the mechanic involved was unhurt.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn: Boots Ennis Is ‘King Of The Castle’
Sports.content:
Hearn says his fighter is no longer in the position of making concessions to land the bout. Boots is now “king of the castle.”

“He was taking the smaller side of the piece last time. He was going to be the B-side. He agreed to everything that they wanted to get that opportunity. So you imagine how he feels now that he’s king of the castle,” said Hearn to the media about Ennis’ position in negotiations with Vergil Ortiz Jr. “Vergil doesn’t have anything Boots wants other than a big fight and a big payday. What does Boots want to do now? He wants to unify.” “I don’t rule out that Ortiz fight at all. One thing is for sure. He ain’t close at all at the moment.“

Hearn’s comments reflect how much Ennis’ position has changed over the past year. During earlier discussions, Ennis was still chasing the biggest opportunities and was willing to accept B-side status to secure a fight with Ortiz. Hearn says those circumstances no longer exist.

Ennis now holds two world titles and has shifted his attention toward becoming the undisputed champion. Hearn indicated that unification bouts remain the priority, but he left the door open for Ortiz if Golden Boy presents an offer that outweighs Ennis’ other options.

“Tell us what the money is. And I’ll go to Jaron, and I’ll say, ‘We got Kelly, Fundora, or Ortiz,'” said Hearn.

Unless Turki Alalshikh gets involved, it’s questionable if a fight with Ortiz Jr. is financially appealing enough for Ennis to take time off from pursuing his goal of becoming the undisputed champion at junior middleweight.

Josh Kelly and Sebastian Fundora remain among the names under consideration, with Hearn making it clear that every possibility will be evaluated before Ennis decides on his next opponent.

A fight is still available for Vergil Jr, but Hearn believes the balance of power has moved. Rather than Ennis pursuing Ortiz Jr. at any cost, Golden Boy must now convince the unified champion that the financial package is worth delaying his pursuit of the remaining 154-lb titles.

Sports.title: Vernon Forrest Silences Shane Mosley Again
Sports.content:
The rematch carried enormous significance. Forrest defended both the WBC and Ring Magazine welterweight championships after taking them from Mosley in their first meeting earlier in the year in January 2002. Many believed Mosley would make the necessary adjustments and reclaim the titles, while Forrest had the opportunity to prove the upset had not been a one-night performance.

The event attracted 15,775 fans, the largest crowd to attend a boxing card in Indiana history at the time. HBO televised the championship bout nationally, and both fighters earned career-high paydays. Forrest received $3.42 million, while Mosley collected $2.8 million. Veteran referee Laurence Cole officiated the 12-round title fight.

Mosley came out aggressively, looking to erase the disappointment of the first bout by forcing exchanges from the opening bell. Forrest refused to be drawn into a firefight. Standing three inches taller with the longer reach, he established his jab early, circled effectively and answered Mosley’s rushes with sharp counters before tying him up whenever the action moved inside.

As the rounds progressed, Forrest steadily took control. Forrest repeatedly stabbed Mosley with the jab before tying him up whenever the challenger got close, forcing Mosley to reset his offense over and over. Referee Laurence Cole was forced to separate the fighters throughout the contest as the tactical battle became increasingly physical.

The middle rounds lacked sustained action, drawing boos from portions of the crowd, but Forrest remained committed to the game plan. One report even noted that a fight in the stands during the sixth round briefly attracted as much attention as the action inside the ring.

Mosley increased the pressure during the championship rounds, finally producing several spirited exchanges in the tenth. Forrest answered with crisp counterpunching and finished strongly, landing several hard right hands late in the eleventh before boxing confidently through the final round. There were no knockdowns, but Forrest consistently landed the cleaner, more effective punches.

CompuBox statistics reflected the tactical nature of the contest. Forrest landed 120 of 446 punches, while Mosley connected on 114 of 259, with Forrest’s jab, timing and ring control outweighing Mosley’s higher connect percentage.

Judges Gary Merritt (117-111), Tony Castellano (116-112) and Jerry Roth (115-113) all favored Forrest. HBO unofficial scorer Harold Lederman and several media scorecards also had Forrest winning, confirming that his first victory had been no accident.

The rematch closed the book on one of the era’s most compelling rivalries. Forrest had defeated Mosley twice as a professional after also beating him during the 1992 U.S. Olympic Trials, establishing a rare mastery over one of boxing’s greatest fighters.

Mosley later captured world titles in higher weight classes, while Forrest continued his championship run before unifying the welterweight division. More than two decades later, the rematch remains one of the signature victories of Forrest’s Hall of Fame career, removing any doubt that his success against Mosley was built on superior technique rather than surprise.

Sports.title: Shakur: Zuffa Promised Haney And Tank Davis Fights
Sports.content:
Even under the best circumstances, it’s not a given that Zuffa will be able to hook a big fish like Gervonta Davis to fight Shakur. Despite Shakur’s elite skills and massive new Zuffa backing, he simply doesn’t move the needle the same way with the casual audience.

If Shakur demands anything close to parity or tries to dictate the terms, Tank will likely dig his heels in. Tank has shown before that he would rather sit out, pursue a lesser name, or even talk about walking away from the sport entirely than give up his leverage to an opponent he feels needs him more than he needs them.

“What really went into the decision was mainly life-changing money. Not only life-changing money, just life-changing opportunities,” Shakur said to Fighthype. “Dana [White] and Nick [Khan], they kept saying, ‘We want to get you in with the best fighters. We wanted you to fight the best.’ The guys that they mentioned was Devin and Tank. And when I heard that, I’m like, why would I go away from what I’ve been wanting to do my whole career? I think my whole career I’ve been saying the titles and all that, I done it. With all due respect to the titles, I appreciate y’all… but I want to fight the best. I want to get in there and prove myself and get under them bright lights and see who’s the best. I’m not scared of taking no risk.”

Haney hasn’t said whether he’s going to fight Shakur next or defend against his WBO mandatory, Keyshawn Davis. If Keyshawn actually upsets Haney to take the WBO welterweight title, Shakur’s biggest potential fight is effectively dead.

“I think that’s what really kind of kicked it off with me and Zuffa. Their vision is as big as mine. I ain’t never really hear promoters with big visions like me. It’s an amazing thing, and I’m happy to be the person to lead the new school and new generation,” Shakur said.

With Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn officially locked in for September 12, a Ryan loss changes everything for the 147-pound division. Ryan is arguably the sport’s biggest ticket seller and pay-per-view draw outside of Canelo. Shakur vs. Ryan is a massive financial fallback if Tank or Haney fall through. If Benn beats Ryan, that golden parachute disappears.

While a Benn victory makes Conor a massive star under the Zuffa banner, a Shakur vs. Benn fight doesn’t carry the same casual fan appeal or domestic PPV weight as a clash with Garcia. Benn doesn’t have the same popularity in the U.S as he does in the UK. American fans view Benn as the son of a famous retired ex-world champion, who has never beaten any elite-level fighters during his career.

Sports.title: Mike McCallum Stunned Donald Curry In Classic Title Fight
Sports.content:
The scheduled 15-round championship bout was televised by HBO from the Caesars Palace Sports Pavilion in Paradise, Nevada. Richard Steele served as referee, while Guy Jutras, Jerry Roth and Ove Ovesen handled the scoring. An official attendance figure was never widely reported, but the event drew major attention as one of the biggest championship fights of 1987.

McCallum was making the sixth defense of the WBA junior middleweight title he had won in 1984. Nicknamed “The Body Snatcher,” the Jamaican-born master tactician had knocked out every opponent during his title reign. Even with those accomplishments, sportsbooks installed him as a 2-1 underdog.

Curry entered as the WBA’s top contender after previously holding the WBA, WBC, IBF and Ring Magazine welterweight championships. Moving to 154 pounds offered a fresh opportunity to reestablish himself among boxing’s elite and position himself for even bigger fights.

The fight also carried significant financial rewards. McCallum earned a reported $475,000, while Curry received $425,000, excellent purses for championship fighters during that era.

For four rounds, the betting odds appeared justified. Curry’s jab repeatedly beat McCallum to the target. His hand speed, combinations and movement kept the champion from settling into his rhythm, and a sharp right hand in the second round buckled McCallum’s knees. By the end of the fourth, Curry had built a comfortable lead on all three scorecards. McCallum remained dangerous, but he looked a step behind as Curry controlled the action.

At 1:14 into Round 5, Curry stepped inside and drove a right hand toward McCallum’s body. McCallum anticipated the attack, gave a subtle body feint of his own, then unleashed a crushing left hook that landed flush on Curry’s jaw. The fight ended instantly.

Curry crashed flat onto his back, staring toward the lights as Steele began the count. He slowly regained awareness around seven but never gathered himself in time to continue. The referee completed the count, and McCallum had retained his championship with one of boxing’s most unforgettable single punches.

The knockout earned KO Magazine’s Knockout of the Year honors and remains one of the finest one-punch finishes ever shown on HBO. Ironically, Sugar Ray Leonard worked the broadcast that night after Curry had reportedly objected to his presence on the telecast, which brought an extra bit of drama to an already memorable evening.

McCallum later vacated the WBA title to pursue championships at middleweight and light heavyweight, eventually becoming a three-division world champion and earning induction into the International Boxing Hall of Fame. Although he never landed the marquee fights against Sugar Ray Leonard, Marvin Hagler, Thomas Hearns or Roberto Durán, his body of work cemented his reputation as one of boxing’s most accomplished champions.

The defeat for Curry proved far more damaging than anyone expected. He won a handful of fights afterward but never returned to the level that once made him one of the sport’s pound-for-pound stars, suffering later defeats to Michael Nunn and Terry Norris before retiring.

More than three decades later, McCallum’s left hook remains one of the greatest one-punch knockouts in championship boxing history and the defining moment of an unforgettable title fight.

Sports.title: Is Eddie Hearn Protecting Diego Pacheco?
Sports.content:
If Aleem was able to land that frequently, what happens against Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez or even middleweights Carlos Adames or Yoenli Hernandez if they moved up? Those fighters carry more power, are physically stronger, and wouldn’t be as forgiving once Pacheco found himself exchanging at close range.

The Kevin Lele Sadjo fight exposed flaws in Pacheco when the action became physical. He didn’t look comfortable under sustained pressure, and those issues weren’t answered against Aleem because the matchup never forced him into the same type of fight.

Pacheco’s post-fight comments focused on Canelo Alvarez and Jaime Munguia. Eddie Hearn has also floated Munguia as a possible next opponent. If Matchroom wants to prove Pacheco belongs with the division’s elite, fights against Iglesias, Lester, Adames or Hernandez would answer far more questions than a quick jump toward a lucrative name.

Hearn has the financial backing to make those fights. If Matchroom bypasses them and heads straight toward Munguia, it will be difficult to ignore the possibility that the priority is maximizing Pacheco’s value before a dangerous contender exposes the flaws that are still visible in his game.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Calls MSG Fight “Storybook” As Questions Follow Zuffa Debut
Sports.content:
Saturday’s main event is a 10-round showcase against Steven Butler, a fringe contender with five defeats who has come up short in his biggest opportunities. Berlanga also enters the fight after losing two of his last three bouts, including a knockout defeat to Hamzah Sheeraz, followed by a year away from the ring.

That leaves little margin for error in his first appearance under the Zuffa banner. An impressive win would give Dana and Zuffa a platform to match Berlanga against recognizable names at 168 or 160 pounds. A poor performance, or an upset loss, would make that job far more difficult.

Ticket demand has also become part of the conversation. The BoxingTickets account on X claimed Zuffa removed roughly half of the remaining inventory for the event before increasing prices on the seats still available, describing the move as “gimmicking the ticket sales.”

Zuffa has not commented publicly on the ticket changes. With the promotion investing heavily in Berlanga as one of its first headline attractions, Saturday’s fight carries importance well beyond the result inside the ring.

Sports.title: Mystery Title For Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn
Sports.content:
The promotion has repeatedly discussed its long-term goal of operating with one champion per weight class. If that plan begins in September, Garcia-Benn would be a logical stage for introducing a Zuffa world welterweight title.

Instead of advertising the fight as the WBC World Welterweight Championship, Zuffa chose far more general language.

Several outcomes remain possible. Ryan may simply enter the ring carrying the WBC belt as champion, with Zuffa avoiding sanctioning-body branding in its own promotional material. Another scenario is that the company reveals its own championship belt during fight week or on the night of the event, making the winner the first Zuffa welterweight champion.

A third possibility is that both titles are recognized, with Garcia entering as WBC champion while the victor also receives a Zuffa championship belt.

None of those outcomes has been confirmed. The poster itself offers no explanation beyond the phrase “World Welterweight Championship.”

For a promotion launching what it has billed as a new era in boxing, the lack of specificity is difficult to ignore. Identifying the fight as a WBC title bout would have been easy. Choosing broader language instead has shifted attention toward what Zuffa plans to place in the ring when Ryan and Benn are introduced.

Zuffa may answer that question during fight week or wait until the championship presentation on September 12. Until then, the identity of the title being contested remains one of the biggest unanswered questions surrounding the event.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Wants Artur Beterbiev Trilogy, Says Eddie Hearn
Sports.content:
“There’s a lot of people saying, ‘Bivol doesn’t want to fight Beterbiev.’ That’s not true at all,” Hearn told Fighthype. “Dmitry wants the trilogy. That’s the fight he wants. We’ll start those conversations and see what happens.”

Hearn’s comments follow questions about Bivol’s next move after his recovery from elbow surgery. The trilogy remains Bivol’s preferred destination. The WBO has ordered him to defend against Callum Smith, creating uncertainty over the title picture if the Beterbiev fight cannot be finalized immediately.

Bivol relinquished the WBC light heavyweight title on April 7, 2025, after choosing the Beterbiev trilogy over a mandatory defense against David Benavidez.

Hearn believes Smith will stay active instead of waiting indefinitely.

“I think Callum Smith will probably end up boxing Joshua Buatsi for the vacant world title if that’s the route it goes,” Hearn said. “We’ll see how everything plays out, but Dmitry wants the Beterbiev fight.”

A Bivol-Beterbiev trilogy would complete one of boxing’s best recent rivalries after the two split their first two meetings. If the trilogy cannot be finalized, Smith and Buatsi could meet for the vacant WBO world title while Bivol continues pursuing Beterbiev.

Ghana News.title: Rumzia Sule crowned Miss Ghana 2026
Ghana News.content:
An International Relations student at Cumbria University, Rumzia Sule, has been officially crowned Miss Ghana 2026, emerging victorious over 12 other contestants to claim the coveted national title.

The grand finale of the 69th edition, held under the theme “Empowering Women, Enduring Legacy,” saw the University of Ghana graduate Fatimatu Zara Ishacufinish as the first runner-up and Whitney Opoku Nketia was adjudged the second runner-up. Anita Dankwa and Nedlyn Appiah won 3rd and 4th runners-up respectively.

Other awards, such as Miss Fitness, Miss Talent, Miss Eloquent, Most Beautiful Skin, Miss Congeniality, Most Disciplined, and Miss Photogenic, went to NedlynAppiah, Lucille Akua Oputa-Otutu, Davinia Owusu Kuffuor, Lawrencia Serwaa Amankwa, Fatimatu Zara Ishacu, Anita Appiah, and Whitney Opoku Nketia, in that order. Rumzia also won the Beauty with The Purpose award.

Unlike previous editions, this year’s pageant adopted a strategic, scaled-down format. Shifting away from traditional pomp and pageantry, to a more personal and community skills development theme. The final selection was held at the Oak Plaza Hotel in Accra before an elite panel of judges, relatives of contestants amongst others present to witness the historic occasion.

According to the organisers, Exclusive Events Ghana and the Miss Ghana Foundation, the format change was a deliberate choice, as part of preparations towards the upcoming milestone for the brand both nationally and internationally ie next year’s landmark 70th, in Ghana and this year's 75th Anniversaries, internationally.

"We made a deliberate choice this year," stated the organisers. "We did not want to be only entertainment focused but more of the personal and corporate development skills. This platform has always been, and will always be, about beauty with a purpose, tangible impact, and an enduring legacy. This crown is not simply an honour; it is a profound responsibility."

Despite the cozy setting of the coronation, the finalists underwent the full, rigorous pageant journey following nationwide auditions on June 27, 2026. The young women participated in intensive, weeks-long mentorship, leadership, and entrepreneurship program designed to test their resilience, empathy, discipline, and professionalism.

The comprehensive training curriculum included: Financial Literacy & Sustainability: Facilitated by Fidelity Bank, Identity, Poise, and Leadership: Coached by Ivana Annan, Chief Executive Officer of Ivana Couture, Personal Branding & Media Excellence: Led by Dr Ike Tandoh (Founder & CEO of 1PR Communications and Dean of Students at UniMAC-GIJ) at the Honeysuckle Restaurant in Labone, Movement & Flexibility: Taught by Dr Terry Bright Kweku Ofosu, Head of the Department of Dance Studies at the University of Ghana’s School of Performing Arts and the 1989 Ghana National Dance Champion, Fitness & Mental Well-being: By Philippa Pepera, the Director at Pippa’s Health Centre, Etiquette,and Personal Development with Jennifer Agyemang, Founder of Amazing U.

To further inspire the contestants, the cohort toured the Despite Automobile Museum in East Legon, learning from the remarkable entrepreneurial journey of businessman Dr Osei Kwame Despite to reinforce resilience in the face of challenges.

True to the pageant’s core mission, these lessons were translated into nationwide social intervention projects. Through the Miss Ghana Foundation’s Beauty with a Purpose initiative, the contestants led a youth mentorship program at Martey Tsuru Presbyterian JHS in Accra, impacting over 300 pupils with sessions on patriotism, civic responsibility, and resilience.

Furthermore, the contestants demonstrated their commitment to national development by rolling up their sleeves for the National Clean-Up Exercise, supporting President John Dramani Mahama’s call to restore cleanliness across Ghana by desilting choked gutters in parts of Accra. The Foundation emphasised that these outreach programs were vital evaluation tools used to identify a queen who genuinely embodies compassion and a willingness to serve society beyond the glamour of the stage.

The outcome was determined by a combination of the preliminary journey, which accounted for a massive 80% of the total score, and the public vote, which made up the remaining 20%. However, organisers indicated that a key turning point was the final presentations, where each finalist took the stage one last time to pitch her 12-month vision for driving social impact through the Miss Ghana Foundation. Rumzia’s exceptional public speaking and commanding vision ultimately separated her from the field.

As the newly minted Miss Ghana 2026, Rumzia will now begin preparations to represent the nation on the international stage at the upcoming Miss World pageant in Vietnam.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi conviction: Ken Ashigbey commends Erastus Asare Donkor, urges wider probe into illegal mining networks
Ghana News.content:
Convener of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining, Dr Ken Ashigbey, has praised JoyNews' Erastus Asare Donkor for his persistent reporting on illegal mining, calling on the government to expand investigations into all individuals and networks implicated in the destructive practice.

Speaking on JoyNews following the conviction and sentencing of New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, Mr Ashigbey said the judgment should embolden authorities to pursue all alleged galamsey kingpins instead of treating it as an isolated case.

He singled out Erastus Asare Donkor for his investigative work, particularly his reports on the alleged involvement of Akonta Mining in illegal mining activities within the Tano River Forest Reserve.

"It was Erastus' report on Akonta Mining being involved in galamsey in the Tano River Forest Reserve, the evidence he gathered, the concessions involved and the impact on the Tano River. Erastus needs to be commended. He continues to be one of the main voices exposing illegal mining," he said.

The Media Coalition convener said recent investigations and official reports have uncovered several outstanding allegations that require urgent action from law enforcement agencies.

He cited the Prof. Kwabena Frimpong-Boateng report, investigations commissioned by the Attorney General, and allegations involving politically exposed persons, arguing that the fight against illegal mining would only succeed if authorities pursue everyone implicated, irrespective of political affiliation.

Mr Ashigbey also referenced recent reports of illegal mining activities in the Bebiani area, alleging that some individuals continue to operate without the required licences.

He disclosed that he had personally confirmed with the Minerals Commission that no licence had been issued for mining in wetlands in the area, describing such operations as "a walking illegality."

He further questioned why district chief executives, municipal chief executives, police commanders and other local authorities have failed to clamp down on illegal mining taking place openly in forest reserves and along major roads.

"Are they waiting for the Minister for Lands to come from Accra, or the President or the Inspector General of Police before they act? If they are not complicit, then they are incompetent and should be fired," he said.

Mr Ashigbey urged President John Mahama to use "Wontumi's conviction as an opportunity to launch a broader offensive against illegal mining syndicates", insisting that only the prosecution of the financiers and masterminds behind the practice would deter others.

He also appealed to media organisations to intensify investigative reporting on illegal mining to sustain public pressure for accountability and ensure that all those involved are brought to justice.

His comments follow the Accra High Court's sentencing of Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

Ghana News.title: DTI calls on youth to embrace AI and future-ready skills at Jobs & Opportunities Fair
Ghana News.content:
The Founder and President of the Design and Technology Institute (DTI), Constance Swaniker, has urged young people to embrace artificial intelligence (AI), strengthen their technical competencies and develop entrepreneurial mindsets to remain competitive in the evolving world of work.

Speaking at the 2026 DTI Jobs & Opportunities Fair in Accra, Ms. Swaniker said Africa's greatest challenge is not the rise of automation but the failure to adequately prepare young people for emerging opportunities in an AI-driven economy.

The event, held under the theme "Navigating Skills, Careers and the Future of Work: Preparing Young People to Thrive in an AI-Enabled World," brought together academia, industry leaders, employers, entrepreneurs, policymakers, development partners and hundreds of young people.

According to Ms. Swaniker, the Fair serves as a platform to connect young people with employment, entrepreneurship and career opportunities through stronger collaboration between educators, employers and innovators.

"We do not train young people for the economy we wish existed. We train them for the economy that exists today and for the one that is emerging," she said.

She cited projections by the World Economic Forum, which indicate that while AI and automation could displace about 85 million jobs globally by 2030, they are expected to create 97 million new roles, making continuous learning and upskilling critical.

Ms. Swaniker also highlighted Ghana's youth unemployment challenge, noting that the Ghana Statistical Service estimates unemployment among persons aged 15 to 24 at 32.5 percent, with more than 1.3 million young Ghanaians currently not in employment, education or training.

She revealed that since its establishment in 2016, DTI has contributed to more than 41,000 employment and entrepreneurship opportunities across the country through its industry-driven training programmes.

Representing the Commission for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (CTVET), Deputy Director-General Anthony Kwame Seyram Zu reaffirmed the Commission's commitment to promoting skills development, innovation and artificial intelligence as part of Ghana's TVET transformation agenda.

He commended DTI for its demand-driven approach to technical and vocational education and assured the Institute of CTVET's continued support in strengthening workforce competitiveness.

Meanwhile, Chief Executive Officer of the Knowledge Web Centre and Lead Consultant for the AI Africa Project, Dr. David King Boison, encouraged young people to see artificial intelligence as an enabler rather than a threat.

"Artificial intelligence will not take your job. But a person who knows how to use it might," he stated.

Dr. Boison noted that professions such as welding, fabrication, manufacturing and design will become even more valuable when combined with AI and digital technologies.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s economy remains resilient despite global uncertainty – Dr Asiama
Ghana News.content:
Dr Johnson Asiama, BoG Governor

The Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Johnson Asiama, says Ghana's economy continues to demonstrate resilience despite growing uncertainty in the global economy, supported by stronger economic growth, rising private sector credit and a stable banking sector.

Opening the 131st Monetary Policy Committee meeting in Accra, Dr. Asiama said the domestic economy has remained robust even as policymakers closely monitor inflationary pressures and external risks.

He disclosed that Ghana's economy expanded by 6.4 percent in the first quarter of the year, compared with 6.2 percent during the same period last year, while the GDP deflator eased to 4.1 percent.

"Growth has held up quite well and this trend is expected to continue," he said.

The Governor also highlighted a sharp recovery in private sector lending.

"Real private sector credit has accelerated to 34.1 percent against a 4.5 percent contraction a year ago. This largely reflects the easing in domestic credit conditions associated with the disinflation process."

Dr. Asiama further noted that the exchange rate has remained broadly stable during the first half of July, while the banking sector continues to be well-capitalised.

"The exchange rate has remained broadly stable through the first half of July and the banking system remains sound and well capitalised."

However, he cautioned that risks remain, particularly in the banking sector, where non-performing loans are still elevated.

"The still elevated non-performing loan ratio indicates that credit risk has not yet been fully worked through the system."

He said the Monetary Policy Committee will carefully assess these domestic developments alongside external risks before determining the appropriate monetary policy stance at the conclusion of its meeting.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi should have received maximum 25-year sentence — Ken Ashigbey
Ghana News.content:
Convener of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining, Dr Kenneth Ashigbey, has said he would have preferred the Accra High Court to impose the maximum custodial sentence of 25 years on Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, insisting that those who finance and facilitate illegal mining deserve the harshest punishment available under the law.

Speaking on JoyNews on Monday, July 20, shortly after the Criminal Division of the Accra High Court sentenced Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region, Dr Ashigbey welcomed the verdict as a major milestone in Ghana's fight against galamsey but argued that the sentence should have been even more severe.

Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay, who presided over the case, sentenced Chairman Wontumi to two concurrent 20-year prison terms after finding him guilty on charges related to illegal mining.

The court also imposed a fine of 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000, with a default custodial sentence should the fine remain unpaid.

Reacting to the judgment, Dr Ashigbey said the punishment, though significant, fell short of what he believed was necessary to deter influential financiers of illegal mining.

"I would have wished that the judge would have given the maximum sentence of 25 years, and also added the maximum fine," he stated.

He explained that Ghana's mining laws empower the courts to impose fines, custodial sentences or both, and argued that cases involving politically exposed persons who profit from illegal mining should attract the most severe sanctions because of the enormous damage caused to the country.

"The law talks about either the fine or the custodial sentence or both," he noted, adding that judges should not hesitate to apply the toughest penalties where the evidence justifies such punishment.

Despite his call for a stiffer sentence, Dr Ashigbey described the conviction as a historic victory for Ghana and for organisations that have spent years campaigning against illegal mining.

"This is a good day for Ghana. This is a good day for the Media Coalition Against Galamsey and the Coalition Against Galamsey in Ghana, and for all who want to see the back of this existential threat that confronts all of us as citizens," he declared.

He disclosed that the Samreboi prosecution originated from a petition submitted by the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining to the then Attorney-General and the then Inspector-General of Police.

According to him, he personally joined private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu and two other campaigners in petitioning the authorities and had followed the case from its inception until judgment.

"This is one case that the coalition petitioned. The then Attorney-General, the then IGP and personally myself, Martin Kpebu and two others also petitioned. We've been following it all this while," he said.

Dr Ashigbey praised the current Attorney-General for ensuring that the prosecution was pursued to its conclusion and commended Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay for what he described as demonstrating courage in delivering judgment in one of Ghana's most closely watched illegal mining cases.

"I think we need to commend the Attorney-General for seeing this case through. We also need to commend the judge who sat on this case for demonstrating courage," he remarked.

READ ALSO: Chairman Wontumi sentenced to 20 years in prison

He also acknowledged the role played by the current Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, recalling that during the Easter holidays in 2025 the minister urgently convened a press conference after reviewing the coalition's petition and conducting investigations into the allegations.

Dr Ashigbey further commended the former Minister for Lands and Natural Resources for publicly declaring that Akonta Mining Company Limited had engaged in illegal mining within the Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve.

He said the then Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Martin Ayisi, subsequently confirmed the findings, but lamented that the Attorney-General and police prosecutors at the time did not proceed with criminal prosecution.

"We kept pushing. It just tells you that if the media continue pushing these issues, we can get somewhere," he observed.

Although he welcomed the conviction of Chairman Wontumi, Dr Ashigbey stressed that the judgment should not mark the end of Ghana's campaign against illegal mining.

He questioned the status of investigations involving other politically exposed persons allegedly implicated in galamsey and urged the authorities to pursue all outstanding cases without fear or favour.

"It is great that we are dealing with one campaigner, but what has happened to the other politically exposed persons who were named?" he asked.

He referred to previous allegations involving some Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives, traditional authorities and Members of Parliament, arguing that accountability must extend to every individual involved regardless of political affiliation or social standing.

"There are several politically exposed persons involved in galamsey. There are MMDCEs demonstrating either complicity or incompetence. There are chiefs who have publicly been accused of involvement. This is just the beginning."

According to him, Ghana would only succeed in eradicating illegal mining if influential individuals who finance and facilitate the practice are prosecuted alongside those directly engaged in mining activities.

Dr Ashigbey defended his call for the maximum sentence by describing the consequences of illegal mining as comparable to crimes that directly result in loss of life.

"The reason why we need to be drastic in sentencing the big financiers involved in galamsey is that what they do is mass murder," he asserted.

"If anybody had taken a gun and shot somebody, we would all be asking for the maximum sentence. These people are causing deaths through environmental destruction."

He argued that illegal mining contributes to flooding, citing the recent flooding in Samreboi as an example of the environmental consequences associated with widespread degradation of forest reserves and river systems.

He also linked galamsey to serious public health concerns, including kidney disease, renal complications, birth deformities and stillbirths, which he said result from pollution of water bodies and environmental contamination.

Beyond its health implications, Dr Ashigbey warned that illegal mining continues to threaten Ghana's economy by contaminating cocoa farms and other agricultural lands with heavy metals, thereby undermining the country's agricultural exports and food security.

Describing financiers of illegal mining as "economic saboteurs" and "nation wreckers", he insisted that the courts must continue imposing severe penalties on offenders to deter others.

"These nation wreckers are to be punished," he concluded.

Convener of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining, Dr Kenneth Ashigbey, has described the conviction and sentencing of Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, as a landmark moment in Ghana's fight against illegal mining, insisting that the judgment should signal the beginning of a broader crackdown on politically exposed persons implicated in galamsey.

Speaking on JoyNews on Monday, July 20, shortly after the Accra High Court sentenced Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region, Dr Ashigbey said the verdict represented a significant victory not only for the country but also for years of advocacy by anti-galamsey campaigners.

Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay, presiding over the Criminal Division of the Accra High Court, sentenced Wontumi to 20 years in prison and imposed a fine of 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000.

The court further ruled that failure to pay the fine would attract an additional three-year custodial sentence.

Reacting to the judgment, Dr Ashigbey said the decision demonstrated that persistent advocacy and sustained public pressure could compel state institutions to act against influential individuals accused of environmental crimes.

"This is a good day for Ghana. This is a good day for Ghana, the Media Coalition Against Galamsey and the Coalition Against Galamsey in Ghana, and for all who want to see the back of this existential threat that confronts all of us as citizens," he declared.

Dr Ashigbey disclosed that the Samreboi case was among several petitions submitted by the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining to state authorities, adding that campaigners had monitored the matter from its inception to its conclusion.

According to him, the coalition formally petitioned the then Attorney-General and the Inspector-General of Police, while he personally joined private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu and two other campaigners in pursuing the matter.

"This is one case that the coalition petitioned. We petitioned the then Attorney-General, the then Inspector-General of Police, and personally, together with Martin Kpebu and two others, we also petitioned. We've been following it through all this while," he said.

He praised the current Attorney-General for prosecuting the matter to its conclusion, while also commending Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay for what he described as her courage in handling one of Ghana's most closely watched illegal mining prosecutions.

"I am happy and I think we also need to commend the Attorney-General for seeing this case through. We also want to commend the judge who sat on this case for demonstrating courage," he stated.

Dr Ashigbey also acknowledged the role played by the current Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, recalling how the minister convened an emergency press conference during the Easter holidays in 2025 after reviewing the coalition's petition.

"I remember Easter Sunday of 2025. I was in my home village of Tsiame when he called because we needed an urgent press conference. He had looked into the petition that we had submitted, carried out investigations and subsequently presented his report to the appropriate authorities," he recounted.

He further praised the former Minister for Lands and Natural Resources for being the first public official to openly state that Akonta Mining Company Limited had engaged in illegal mining activities within the Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve.

According to him, the former Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Commission, Martin Ayisi, subsequently confirmed the allegations, although he expressed disappointment that the authorities at the time failed to prosecute the case.

"The former minister publicly declared that Akonta Mining was involved in illegality in the Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve. Martin Ayisi also confirmed it. Unfortunately, the Attorney-General then and the police prosecutors did not prosecute, and we kept pushing," he noted.

While welcoming the conviction, Dr Ashigbey insisted that Ghana's campaign against illegal mining would remain incomplete if only one politically exposed person faced prosecution.

He reminded Ghanaians that President John Dramani Mahama, while campaigning ahead of the 2024 general election, had argued that the fight against galamsey would achieve little unless influential financiers and political actors behind the practice were brought to justice.

"It is great that we are dealing with one campaigner, but what has happened to the other politically exposed persons who were named in Professor Frimpong-Boateng's report?" he questioned.

He also called for updates on investigations into other politically connected individuals allegedly implicated in illegal mining, arguing that accountability should not be selective.

"There are several politically exposed persons who are involved in galamsey. There are Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives demonstrating either complicity or incompetence. There are chiefs who have openly been accused of involvement, and there have been public statements by eminent national figures indicating that some parliamentarians are facilitating illegal mining. What is happening to all these cases?" he asked.

Although he welcomed the 20-year prison sentence, Dr Ashigbey said he would have preferred the court to impose the maximum custodial sentence permitted under the law.

"I would have wished that the judge had given the maximum sentence of 25 years and also imposed the maximum fine," he stated.

He argued that illegal mining should be regarded as a grave offence because of its devastating environmental, economic and public health consequences.

According to him, illegal mining has contributed to flooding, widespread pollution of water bodies, the destruction of agricultural lands and serious health complications affecting communities across the country.

"The reason why we need to be drastic in sentencing the big financiers involved in galamsey is that what they do amounts to mass murder," he said.

"If somebody had taken a gun and shot another person, we would be demanding the maximum sentence. These people contribute to flooding, people are dying from kidney diseases, children are being born with deformities, pregnant women suffer complications, and they destroy our rivers, forests and agricultural lands."

Dr Ashigbey further argued that illegal mining threatens Ghana's long-term economic future by contaminating cocoa farms and other agricultural produce with heavy metals, thereby undermining exports and food security.

Describing the financiers of illegal mining as "economic saboteurs" and "nation wreckers", he maintained that the law must be applied without fear or favour regardless of political affiliation, social status or traditional authority.

"This is just the beginning. If we are truly going to deal decisively with galamsey, then we must ensure that all the powerful people who continue to profit from destroying our environment are also investigated, prosecuted and, where found guilty, punished in accordance with the law."

He expressed hope that the Wontumi conviction would serve as a strong deterrent to others engaged in illegal mining and mark a turning point in Ghana's efforts to protect its forests, rivers and future generations from the devastating effects of galamsey.

Ghana News.title: BoG warns global oil price volatility could heighten inflation risks for Ghana
Ghana News.content:
Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama

The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr. Johnson Asiama, has warned that renewed tensions in the Middle East and rising global oil prices could pose fresh inflation risks for Ghana, as the Monetary Policy Committee begins deliberations on the country's monetary policy stance.

Speaking at the opening of the 131st MPC meeting, Dr. Asiama said global economic developments have broadly evolved as expected since the last meeting, but downside risks have become more pronounced.

According to him, while a ceasefire in mid-June temporarily eased tensions and reduced oil prices, renewed hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz have reignited volatility in energy markets, with Brent crude climbing above 85 dollars per barrel earlier this week.

"The persistence of elevated energy prices has slowed the anticipated pace of global disinflation and prompted several central banks to reassess the timing of further easing."

Dr. Asiama said the developments are particularly significant for Ghana because the country exports commodities but relies on imports for its energy needs.

"For Ghana, as a commodity exporting yet energy importing economy, these developments reinforce the need to assess carefully the extent to which external cost pressures may influence the domestic inflation outlook over the policy horizon."

He said the MPC would also assess how continued volatility in global oil markets could affect Ghana's balance of payments, foreign reserves and exchange rate.

"The committee must consider what renewed volatility in global oil markets implies for the balance of payments, for reserve accumulation and for the exchange rate," he said.

The Governor noted that Ghana's external buffers remain a source of resilience, adding that prudent reserve management and exchange rate flexibility will continue to support macroeconomic stability.

"Ghana's external buffers remain a source of resilience and disciplined reserve management alongside continued exchange rate flexibility."
