World.title: Iraqi forces destroy six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi military announced on Monday that Iraqi security forces had identified and destroyed six suspected hideouts belonging to ISIS in the northern province of Kirkuk during an air operation.

Iraq’s Joint Operations Command said in a statement that an airborne group of Special Forces carried out a rapid security operation early on Monday.

The hideouts were destroyed in precise airstrikes after field operations identified them in the Zghitun Valley area in Kirkuk, according to the statement.

The Kurdistan Region Security Agency (Asayish) also announced the arrest of two suspected ISIS militants in separate operations coordinated with Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) in Sulaymaniyah province earlier in July.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Economist: Dollar return is out of reach for restricted Iraqi banks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prominent economic expert Ziad Al-Hashemi issued a sobering analysis on Monday, July 20, 2026, regarding the recent joint understanding between the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) and the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

Al-Hashemi cautioned that the official statements do not imply an imminent return to U.S. dollar transactions for the restricted Iraqi financial institutions, describing full dollar integration as currently “out of reach” due to stringent compliance benchmarks.

The critique follows an announcement by the Central Bank of Iraq and a welcoming statement from Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi regarding a framework to qualify seven restricted Iraqi banks for a return to international correspondent banking channels.

While the government celebrated the milestone as a major leap forward for global financial integration, Al-Hashemi emphasized that the U.S. Treasury has explicitly conditioned the lifting of restrictions on a series of rigorous structural reforms that remain far from complete.

According to Al-Hashemi’s assessment of the official U.S. Treasury declaration, the transition for these restricted institutions will be heavily phased and contingent on challenging corporate governance overhauls:

Alternative Currencies Only: The initial phase of the agreement only explores re-integrating select banks into global correspondent networks using non-dollar currencies, such as the Euro, UAE Dirham, and Chinese Yuan.

Lack of American Correspondent Partners: To date, no restricted Iraqi bank has regained the ability to conduct foreign currency transactions, primarily because major U.S. banking institutions refuse to establish correspondent relationships with them.

The Structural Phase One: The first phase of the CBI-led banking reform initiative is scheduled to conclude this summer, but eligibility for alternative currencies remains strictly tied to meeting baseline governance and compliance standards.

The Stringent Path to the Dollar: To eventually handle U.S. dollars, banks must successfully complete all subsequent reform phases, pass a satisfactory third-party audit of their compliance functions, attract a qualified institutional investor, and meet international standards regarding professional competence, integrity, and fitness.

Ownership Restructuring Barriers: Domestic banks view these extensive conditions as exceptionally difficult to implement, with the U.S. Treasury’s strict mandates regarding bank ownership percentages posing the most significant structural hurdle.

Citing the formal documentation, Al-Hashemi highlighted the explicit security guardrails embedded within Washington’s fiscal policy toward Baghdad: “The United States will not tolerate the abuse of Iraqi banks by armed groups allied with Iran, and will take independent action, when necessary, to target such activities.”

Al-Hashemi noted that the primary misconception in the local market stems from confusing the allowance of alternative currency clearing with the lifting of the actual U.S. dollar ban. He asserted that it is highly improbable for these seven banks to enter the U.S. dollar transfer system over the short or medium term.

Beyond the lack of acceptance from institutional U.S. correspondent banks, the restricted Iraqi financial firms have failed to fully implement the comprehensive restructuring requirements mandated by the global consulting firm Oliver Wyman. The Oliver Wyman plan serves as the core technical benchmark for the Central Bank of Iraq’s broader strategy to modernize the domestic financial sector, increase corporate transparency, and combat money laundering and illicit financial flows.

Until these foundational auditing and ownership criteria are completely satisfied, Al-Hashemi concludes that the financial integration celebrated during the Washington summit will remain an idealized roadmap rather than an immediate commercial reality.

World.title: Ryanair quarterly profit slides on Mideast war impact
World.content:
London – Irish no-frills airline Ryanair on Monday said net profit slumped 34 percent in its first quarter as the Middle East conflict sent jet-fuel prices soaring and impacted ticket sales.

Profit after tax dropped to 538 million euros ($616 million) in the three months to the end of June, from 820 million euros one year earlier, the Dublin-based carrier said in a statement.

Ryanair, which is Europe’s biggest airline by passenger numbers and flies mainly across the continent, said the cost of fuel not subject to advance purchase agreements had soared owing to the US-Iran war.

“Operating costs rose 11 percent to 3.81 billion euros as the price of our 20-percent unhedged jet-fuel more than doubled” in the first quarter, chief executive Michael O’Leary said in the earnings statement.

While passenger traffic grew six percent, fares dropped six percent.

Fares “required stimulation as the Middle East conflict led to consumer hesitancy, concerns about EU jet-fuel shortages, economic uncertainty and later bookings”, O’Leary said.

He added that Ryanair’s net profit for the remainder of its financial year “remains highly sensitive to… conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine, the price of unhedged jet-fuel, macro-economic shocks” and European air traffic control strikes.

Ryanair’s share price slid nearly six percent in Dublin midday trading after investors reacted to the bigger-than-expected drop in profits.

The airline’s “results show just how quickly nervousness surrounding the war has seeped into booking patterns and operational costs”, noted Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

“It’s a sign that consumers are once again tightening their belts and delaying discretionary spending, leaving airlines exposed not just to soaring jet fuel costs but also the prospect of softer demand.”

World.title: Iraq leads Gulf oil exports growth despite Hormuz crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq was one of the main drivers of the increase in crude oil exports from the Gulf region during the first half of July, according to shipping firms Kpler and Vortexa.

This development comes at a time when oil export levels from the region were at their peak since the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February, despite reduced tankers’ movements in the Strait of Hormuz due to increased military operations.

Oil exports from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Kuwait, and Iran increased by roughly 16 percent compared to June, hitting approximately 12 million barrels per day, according to Kpler, while Vortexa estimated the figure at 13.06 million barrels per day.

Iraq experienced the largest increase in oil shipments among the Gulf countries during that period, contributing significantly to the overall growth in crude exports alongside Saudi Arabia and Iran, according to Vortexa.

Despite this improvement, Reuters noted that oil shipments from the Gulf region are still approximately 32 percent below their pre-war level of 17.6 million barrels per day in February.

The number of oil tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz plummeted to three on a single day, the lowest level since May, raising fears about growing tensions and potential threats to Red Sea commerce, which might affect global oil flows.

World.title: Burnham becomes new UK PM after meeting king
World.content:
London – Andy Burnham became British prime minister Monday after meeting King Charles III at Buckingham Palace and was set to set out his vision for the country after taking over from Keir Starmer.

Starmer departed Downing Street on Monday morning, insisting in a farewell speech his two years in office had made Britain a better place.

The monarch met Starmer to accept his resignation and Burnham arrived next for the formal procedure in which the king asked him to form the next government and he accepted.

The 56-year-old is the sixth prime minister to enter Downing Street in the last 10 years.

“I am confident that Britain is now stronger and fairer than it was two years ago,” Starmer told reporters in his farewell speech outside his central London office.

“I go with good grace, I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved,” he added.

Burnham will face an in-tray overflowing with challenges with little time to make his mark.

In an interview with The Times published late Sunday, Burnham said he wanted to draw a line under a decade of political turmoil.

“What we’ve been doing hasn’t been working. That’s the way I see it,” he said.

“I am going to try and do things in a different way.”

In his first speech, Burnham will set out “priorities for restoring confidence in government and giving Britain more breathing room” amid the cost-of-living crisis, his team said.

Delivering growth and devolving power to regional communities are also expected to feature.

Also on Monday he is likely to announce his senior cabinet appointments, with all eyes on who will replace Rachel Reeves as finance minister.

The former mayor of Greater Manchester, nicknamed the “King of the North”, has been parachuted in by the Labour Party, after Starmer resigned last month, with MPs viewing him as the party’s best chance of reining in Nigel Farage’s anti-immigration Reform UK party.

– ‘Bigger, bolder’ –

Among Burnham’s most urgent challenges will be a tepid economy, high government borrowing costs, a ballooning welfare bill and irregular migrants arriving in small boats that have fuelled support for Reform.

Unpredictable energy prices due to the US-Iran war and a volatile American president in Donald Trump also threaten to buffet his premiership.

Burnham told The Times he would take a “different approach to public spending, and to running the economy — more focused on early investment, early intervention, setting people up for success, and much less paying for failure.”

He promised “early moves to help” with the cost of living, saying that while campaigning he heard the “pressure people feel around their finances”.

Starmer led Labour to power in July 2024 in a landslide election victory after 14 years of Conservative rule.

He announced that he would resign as prime minister and Labour Party leader in late June after a string of scandals, missteps and policy U-turns blighted his leadership.

But Burnham, who only returned as a member of parliament four weeks ago, has little room to manoeuvre amid sluggish economic growth, high public debt and strict financial rules requiring him to balance government spending against tax revenue.

– ‘Last chance’ –

Burnham was an MP between 2001 and 2017, serving as a minister in the governments of Tony Blair and Gordon Brown.

He has since reinvented himself as a man of the people, melding a relaxed, folksy style with slick social media videos.

But he has only three years to turn things around, with Reform leading in polls ahead of the next general election expected in 2029.

Burnham told supporters on Friday his Labour takeover was the “last chance” for the party to get things right.

Critics have accused Starmer’s government of being under-prepared for power when he was elected in July 2024.

Burnham has insisted he has a “plan”.

But his swift “coronation” as Labour leader has raised questions on how he will achieve his aims.

His first policy announcement came on Saturday when he scrapped Starmer’s flagship nationwide digital ID scheme, estimated to cost £1.8 billion over three years.

A spokesperson said the time and resources would be diverted “to where it’s most needed, such as helping with the cost of living”.

World.title: Boeing gets order for 100 737 MAX jets from leasing company SMBC
World.content:
Farnborough – US aircraft maker Boeing said Monday that it has received an order for 100 of its 737 MAX jets from leasing company SMBC Aviation Capital.

In the first major order to be announced at the Farnborough Air Show that opened in the UK on Monday.

The head of Boeing’s Commercial Airplanes division, Stephanie Pope, said that the order “reflects the strong demand we are seeing for the 737 MAX family’s efficiency, reliability and versatility”.

Following production quality issues, lawsuits, and an overhaul of its governance, the US company plans to stage a major comeback at Farnborough, just outside London.

The green light from the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in October 2025 to lift the cap on production of the single-aisle 737 MAX, its best-selling aircraft, is seen as an important milestone.

It is also awaiting the certification — after several years of delays — of its three new aircraft.

SMBC’s order, the value of which has not been disclosed, covers 60 737-10 aircraft and 40 737-8 aircraft.

“Our partnership with Boeing goes back more than two decades, and this order reflects market momentum, as our airline and investor customers look to increase capacity with the 737-10,” said SMBC chief executive Peter Barrett.

“This order will support their growth ambitions well into the next decade and reflects our strong confidence in the Boeing 737 MAX and sustained demand for fuel-efficient, technologically advanced narrowbody aircraft,” he said.

The company, based in Dublin, Ireland, and described as the world’s leading aviation finance platform, manages a fleet of 1,700 aircraft for more than 170 airlines worldwide.

Boeing also announced Monday that Saudi carrier Riyadh Air is exercising options for 28 787 Dreamliners from an order placed in 2023, and will convert 20 options to the largest variant of this aircraft.

Riyadh Air has also “confirmed an order for six additional Airbus A350-1000s, bringing its firm commitment for this type of aircraft to 31,” said the European aircraft manufacturer, Boeing’s rival, in a separate statement.

World.title: EU fines AliExpress 550 mn euros over illegal products
World.content:
Brussels – The EU on Monday slapped a 550-million-euro ($630 million) fine on online retailer AliExpress for allowing the sale of illegal products, including unsafe toys and cosmetics.

The European Union said AliExpress also did not do enough to stop the sale of counterfeit products and that when the platform detected illegal goods were on sale, many remained online for several weeks.

The EU found some of the products sold on the platform did not meet the bloc’s strict environmental and safety standards during its investigation into AliExpress launched in March 2024.

“Risks must be identified and addressed systematically to ensure consumers can safely shop online. Today, we are holding AliExpress to this standard and request it to take action,” EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said in a statement.

It is the largest fine ever imposed under the EU’s powerful Digital Services Act (DSA), part of the bloc’s armoury to police big tech that entered into force in 2022.

Elon Musk’s X social media platform received a 120-million-euro fine in December last year, while the EU slapped e-commerce giant Temu with a 200-million-euro fine in May.

The EU said the fine’s amount took into consideration the nature of the violations, the impact on Europeans and the duration of the infringements.

AliExpress is the biggest Chinese e-commerce platform in the EU with 193 million users, while Asian fashion giant Shein and retailer Temu respectively have 156 million and 130 million users.

The EU is AliExpress’ biggest market, a senior European official said.

Under the DSA, the world’s most popular digital platforms including social media networks and online retailers must evaluate what risks they pose and take measures to tackle the dangers.

– Illegal products reappearing –

The EU said AliExpress’ “overestimated the effectiveness of its system in detecting and removing illegal products”.

Millions of products would also reappear, the EU official said. And many illegal products would be recommended to users before they were removed.

Those selling illegal goods were still able to remain active on AliExpress.

The platform also did not “adequately” stop the sale of counterfeit products because its mandatory “brand authorisation” system “proved ineffective and understaffed. Therefore, traders easily bypassed this”, the EU found.

The DSA is part of a strengthened legal weaponry to rein in what the EU views as Big Tech’s excesses, and fines can go as high as six percent of a company’s total worldwide annual turnover.

The EU official said the global turnover of Alibaba, AliExpress’ parent company, was 122 billion euros last year, but the fine was well below six percent of that.

AliExpress has to now pay the fine and present a plan to the EU by October 20 that includes what action it will take to tackle the breaches.

If it does not comply, AliExpress risks periodic penalty payments.

Virkkunen told reporters AliExpress was “cooperating very actively” with the European Commission, the EU’s digital watchdog.

The EU has stepped up its efforts in recent years to combat what it says is unfair competition from Chinese retailers, including slapping a levy of three euros this month on cheap parcels entering the 27-nation bloc.

But Virkkunen insisted the EU did not target platforms based on their origin.

“We are investigating several online platforms. So a big part of them are from the USA, many of them are from China and also from Europe,” she said.

World.title: Cash reserves in Iraq’s central bank decline sharply
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed data on Monday indicating a sharp drop in cash reserves over the first four months of 2026, falling from 1.9 trillion Iraqi dinars ($1.45 billion) at the end of December 2025 to 566 billion Iraqi dinars ($432.7 million) by the end of April 2026.

According to the figures, cash reserves fell to 1.52 trillion Iraqi dinars ($1.16 billion) at the end of January, one trillion Iraqi dinars ($764.5 million) at the end of February, 849 billion Iraqi dinars ($649.1 million) at the end of March, and 566 billion Iraqi dinars ($432.7 million) at the end of April.

The analysis indicated that cash liquidity in the CBI’s vaults decreased by approximately 1.34 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $1.02 billion) over the four-month period, representing a 70.3 percent decline compared to December 2025, as reported by local news outlet Shafaq News.

Although cash liquidity remained greater than it was at the end of 2023, when it recorded 323 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $247 million), it fell dramatically compared to the end of 2024, when it hit two trillion Iraqi dinars ($1.52 billion), marking a 72.9 percent decline.

On the other hand, the official exchange rate stayed steady at 1,300 dinars to the US dollar from January to April 2026, while inflation rose steadily from 0.9 percent in January to 1.7 percent by the end of April.

World.title: Trainee IPS officer, accused of sexual harassment by colleague, hospitalised after suspected suicide attempt
World.content:
Representative image

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A trainee IPS officer, who was booked for allegedly stalking and sexually harassing a fellow trainee at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (SVPNPA) in Hyderabad, was hospitalised on Monday following a suspected suicide attempt, police said.According to a doctor who treated him, the trainee officer was brought to a private hospital in an unconscious state by his brother and friends, who suspected that he had consumed a harmful substance.The doctor added that a stomach wash was performed, but no "abnormal" substance was found.The trainee officer's blood and urine samples have been sent for tests, while his vital parameters remain stable.Although he was unconscious when brought to the hospital, he is now drowsy. The doctor added that further details would emerge after he regains full consciousness and the test reports are received.An alcohol bottle and a sanitizer bottle were found near his bed, according to the doctor, who cited the trainee officer's brother.The case stems from a complaint filed by a 30-year-old woman trainee IPS officer, who accused her fellow trainee of stalking and sexually harassing her. She alleged that he had been sending sexually abusive messages through an instant messaging app since June 23 and making derogatory remarks about her in front of her colleagues.The complainant claimed that the officer falsely accused her of having a relationship with another trainee and pressured her to admit to it, while using abusive language.She further alleged that on July 9, he restrained her, took her to his room by force, pulled her hair, attempted to strangle her, and held a knife to her neck, preventing her from leaving. She also accused him of assaulting her the following day.The woman alleged that the officer recorded a private video of her without consent and sent it to her husband in an attempt to blackmail her.Based on the complaint, a case was registered at Attapur police station on July 18 under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including charges related to assault or criminal force against a woman, sexual harassment, stalking, and insulting the modesty of a woman, along with provisions of the Information Technology Act, police said.The trainee IPS officer denied the allegations in a social media post, calling the complaint and rumours against him "baseless and untrue.""I fully trust the legal process and believe justice will prevail," he wrote.A police official said investigators would issue a notice asking him to appear in connection with the case.Following the registration of the case, the trainee officer left the academy, according to sources. He had earlier served as a constable in Andhra Pradesh.

World.title: 'Disgusting what government is doing': Rahul Gandhi slams police action against protesters; shares video
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha

on Monday called Prime Minister

the 'most youth-hostile Prime Minister in India's history'.

He also criticised the use of tear gas and lathi charge against students protesting the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, saying they were only demanding a fair education system.

In a video statement shared on X, Rahul alleged that students protesting for a fair education system were being treated like criminals instead of being heard.

"This country has a majority of young people. Prime Minister Modi is the most anti-youth Prime Minister India has ever had. The boys and girls who are walking the streets of Delhi are not criminals. They are demanding their rights. Their rights are to have an education system that respects them, an education system that is fair and an education system that is working," Rahul said.

He criticised the police action against protesters, saying, "There is absolutely nothing wrong in what they are doing. It is disgusting what the government is doing and what the police is doing. Tear-gassing students and lathi-charging students is not democratic. It is not India's way and it is not the way this should be done."

Rahul said the protesters' demands were legitimate and urged the Prime Minister to act on them.





"The Prime Minister should accept these demands and do something about it. Everybody is sick and tired of the way our education system is running. Everybody is sick and tired of how the RSS has captured our education system and how all our institutions are being run by one organisation," he said.

Claiming that the Congress had been raising concerns over the education system for years, Rahul added, "This is a natural response that the young people of India are making and it should be respected.

We've been raising this issue not for weeks or months. We've been raising it for years. There's a fundamental problem and Modi disrespects all the young people of this country. All they believe in is Asatya and Hinsa, which are anti-Indian principles.

"

In a separate post on X, Congress MP alleged that PM Modi had failed to act against Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan despite repeated examination controversies.

"Prime Minister Modi is the most youth-hostile Prime Minister in India's historyâso youth-hostile that he can't even demand the resignation of a failed Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan," Gandhi wrote.

He further claimed, "152 paper leaks. 7.5 crore students victimised. And not a single guilty person punished. Who got the punishment? The hardworking youth."

Referring to the police action, Lok Sabha LoP said, "When these children raised legitimate questions about education, they were met with batons and detention.

The criminals who leaked the papers roam free, while the students raising valid issues are dragged around and beaten. This government isn't just failing the youthâit is pouncing on them."

His remarks came as the protests intensified outside Parliament, where members of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) attempted to march towards Parliament demanding accountability over the alleged paper leak and the resignation of Pradhan.

Delhi Police used mild force to disperse protesters after they attempted to breach barricades. Police said several personnel were injured during the clashes after stones were allegedly thrown at security personnel.

Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also criticised the police action, questioning why students protesting over issues related to the education system were being met with tear gas and baton charges.

Delhi Police, meanwhile, denied claims by the CJP that its founder Abhijeet Dipke had been detained during the protest, saying he was 'available on stage' and dismissing reports of his detention as 'entirely false.'

Security remained tightened across New Delhi as prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) continued to remain in force.

World.title: 'It destroys academic freedom': TMC on VBSA bill as JPC defers report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With the JPC deciding to defer the report on the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan bill,

MP Sagarika Ghose said the opposition forced the govt to put a hold on the controversial legislation that would destroy the education sector.

Ghose said, âThe shelving of the bill is a big win for the opposition. Trinamool Congress pushed back against the VBSA bill which is anti-student and anti-federalism.â

TMC sources said the bill exceeds the constitutional parameters while making higher education the preserve of the rich. âIt attacks federalism, creates a massive centralized structure and rule by New Delhi. It destroys academic freedom and constitutes a narrow interpretation of Bharatiya Knowledge Systems based on only one religion.â

A senior TMC leader claimed the govt intends to demolish the UGC, in the absence of which the universities will take loans and repayment of the loans will lead to hiking of fees. âHow will poor students afford education,â she asked.

The bill was strongly opposed by Congress, DMK, Shiv Sena while, it is reported, govt ally TDP too had reservations over it.

World.title: Fresh landslide kills seven in rain-ravaged Poonch, J&K toll rises to 17
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At least seven people were killed after a landslide struck a mud house in Jammu and Kashmir's rain-hit Poonch district on Monday, officials said.

The latest incident occurred in the higher reaches of Loran village, where a mud house was buried under debris following the landslide.

Among those killed were four women, officials said.

Rescue operations are under way at the site.

Officials said Poonch has been battered by torrential rain since Saturday evening. With the latest incident, 17 people have lost their lives in the district, while six others remain missing.

In a separate operation, a joint team of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the Indian Army carried out a rescue and recovery operation to retrieve a body from the Munawar River in the Nowshera area of Rajouri district.

The fresh tragedy comes a day after torrential rain triggered flash floods and landslides across the Pir Panjal region, killing at least 14 people and leaving several others trapped under debris.

Chief minister Omar Abdullah cut short his visit to New Delhi and flew to Jammu on Sunday to oversee relief and rescue operations. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha also reviewed the situation and directed officials to provide immediate assistance to affected families.





The heavy rain also disrupted traffic on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway and led to the temporary suspension of the annual Amarnath Yatra and pilgrimages to the Vaishno Devi shrine and Shiv Khori after the India Meteorological Department forecast more adverse weather.

Rescue operations involving the Army, police, SDRF, NDRF, civil administration and local volunteers are continuing in the worst-affected areas of Poonch and Rajouri as authorities search for the missing and assess the damage.

World.title: Evening news wrap: CJP delegation meets JP Nadda as protest intensifies, Andy Burnham becomes UK's new PM & more
World.content:
CJP leaders met Union minister JP Nadda, demanding Sonam Wangchuk's release, Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and compensation for families of NEET aspirants, while the minister assured them he would discuss the demands with the government.

Andy Burnham became the United Kingdom's 59th prime minister after succeeding Keir Starmer, promising to focus on affordability, regional equality and economic reforms.

The Supreme Court said the alleged Ram temple donation embezzlement case should not be politicised and asked the Uttar Pradesh government to update it on the SIT probe on July 27.

Parliament's Monsoon Session opened with repeated disruptions over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak and Ram temple donation case , forcing multiple adjournments in both Houses.

, forcing multiple adjournments in both Houses. The Delhi high court sought Sonam Wangchuk's complete medical records and directed doctors to appear before it before deciding on his plea to shift to a private hospital.

Here are the top 5 news stories

CJP takes NEET demands to JP Nadda as protest enters talks

Cockroach Janata Party delegation met BJP president and Union minister JP Nadda, demanding Sonam Wangchuk's release, Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and compensation for families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.

Nadda assured the delegation he would discuss the demands with the government but made no commitments, while appealing to protesters to end their sit-in and help restore normalcy.

Andy Burnham becomes UK's new PM after Starmer's exit

Andy Burnham formally became the United Kingdom's 59th prime minister after succeeding Keir Starmer unopposed as Labour leader. The former Greater Manchester mayor will now form his Cabinet, begin a nationwide listening tour during Parliament's summer recess and prepare to roll out his domestic agenda before MPs return in September.

'Don't politicise it': Supreme Court on Ram temple donation case

The Supreme Court said the alleged Ram temple donation embezzlement case was a criminal matter that should not be politicised and stressed that its role was to ensure a fair investigation. The court sought details on the SIT probe, while the Uttar Pradesh government is set to update it on the investigation's progress on July 27.

Monsoon Session opens with protests, repeated adjournments

The opening day of Parliament's Monsoon Session witnessed repeated disruptions as opposition parties demanded discussions on the alleged NEET-UG paper leak and Ram temple donation case.





Both Houses were adjourned several times, while protests outside Parliament over the NEET issue led to police action and heightened security in central Delhi.

Delhi HC seeks Wangchuk's medical records, doctors' presence

The Delhi high court directed authorities to submit Sonam Wangchuk's complete medical records, including fresh health reports, and asked doctors from Safdarjung Hospital, AIIMS and Wangchuk's medical team to appear before it. The court will decide on Tuesday whether to allow his transfer to a private hospital.

World.title: Ram Temple donation row: Trust deploys new cash-counting team, introduces two-shift system under SBI supervision
World.content:
Ram Temple in Ayodhya

NEW DELHI: The Ram Temple trust in Ayodhya has deployed a new team to count cash offerings from donation boxes and introduced a two-shift system under the supervision of the State Bank of India (SBI), even as an investigation continues into allegations of donation theft.The responsibility for counting the money collected from donation boxes installed inside the Ram Temple premises lies with the SBI.The exercise began on Sunday after the completion of a week-long trial, following which the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, which manages the temple, formally handed over the cash-counting process to SBI, PTI reported, citing sources.According to temple sources, 10 to 12 personnel have been assigned to each shift. The first shift runs from 8 am to 2 pm, while the second operates from 2 pm to 8 pm.The trust has appointed Shobhnath Mishra as the new in-charge of cash counting after his predecessor, Subhash Shrivastava, was sent to jail in connection with the alleged donation theft case.To strengthen monitoring, the trust has appointed four supervisors, including a former serviceman, to oversee the counting process.Trust security in-charge and former Army officer Captain KK Tiwari has been designated the senior in-charge and will be responsible for submitting daily reports on the exercise.Former defence personnel SP Dubey and Sheshmani Tiwari have also been appointed as trust representatives to supervise the cash-counting process.The alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple donations came to light in the first week of June, following which the Uttar Pradesh government constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) on June 13 to investigate the matter.After the SIT submitted its preliminary report on June 23, an FIR was registered on June 25. Eight accusedâAvinash Shukla, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Kumar Yadav, Karunesh Pandey, Ramashankar Mishra, Subhash Srivastava and Ramashankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadavâwere arrested.During the investigation, police recovered cash from several accused, with the highest recovery of Rs 20.39 lakh from Avinash Shukla. Authorities also seized gold, silver, foreign currency and a donation box marked "Ramrajya Kosh."

World.title: Delhi HC seeks comprehensive medical record on Sonam Wangchuk's condition
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Monday sought a comprehensive record of climate activist

's medical condition and directed the authorities to place all relevant health documents before it.

A division bench of Chief Justice D K Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia asked the authorities to submit all pathological reports prepared by Safdarjung Hospital,

and the private laboratory, along with every health bulletin issued on Wangchuk's condition.

"The report should include today's sample analysis", said the bench said.

It also directed the appellant to file reports of tests conducted through the private laboratory.

The court further directed the doctor heading the medical team treating Wangchuk at Safdarjung Hospital, AIIMS Director, and Dr Akshay, In-charge of Emergency Medicine at AIIMS, to remain present before it on Tuesday. It also requested the doctor engaged by Wangchuk's family to appear and assist the court.

The court said that it would take a call on Tuesday on whether to allow Angmo's plea to shift Wangchuk to a private facility.

The directions came while hearing an appeal filed by Wangchuk's wife against a single judge's refusal to interfere with the Centre's decision to shift the activist to Safdarjung Hospital.

On Sunday, the single judge had upheld the government's decision, observing that shifting Wangchuk to the hospital was not arbitrary in view of his deteriorating health after weeks of fasting.





The court had issued notice to the Centre and directed it to file a status report within three days.

"Since the government has taken the decision to shift him to the hospital on account of his medical condition, this court does not find the same to be an arbitrary action," the court had observed.

"Since doctors at Safdarjung are closely monitoring his health and have only given oral things as per his consent, it can't be said any force is being used against him," it added.

World.title: Govt, opposition face off on Day 1 of Monsoon Session: Key takeaways
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The opening day of Parliament's Monsoon Session descended into a government-versus-opposition showdown on Monday as repeated protests led to multiple adjournments before both the Houses were adjourned for the day.

The opposition demanded discussions on the alleged NEET-UG paper leak and the alleged embezzlement of donations meant for the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, while the government pressed ahead with its legislative business amid the disruptions, according to news agency PTI.

This development comes as large number of students and protesters attempted to march towards Parliament following a call by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), but were stopped by police, who used tear gas and carried out a lathi-charge after the crowd tried to breach barricades.

Lok Sabha disrupted from the start

11 am

: The Lok Sabha convened at 11 am, but proceedings were disrupted almost immediately as opposition members raised slogans and displayed placards, demanding discussions on the NEET-UG paper leak and the alleged Ram Temple donation scam.

Speaker Om Birla objected to members raising slogans while obituary references for six former MPs were being read, calling it an inappropriate precedent. With protests continuing, the House was adjourned till 12 noon.





12.00 pm:

When the House reassembled at 12 noon, the disruptions continued, forcing another adjournment till 12.30 pm.

During the brief sitting, Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal introduced The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to replace the ordinance increasing the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges from 34 to 38, including the Chief Justice of India.

12.30 pm:

The House met again at 12.30 pm, but repeated appeals by the Chair to allow Zero Hour to function failed to calm protesting MPs.

Presiding officer Dilip Saikia adjourned proceedings till 1 pm.

At 1 pm:

Opposition protests continued. Saikia urged members to return to their seats, saying, "The House is ready for discussions on various issues. But you are not interested. You don't want to discuss people's issues. This is not the way."

"You are disrupting the House repeatedly. You are showing banners and posters which is not acceptable," he added.

As protests continued, the House was adjourned till 2 pm.

2.00 pm:

When the Lok Sabha reconvened at 2 pm, presiding officer Jagdambika Pal said there was adequate quorum to conduct business, although opposition MPs alleged they were being prevented from entering the House. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju maintained that the House could not function amid continuous disruptions.

The House was adjourned again at 2.30 pm as opposition members continued protesting despite appeals to allow proceedings under Rule 377.

Adjourned at 3.00 pm:

After assembling six times during the day, the Lok Sabha was finally adjourned at around 3 pm and will reconvene at 11 am on Tuesday.

Rajya Sabha also adjourned

11 am:

The Rajya Sabha witnessed similar scenes, with opposition members demanding discussions on the same issues. Repeated disruptions prevented normal business, forcing the Upper House to adjourn for the day.

It will also reconvene at 11 am on Tuesday.

Earlier in the day, Rajya Sabha Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan administered the oath to newly elected members, including senior Congress leader Pawan Khera, BJP MPs Dr Mukeshbhai J.

Rathwa, Mahesh Kewat, NPP's James Pangsang Kongkal Sangma, and BJP's Prakash Chik Baraik.

PM Modi appeals for productive session

Minutes before Parliament convened, Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged MPs to ensure a productive Monsoon Session. "We hope that the monsoon and the Monsoon Session of Parliament are productive... I appeal to all MPs to wholeheartedly participate in proceedings of Monsoon session," he said.

"We are well aware, and the entire world is concerned about the persistent threat of war in various regions.

The conflict in West Asia posed a major crisis for countries like India that rely on others for energy. Numerous obstacles and crises arose regarding petrol, diesel, LPG, fertilisers, and chemicals. Despite this, India maintained a growth rate of 7.7 per cent, emerging as the fastest-growing major economy in the world," he added.

The prime minister also took a veiled swipe at leader of opposition in Loka Sabha, Rahul Gandhi while praising the young team behind Skyroot Aerospace's successful launch of India's first privately developed orbital rocket.

"I am told that the average age of the team working at the Skyroot start-up is just 28 years. It is these young minds who have made this possible. I am not talking about a 56-year-old young man; I am talking about a start-up whose team, with an average age of just 28, has planted India's flag in the realm of space," Modi said.

Opposition attacks government

Leader of the opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of suppressing democratic protests and demanded accountability over the alleged Ram Temple donation scam.

"Lathi-charge on students is an attack on democracy. This government is not capable of staying in power," Kharge said.

"We have also raised the issue of theft of donations (at Ayodhya Ram Temple). Modi sahib should take responsibility because he is the one who created the Trust," he added.

Priyanka slams police action on protesters

Congress general secretary

also criticised the Centre over the police action against students and protesters marching towards Parliament, accusing the government of refusing to discuss issues related to the education system while resorting to force.

"It's ridiculous... They are our own children... they are the future of the country. This Parliament belongs to them. It's no one's personal fiefdom," Priyanka Gandhi told reporters in the Parliament House complex.

"It is a genuine issue, Rahul ji has been raising this issue for quite some time. We have been saying there should be a discussion as there are problems in the education policy. You are not ready to discuss and fire tear gas at children and beat them up.

For what? They are our children," she added.

Tharoor: Parliament cannot become a notice board

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor criticised the government for refusing to allow discussions on key issues. "Parliament is supposed to be the place where we can ventilate the voice of the people," he said.

"It cannot be a notice board for government to announce its bills and get them passed with a rubber stamp." Questioning the police action against protesters, Tharoor added, "Lathi-charge is not an act of non-violence, it is an act of violence.

I don't understand the logic of it."

SP chief Akhilesh backs protesting students

Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also targeted the government over the alleged NEET paper leak and the handling of student protests.

"They are keeping protesters in police stations and beating students outside. What kind of government is this that talks about 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas' but doesn't want to listen to children? Is it a government or is it your ego?" he asked.

Questioning the credibility of the examination process, Yadav said, "If the NEET examination happened and there was cheating, who is responsible? What about the credibility?" He also said students protesting for justice should be treated with dignity.

Protests outside Parliament

The political confrontation extended beyond Parliament as protesters led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) attempted to march from Jantar Mantar towards Parliament, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak.

Police stopped the march after protesters attempted to breach barricades, using mild force to disperse the crowd. Security around Parliament was tightened, with several entry gates closed and additional personnel deployed.

Earlier in the day, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke ended his indefinite hunger strike at the request of activist

, who remains admitted to Safdarjung Hospital after his own hunger strike.

The session, which will continue till August 13, is expected to witness intense exchanges as the opposition presses the government on a host of issues ahead of key state elections.

World.title: Coimbatore Corporation’s repurposed container shops remain vacant
World.content:
The 11 shops developed from repurposed shipping containers by the Coimbatore Corporation on Codissia Road have remained vacant for nearly five months after their inauguration, as they are yet to receive a dedicated high-tension (HT) electricity connection.

The project, executed at a cost of around ₹30 lakh, was inaugurated by Coimbatore MP Ganapathy P. Rajkumar in February this year. The initiative was aimed at creating commercial space by repurposing shipping containers.

According to Corporation officials, the shops have not been opened for occupation as the facility is awaiting the installation and energisation of a dedicated HT electricity connection. Once the power connection is provided, the civic body will complete water supply arrangements for the shops.

Officials said the Corporation would then float a tender for allotting the 11 shops.

World.title: CJP protest in Delhi LIVE: Govt reaches out to CJP amid raging protest; several injured, detained as police crack down
World.content:
Protesters marching toward Parliament from Sansad Marg side were stopped by security forces outside the Sansad Marg Police station on Monday (July 20, 2026). Security forces used batons to control the crowd, injuring a few protesters who received first aid on site. Police fired tear gas at protesters, who have been stopped at Raisina Road, barely 200 metres from Parliament. The Parliament march began from Jantar Mantar, where the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has been holding a sit-in since June 20, and coincided with the first day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

CJP on Monday said that it’s spokespersons met Health Minister J. P. Nadda and they submitted a letter, demanding the immediate release of Sonam Wangchuk, Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation and one crore compensation for all NEET-UG aspirants who died after the NEET-UG paper leak.

Also read: Neha, a prominent face of the CJP protests, presses on with hunger strike

Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Monday urged the authorities at Safdarjung Hospital to discharge him, citing his stable health condition, so that he could participate in the “Sansad Chalo” march to Parliament led by Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and other activists.

World.title: Andy Burnham: U.K.’s latest PM | Infographics
World.content:
Veteran Labour politician and former Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham is set to become the United Kingdom’s next Prime Minister on Monday (July 20, 2026), formally succeeding Keir Starmer, who announced his resignation last month.

Burnham was the only candidate to secure enough nominations from Labour lawmakers to contest the party leadership, effectively guaranteeing his election. As Labour commands a majority in Parliament, its leader automatically becomes the U.K. Prime Minister.

Burnham won the backing of 349 of Labour’s 401 MPs and was elected party leader at a special Labour conference on Friday (July 17, 2026). He will formally assume office on Monday after meeting King Charles III at Buckingham Palace, where he will be invited to form a government. Until then, Starmer remains caretaker prime minister.

Starmer announced his resignation as Labour leader on June 22, 2026 after less than two years in office, bringing to an end a tenure marked by a series of political setbacks. The most damaging was his appointment of a man with close ties to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein as Britain’s ambassador to the United States.

Burnham’s appointment makes him Britain’s seventh prime minister in a decade.

The rapid turnover of leaders began after the 2016 Brexit referendum. Since then, the U.K. has grappled with sluggish economic growth, high public debt, rising welfare costs and increasing geopolitical uncertainty while seeking to redefine its place outside the European Union.

Here is a look at Britain’s latest leadership transition and the key events that led to it:

A brief timeline on Andy Burnham

The 56-year-old projects the image of an approachable northern everyman, preferring T-shirts to suits and spending his free time playing football or DJing with 1990s music.

But Burnham is also a veteran politician. His career has taken him from senior Cabinet positions to serving as Mayor of Greater Manchester, and now to the brink of becoming Britain’s prime minister.

Here is a brief timeline on his career:

World.title: Farmers urge Coimbatore Collector to reconsider 430-kV transmission line route through farmlands
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Farmers Protection Association (Tamilaga Vivasayigal Paadhukaappu Sangam) have petitioned the Coimbatore District Collector on Monday to reconsider the proposed 430-kV power transmission line from Kavuthampalayam in Tiruppur district to Idaiyarpalayam in Coimbatore district, urging the authorities to replace overhead transmission towers with an underground cable system.

In the petition, they said the proposed alignment would pass through fertile agricultural lands in Coimbatore district, affecting thousands of farming families. They contended that the transmission towers would reduce cultivable area, hinder the use of farm machinery, lower land value, restrict future development, and affect farmers’ livelihoods.

The petitioners also said the project could impact horticulture, dairy farming and other agriculture-based activities. They expressed concerns over safety during seismic events and claimed that electromagnetic fields from high-voltage lines could pose health and environmental risks.

World.title: Two die after overhead tank falls on mini-lorry in Namakkal
World.content:
Two persons died when an overhead water tank fell on a mini-lorry at Sathya Nagar bus stop near Mallasamudram in Namakkal district on Sunday evening.

According to police, B. Subash (29), a resident of Sekkarapatti near Elachipalayam and a mini-lorry driver, headed to Krishnagiri district to unload eggs in a mini truck on Sunday evening. He was accompanied by loadman K. Kumar (45), a resident of Akkaraikadu near Mallasamudram.

At Sathya Nagar Bus Stop near Mallasamudram, Subash lost control of the vehicle, which hit the pillar of an overhead water tank on the roadside. In the impact, the water tank, which was 25-years-old, collapsed and fell on the vehicle.

On information, Fire and Rescue Service Department personnel rushed to the spot, removed the debris with an earthmover and retrieved the bodies.

The bodies were sent to Namakkal Medical College Hospital for a post-mortem examination.

The Mallasamudram police registered a case.

The water in the tank had been supplied to more than 10 streets in the locality earlier in the day. As such, it was empty at the time of the accident, sources added.

World.title: SIT probing examination anomalies carries out checks at Kerala PSC headquarters
World.content:
The special investigation team (SIT) probing the alleged malpractices in the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) examination system carried out checks at the PSC headquarters in Thiruvananthapuram on Monday (July 20, 2026).

In the fourth round of checks carried out by the SIT led by Inspector General (IG) Ajeetha Begum, the team mainly looked at the software used for conducting examinations.

The team was accompanied by IT experts to look into the examination software that involves an On-Screen Marking (OSM) system. The Internal Vigilance Wing of the PSC had found anomalies in the valuation of 10 questions in the examination for the Chief (Industry and Infrastructure) post in the State Planning Board.

According to the interim report filed by the vigilance officer, the answers to nine questions for any of the 228 candidates had not been evaluated due to an error in assigning these questions for evaluation in the OSM system.

World.title: Bengali to be used in all official State communication from September 1, says CM Suvendu
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday (July 20, 2026) announced that starting from September 1, the State Government will give priority to the Bengali language in all official government work.

Mr. Adhikari made the announcement on the floor of West Bengal Legislative Assembly, stating that all official correspondence, and administrative orders of the State government departments will be carried out in Bengali language. The Chief Minister stated that Union Home Minister Amit Shah had written, to him requesting that, on the occasion of the 125th birth anniversary of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee, the use of the Bengali language in West Bengal should be promoted more extensively.

The move to promote Bengali language by the BJP government in West Bengal is an interesting political shift as the Opposition parties, particularly the Trinamool Congress, has accused the BJP of imposing the Hindi language in the State.

“Instead of a foreign language, Bengali and Rajbhasha Hindi can be used in official communications with the Centre,” Mr. Shah said in the letter to Mr. Adhikari.

Mr. Shah mentioned that Bengali language should be given priority in public services, digital administration, and other communications, websites, mobile apps, media s and other governmental interactions.

The Chief Minister said that the State government welcomes this suggestion and that henceforth all official correspondence within West Bengal will be conducted in Bengali.Mr. Adhikari said that Home Minister had suggested that Bengali language should be used extensively in the registration of FIRs, complaint filing, citizen information, and public awareness messages to strengthen the people’s faith in and their participation with the administration.

For communication with the Central Government, both Bengali and Hindi will be used, the Chief Minister said.

The Chief Minister reiterated that the process of fully implementing Bengali as the language of administration in the State government’s work will officially start on September 1.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) welcomed the Chief Minister’s remarks on making Bengali mandatory for all official communication. “TMC gave lip service, but the BJP government walks the talk! Under the decisive leadership of Chief Minister Shri @SuvenduWB, a historic step is here to uphold the absolute dignity of our mother tongue. Starting 1st September, the usage of Bengali language is mandatory across all government departments!,” the West Bengal BJP posted on its official X handle.

World.title: LAWCET counselling dates further extended
World.content:
The last date for online registration and uploading certificates for verification for admission into LL.B 3YDC and LL.B 5YDC courses has been extended yet again.

Candidates can now upload their documents up to July 28, as per the revised schedule announced on Monday. Accordingly, web options are to be exercised from July 28 to 31. The provisional list of selected candidates will be published on August 5. A similar revision was announced on July 10, setting July 20 as the deadline.

The revision, according to officials, was made after examining concerns, including pending results of final-year students of certain courses at Osmania University. There have been instances of students securing a rank in the CET but still waiting for crucial documents to proceed with registration and payment.

World.title: UK universities hit record high applications; Indian students rank second among international UG applicants
World.content:
The UK has recorded its highest-ever number of undergraduate applicants in 2026, with fresh Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (UCAS) data showing a record surge in international applications. India emerged as the second-largest source of overseas undergraduate applicants, behind only China.

A total of 695,740 students applied through UCAS for undergraduate admissions this year, up 4.6% from 665,070 in the previous year. International applications rose 7.1% year-on-year to a record 148,350, outpacing growth among domestic applicants.

Record international demand



International undergraduate applicants reached a record 1,48,350 in 2026, a 7.1% increase from 138,460 last year. This translates to an additional 9,890 overseas applicants in a single admission cycle.

The latest figure also continues a long-term upward trend. International applications stood at 120,080 in 2017 and have steadily climbed over the past decade, touching a new high this year after minor fluctuations in recent admission cycles.

World.title: Amid SIR, Karnataka starts door-to-door drive for caste, residence papers
World.content:
Amid the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll by the Election Commission of India (ECI), Karnataka’s Congress government Monday launched a door-to-door drive to deliver caste certificates and empowered deputy tahsildars to issue permanent residence certificates (PRCs).

Both certificates feature in the ECI’s “indicative list of documents” used to verify a voter’s identity during the SIR’s notice phase.

The government has already classified and shared 4.85 crore digital caste certificates with deputy commissioners. “The district administration will print the certificates and deliver them directly to beneficiaries,” Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said during the launch of the initiative.

Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said the free door-to-door distribution of caste certificates and PRCs aims to help people easily obtain the documents required for SIR. “These certificates will not only facilitate access to various government services but also help citizens establish their status as permanent residents of Karnataka,” he said.

A mobile application has been developed to record beneficiaries’ Aadhaar, mobile numbers, and acknowledgements after the certificates are delivered. People will also be able to download their caste certificates free of cost through the designated government website using the certificate’s RD number, ration card number, or Aadhaar number, according to the chief minister.

The service will also be available at government assistance centres established at the level of village clusters where citizens can obtain printed copies of caste certificates and other essential documents free of charge.

According to Shivakumar, around 57 lakh caste certificates are already linked to beneficiaries’ mobile numbers, and download links have been sent through WhatsApp and SMS.

Eligibility criteria for permanent residence certificate



On the eligibility criteria to obtain a PRC, Parameshwara said that applicants must either be born in Karnataka or meet prescribed conditions. The conditions include being a resident of the state for at least 10 years, completing II PUC or an equivalent qualification in Karnataka, and studying in a recognised educational institution in the state.

“Eligibility also extends to those who have served for at least seven years in government or local bodies. Applicants may also qualify if their father, mother, husband, or wife has resided in Karnataka for at least 10 years,” he said.

In addition, applicants should own or lawfully occupy immovable property in Karnataka, have their names in the electoral roll, and should reside in the state in the case of those married to a resident. These form the basis for issuing the PRC, he added.

The government announced the drive to ensure identity documents a month ago, before the SIR began in the state on June 30.

The Opposition BJP has criticised the government’s move, alleging that it was an “illegal” ploy to protect Bangladeshi migrants and create a vote bank for the Congress.



Booth-level officers are verifying voter documents door-to-door. After this, the draft electoral roll will be published on August 17. Claims and objections of those served notices during the first phase will be disposed of between August 17 and October 15. The final roll will be published on October 19.

World.title: ‘I gained 4-5 kilos’: Shamita Shetty on endometriosis, severe pain and weight changes
World.content:
Shamita Shetty, 47, recently shared that she gained 4-5 kilos in the run-up to endometriosis surgery, which happened in May 2024. “I kind of dragged it on. The right kind of diagnosis wasn’t given to me, and then every time I felt certain symptoms, I thought maybe it was normal. Before the surgery, I was in severe pain for 6-8 months. When the pain woke me up from sleep, that’s when I came to my doctor. I thought it was related to perimenopause. The pain was getting in the way of every other activity I was doing, whether it was my workout or anything else. There was constant lower back pain. I also had a problem with cysts,” said Shetty on actor Soha Ali Khan’s YouTube podcast.

During the conversation, she also spoke about “sudden” weight gain. “I think I must have gained about 4-5 kgs. That was the heaviest I have ever been. I was perimenopausal too,” she said, adding that she also had water retention.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

Her treating doctor, Dr Neeta Warty, noted that she has Pelvic Inflammatory Disease, which is an infection in the tubes. “We treated her for that. After that, we asked her to come back to check the source of pain, as initially, it was difficult to treat when extremely painful,” said Dr Warty.

Shetty also shared that it took her “a couple of years” to lose the weight.

Dr Dimple Jain, consultant obstetrician and gynaecologist at KIMS Hospitals, Thane, said endometriosis is not a direct cause of significant weight gain, but many women with the condition notice changes in their weight. “One main reason is bloating and water retention, especially during the menstrual cycle. Hormonal changes and ongoing inflammation can make the abdomen feel swollen, creating the illusion of weight gain even when there hasn’t been an increase in body fat. In fact, this bloating, sometimes called “endo belly,” can be so noticeable that it alters how clothes fit within just a day or two,” said Dr Jain.

Additionally, chronic pelvic pain can limit physical activity. “Hormonal medications used to treat endometriosis may also lead to fluid retention or changes in appetite in some women. As a result, many patients feel heavier or notice that their clothes fit differently, even if the scale hasn’t changed much,” said Dr Jain.



Can surgery for endometriosis affect body weight?

Yes, but not always in the expected way. “Surgery itself does not cause long-term weight gain or loss. In the weeks after an operation, temporary fluid retention, reduced mobility during recovery, and changes in eating habits may affect the scale. Once healing is finished and pain lessens, many women gradually return to their usual activity levels, which often helps them regain their previous fitness and weight over time. Patience during recovery is important; the body needs time to heal before it can return to old routines,” said Dr Jain.

Why can it take months or even years to lose the extra weight?

Weight recovery after endometriosis depends on several factors, including hormonal balance, the severity of the disease, lifestyle, stress, sleep, and whether medications are still being taken. “For women who have dealt with pain for years, rebuilding exercise routines and healthy habits often takes time, rather than happening quickly. Sustainable weight loss requires patience and shouldn’t be hurried; small, consistent changes usually last longer than drastic ones,” said Dr Jain.

When should women seek medical advice?

Persistent pelvic pain, painful periods that disrupt daily life, pain during intercourse, difficulty conceiving, or frequent bloating should not be ignored as normal. “Early evaluation can help identify endometriosis before it worsens. While weight changes alone are rarely a sign of the condition, they should be looked at in combination with other symptoms. A timely diagnosis and proper treatment can improve quality of life, preserve fertility in many cases, and help women return to their normal routines sooner,” said Dr Jain.

Weight changes linked to endometriosis usually relate more to bloating, medication side effects, and reduced activity than to actual fat gain. “Understanding this can help women feel less discouraged and more informed about what their bodies are experiencing and when to consult a doctor,” said Dr Jain.

World.title: Nico Williams & Ferran Torres: A tale of immigration, a battle with depression
World.content:
105:28. New Jersey.

Final of the World Cup. 0-0.

Nahuel Molina glanced over his shoulder. Nico Williams lingered a few yards behind. Should a cross arrive from the opposite flank, Argentina’s right-back assumed he would have it covered.

Molina set himself to meet Pedro Porro’s delivery. Then came the chill. Williams was no longer behind him. He was in front.

Molina had been beaten by the sprint.

It is what Williams does. Second among Spaniards on top speed, third on number of sprints per 90 minutes.

He scores, creates, dribbles and dances. Mostly, though, he runs.

He runs because two others once walked.

Spain’s Ferran Torres, left, and Nico Williams (17) celebrate after scored the winning goal in the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough) Spain’s Ferran Torres, left, and Nico Williams (17) celebrate after scored the winning goal in the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

***

1994. Akim Oda, eastern Ghana.

Maria Comfort Arthur and Felix Williams wanted a life their jobs — hairdresser and electrician respectively — could not provide. England, they had learned, was a thriving hub for Ghanaian immigrants – Haringey, Southwark, Croydon.

“Go to Spain instead,” suggested a friend. “It’ll be a lot cheaper.”



Cheaper, it was. What they were not told, however, was the excruciating pain their 5,000-kilometre journey entailed. They would cross most of the Sahara Desert on foot. Temperatures touched 50°C. If sand could melt flesh and char bones, it would.

Nico always knew his father limped. Only later did he learn the injury originated in that desert.

Maria, three months pregnant with her elder son, Inaki, was convinced she would not make it to Spain. Along the path that crossed five nations — Burkina Faso, Niger, Algeria, Morocco, and finally, Spain — she would bury — literally, not metaphorically — many friends. In the hunt for a better life, many sacrificed the one they had.

She did, however, make it to Melilla — the autonomous Spanish city nestled in Morocco. Only to be caught by the civil guards. There would not have been a Spanish fairytale without the lawyer who suggested the Williams destroy every document that could trace them back to Ghana, and claim they had fled the Liberian civil war. Only this way would they be eligible to seek asylum.

The Goal that depicts Spain winning the FIFA World Cup! 🏆 pic.twitter.com/haCKMQYzOL — SANTINO (@TheRealSantino) July 20, 2026

Felix found work in a chicken slaughterhouse. Maria took whatever jobs she could — pizzeria, supermarket, airport. Inaki would become Athletic Bilbao’s first Black star, and Nico one of the brightest talents the nation has ever produced.



The talent was displayed at the Euros. A goal in the final against England. This World Cup had been crueller — predominantly owing to injuries. Sports hernia at the start of the season, hamstring issues towards the end, and then a contact injury in the World Cup game against Uruguay.

“Today is one of the worst days of my life,” he had said after the game, disconsolate. Sunday was one of his best.

***

105:33. New Jersey.

The angle was acute when Williams met Pedro Porro’s cross, but the rare opportunity of being a national hero at 24 beckoned. Seductive as it was, he — perhaps to the surprise of Argentine goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez — laid off his header in the direction from where the ball had come.



Growing up, Williams had been raised on one maxim. It was his mother Maria’s favourite saying, the one Iñaki has tattooed on his arm.

“If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together.”

Heroes are usually remembered for choosing themselves.

Williams chose the better option. Ferran Torres.

Spain’s Ferran Torres, left, celebrates next to Nico Williams after scoring the opening goal during the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis) Spain’s Ferran Torres, left, celebrates next to Nico Williams after scoring the opening goal during the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

***

2024. Barcelona, northeastern Spain.

A rare season without a trophy. A 4-1 El Clasico defeat in the Supercopa de España. Same scoreline against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.



When seasons unravel at Barcelona, blame rarely remains unclaimed. Ferran Torres became its custodian.

Signed for €65 million when the club could scarcely afford such extravagance, he had scored only 25 goals in his first 113 appearances. 0.22 per game.

The vitriol was relentless. Social media became a conveyor belt of ridicule. Torres muted much of it, but not enough. He did not want to play football anymore. The joy had left him, and all that was left was an existential burden.

“I fell into a bottomless pit; I didn’t know how to get out. I was at a place where I had lost all confidence in my abilities. When you’re in that place, you have no desire to do anything. I even lost the joy of playing football.”

Torres sought therapy.



Wait, a psychologist? Is football — the male variant, at least — not supposed to be all about machismo, masculinity, bravado? Why could Ferran not smash into someone to feel better, as Roy Keane would have it?

He never cared enough about stigma. Equally unashamedly, he declared himself a Swiftie, once naming Taylor Swift’s Blank Space among his favourite songs.

‘Oh my God, look at that face // You look like my next mistake.’

One could imagine Keane, if he were to discover these lyrics, twitching his eyebrows.

The sessions helped. In the next two seasons, he would score 40 goals in 94 matches. 0.43 per game.



“This (seeking a psychologist) should not be a taboo subject. I don’t go to a psychologist because I am sick. I go to get a perspective outside of my family and inner circle, and to vent. Sometimes, letting your feelings out sets you free.”

***

105:36. New Jersey.

Torres’ shot nestled into the roof of the net. Spain has the second star on the jersey — courtesy of their two stars.

One — a self-proclaimed ‘citizen of the world’ — broke the shackles of geographical borders. The other broke the shackles inside his mind.

Two escapists. Escaping into euphoria.

World.title: Mumbai court sentences 44 Somali pirates to life imprisonment in 2024 hijacking cases
World.content:
A special court in Mumbai on Monday sentenced 44 Somali pirates, arrested in 2024 in two separate cases, to life imprisonment. In their pleas before the court earlier, they had spoken about the hardships they had been facing due to difference in language, diet, culture and lifestyle, hoping for leniency from the court and the government.



Special judge Sanjay Dige said that the Somali pirates were found guilty under various sections, including the Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and attempted murder, kidnapping under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

Nine of the 44 Somali pirates were arrested after the Indian Navy in March 2024 intercepted an Iranian fishing vessel hijacked by the pirates. The vessel was also carrying some Pakistanis. The same month, the Navy apprehended 35 pirates for allegedly hijacking a merchant vessel.

World.title: When Sonam Wangchuk stood up for Pune’s environmental causes
World.content:
In 2024, when Sonam Wangchuk went on a 21-day fast in the sub-freezing temperatures of Leh to demand constitutional and environmental safeguards for Ladakh, a movement was born in Pune. The Friends of Ladakh (FoL), a citizen-led collective, supported Wangchuk by fasting for a day. Santosh Lalwani, an engineer and environmentalist, decided to take the protest further. He continued to fast as long as Wangchuk did. For 10 more days, Lalwani lived on water. Lalwani works with the environment of Pune, and Wangchuk’s battle resonated with him.

On Monday, as thousands of protesters challenged Delhi’s seats of power, Lalwani was among them. “There is a huge gathering here, thousands and thousands and thousands. There are students, middle-aged people, old people. The sentiments are strong. The common citizen, which has been suppressed by the government in terms of education and the environment, wants to be heard. They want the government to listen, and they can’t be ignored,” said Lalwani.

“When an educationist, innovator and environmentalist is saying something, we should support him. He is talking about the future of the children of India,” he added.

World.title: ‘Hit on every inch of my body’: Protester from viral ‘maaro sir’ video
World.content:
Amid a lathicharge against protesters in New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Monday afternoon, a video went viral showing one man surrounded by several security personnel, who were hitting him with lathis while he repeatedly shouted out, “Maaro (hit me), sir.”

The incident took place amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest march towards Parliament, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over paper leaks.



As the situation spiralled out of control, police launched a lathi charge at the Jantar Mantar protest site, chasing away protesters and dismantling the tents they had set up when the protest began.

Amid the many videos emerging from the site was that of the lone protester surrounded by the security personnel. After he endured a few hits, a policewoman holding a Tricolour intervened and attempted to take him away.

World.title: New series propels June core sector growth to 5%, iron ore debuts with 43.9% rise
World.content:
The commerce ministry’s revised Index of Core Industries (ICI) surged to a five-month high of 5% in June. The inclusion of iron ore as the ninth sector was instrumental as its output was 43.9% higher compared to June 2025, according to data released Monday, with a low base effect responsible for this outsized rate of growth.

The new core sector data series – which has 2022-23 as the base year as against 2011-12 in the old one – continues the government’s overhaul of India’s official statistics. So far in 2026, the statistics and commerce ministries have already released updated data series for GDP, Consumer Price Index, Index of Industrial Production, Wholesale Price Index as well as the inaugural Output Producer Price Index and trial numbers for input PPI and an Index of Services Production.

The new data series downgrades core sector growth in 2024-25 sharply to 4.3% from 6.9%. However, it has upgraded the figure for 2025-26 to 3% from 1.1%.

Core Sector Data Chart Core Sector Data Chart

While iron ore only makes up 4.9% of the new Index of Core Industries, the 43.9% jump in its production in June was key to the entire core sector output rising the most in five months. The growth for May has been revised higher to 3.2% in the new series from a 1% under the old series.

Iron ore, whose output is estimated to have risen by 19% in May, has been added to the index due to its extensive industry use and significant contribution to industrial development.



The other eight sectors part of the ICI are coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, and electricity.

Some of the other key changes in the revised core sector data include the use of gross production data for compiling the steel index, the coal index including only ‘raw coal’ and not coal middlings and washed coal to eliminate double counting, among others.

Apart from iron ore, core sector growth in June was driven by a 9.8% rise in electricity generation, with the high temperatures and rainfall deficit boosting demand for power. The same sub-par monsoon helped raise coal output by 1.4% after three consecutive months of decline.

Mining activity is disrupted by rains.

Steel output rose 4.6%, while cement production was up 9.8%.



Meanwhile, petroleum-related sectors all reported a fall in production in June compared to last year, which Madan Sabnavis, Chief Economist at Bank of Baroda, said can be attributed to higher imports on account of global crude prices declining.

Also Read | Reliance on coal soars as weak rains drag hydro output by 19.5%

“Export of refinery products had slowed down this month. In case of fertilisers imports tended to increase,” Sabnavis said.

Crude oil fell for the 18th month in a row in June and was down 4.2% year-on-year.

Natural gas output (down 7.4%) contracted for the 24th consecutive month.

Refinery products (down 4.7%) saw their production shrink for the third month in a row.

Prodcution of fertilisers (down 3.3%) was lower for the fourth straight month.
